title: A conformal spatial operator with the simplex spectrum
summary: The critical conformal scalar operator on a round even-dimensional sphere has exactly the normalized simplex spectrum, while its spinor realization, spatial geometry and master interaction remain additional requirements.
text:
Summary: The critical conformal scalar operator on a round even-dimensional sphere has exactly the normalized simplex spectrum, while its spinor realization, spatial geometry and master interaction remain additional requirements. An exact geometric occurrence of the mass-count polynomial There is a known natural differential operator whose normalized eigenvalues are exactly S(n,d)= inom{n+d-1}{d}. 	ag{1} For even d, it is the critical conformal scalar operator on a round d-sphere. The result follows from spatial conformal covariance and can also be verified by direct differentiation. It gives a distinct mathematical origin for the same sequence used in the mass-spectrum construction. This calculation specifies a round physical spatial geometry S_R^d, with undetermined radius R. It is a conditional comparison, not a replacement of the CP3 candidate or a determination of physical topology. Its directions are ordinary macroscopic spatial directions; there is no compactification or hidden small radius. Spherical harmonic coefficients do not add dimensions. The operator acts on scalar spatial functions. Its appearance in the master spinor interaction, and the identification of its harmonic degree with an occupied particle mode, must be derived separately. Conformal covariance fixes the recurrence Work first at unit radius. Let P commute with round-sphere rotations, and let its scalar eigenvalue on the complete degree-\ell harmonic space be p_\ell. Rotation covariance alone leaves those eigenvalues free. Impose the stronger critical conformal law P(C^*f)=\Omega^d C^*(Pf),\qquad C^*g=\Omega^2g. 	ag{2} This is the scalar law with input conformal weight zero and output weight -d. Its infinitesimal form, for \mathcal L_Vg=2\omega g, is [P,V]f=d\omega Pf. 	ag{3} Choose the height coordinate t=X_{d+1} on the unit sphere and V=
abla t. Since 
abla^2t=-tg, its conformal factor is \omega=-t. For \ell\ge1, the complex harmonic H_\ell=(X_1+iX_2)^\ell satisfies VH_\ell=-\ell\,tH_\ell. 	ag{4} The ambient polynomial tH_\ell is itself harmonic and homogeneous of degree \ell+1, because H_\ell is independent of t. Applying (3) to (4) gives -\ell(p_{\ell+1}-p_\ell)tH_\ell =-d\,p_\ell tH_\ell. Thus  oxed{ rac{p_{\ell+1}}{p_\ell}= rac{\ell+d}{\ell}} \qquad(\ell\ge1,\ p_1
e0). 	ag{5} Applying (3) to the constant function also gives p_0=0. Iteration yields  oxed{  rac{p_\ell}{p_1} =\prod_{j=1}^{\ell-1} rac{j+d}{j} = inom{\ell+d-1}{d}. } 	ag{6} The last expression is exactly the cumulative Hockey-Stick count in (1). Here it is an eigenvalue ratio forced by the specified conformal law, rather than a count being substituted for an eigenvalue. The chosen complex harmonic is a convenient way to derive the recurrence; rotation covariance gives the same value on every polarization of its harmonic space. A local differential operator realizes that law Let \Delta=-
abla^a
abla_a be the nonnegative scalar Laplacian, and write d=2h. The critical GJMS operator has order d; critical means that its differential order equals the spatial dimension. On the round sphere it is  oxed{ P_{d,R}= \prod_{j=1}^{h} \left[\Delta+ rac{(h-j)(h+j-1)}{R^2}ight]. } 	ag{7} The factors and the conformal transformation law are the standard Branson factorization, derived explicitly through stereographic projection in Graham, Proposition 1. The leading term in (7) is \Delta^{d/2}. On a degree-\ell scalar harmonic, R^2\Delta=\ell(\ell+d-1). Each factor becomes \ell(\ell+d-1)+(h-j)(h+j-1) =(\ell+h-j)(\ell+h+j-1). 	ag{8} The first factors cover \ell,\ldots,\ell+h-1 and the second cover \ell+h,\ldots,\ell+d-1. Therefore  oxed{ P_{d,R}Y_{\ell,a} = rac{\ell(\ell+1)\cdots(\ell+d-1)}{R^d}Y_{\ell,a} = rac{d!}{R^d}S(\ell,d)Y_{\ell,a}. } 	ag{9} The label a runs over the complete scalar harmonic multiplet. Its multiplicity is  inom{\ell+d}{d}- inom{\ell+d-2}{d}, with the second term zero when \ell<2. That multiplicity is separate from the eigenvalue (9). The constant harmonic has eigenvalue zero. For the two charged-lepton depths, the operators are particularly explicit:  egin{aligned} P_{6,R} &=\Delta\left(\Delta+ rac4{R^2}ight) \left(\Delta+ rac6{R^2}ight),\ P_{10,R} &=\Delta\left(\Delta+ rac8{R^2}ight) \left(\Delta+ rac{14}{R^2}ight) \left(\Delta+ rac{18}{R^2}ight) \left(\Delta+ rac{20}{R^2}ight). \end{aligned} 	ag{10} Define the dimensionless operator \widehat P_d=R^dP_{d,R}/d!, which normalizes the first positive harmonic eigenvalue to one. At the stated integer indices: Spatial dimension d Scalar harmonic degree \ell Eigenvalue of \widehat P_d 6 13 18\,564 6 35 3\,838\,380 10 23 64\,512\,240 The degrees in the table have not been selected by (2) or (7). Identifying \ell=n with a particle's occupied mode is an additional physical step. The harmonic degree \ell is also different from the oscillator cutoff N=n-1. No change of particle dimensionalities or unrestricted mode search is being used. At the level of scalar spatial operators, a trial family M_d=\mu_d\widehat P_d has precisely the proposed eigenvalue sequence. It is one differential operator for all harmonic degrees, with a common scale in each dimension. Its cumulative harmonic compressions obey the ordinary consistency law. This is not the auxiliary rank-one contact family. Normalizing by d! is an explicit spectral convention. It does not derive the dimensional coefficient \mu_d, nor the charged-lepton relation \mu_{10}=\mu_6. A master reduction must fix those physical normalizations across sectors. Verify it by differentiating spatial functions In stereographic coordinates, put s=|x|^2 and \Omega=2/(1+s). At unit radius, the critical conformal law gives P_d f=\Omega^{-d}(-\Delta_{\mathbb R^d})^{d/2}f. 	ag{11} For a zonal harmonic, f(s)=C_\ell^{(d-1)/2}\left( rac{1-s}{1+s}ight),\qquad \Delta_{\mathbb R^d}f=4s f''+2d f', 	ag{12} where C_\ell^\alpha is a Gegenbauer polynomial. Exact rational differentiation of (11)–(12) gives (9), including the assigned degrees. A second family retains a complex angular phase. With the homogeneous Euclidean harmonic H_\ell=(x_1+ix_2)^\ell, f(x)=2^\ell H_\ell(x)(1+s)^{-\ell},\qquad \Delta_{\mathbb R^d}(H_\ell h(s)) =H_\ell\left[4s h''+(2d+4\ell)h'ight]. 	ag{13} It gives the same eigenvalue independently of the zonal calculation. Thus the spectral identity is supported by both the conformal recurrence and the actual spatial differential action. The existing CP3 geometry gives a different spectrum The factorization extends to an Einstein metric \operatorname{Ric}=(d-1)K g by replacing R^{-2} in (7) with K. This is Gover, Theorem 1.2. Its eigenvalues still depend on the Laplacian spectrum of the actual geometry. For CP3 with the existing FS convention of holomorphic sectional curvature 4/R^2, one has \operatorname{Ric}=8g/R^2 and scalar eigenvalues 4\ell(\ell+3)/R^2. Thus the same critical conformal construction gives  oxed{ P_6^{\mathrm{CP}^3} =\Delta\left(\Delta+ rac{32}{5R^2}ight) \left(\Delta+ rac{48}{5R^2}ight). } 	ag{14} Putting x=\ell(\ell+3), its dimensionless eigenvalue is 4x(4x+32/5)(4x+48/5). At \ell=13,35, its ratio is  rac{7\,374\,117\,835}{28\,664\,896} =257.252558495\ldots, 	ag{15} whereas the round-sphere simplex ratio is 3515/17=206.764705882\ldots. A common scale cannot change either ratio. This compares one specified scalar operator on two six-dimensional geometries at the same harmonic degrees. It does not compare alternative particle dimensionalities, and it does not test the separate auxiliary contact prescription on CP3. Scalar covariance is not automatically spinor covariance The standard untwisted spinor Dirac spectrum on a round sphere is \pm(k+d/2)/R, with k=0,1,\ldots, as discussed in round-sphere Dirac counts. Its conformal differential powers have a different factorization: at unit radius they include \mathscr D\prod_{j=1}^{m}(\mathscr D^2-j^2). 	ag{16} The spinorial intertwining family has multipliers proportional to  rac{\Gamma(d/2+k+1/2-\lambda)} {\Gamma(d/2+k+1/2+\lambda)}. 	ag{17} For even dimension the intertwiner maps between the appropriate chiral bundles; it is not the scalar operator acting on independent component functions. These conventions and (16) are given in Clerc and Ørsted, Proposition 7.1 and Theorem 7.1. At the parameter \lambda=-d/2, the magnitude of (17) becomes \left(k+ rac12ight) \left(k+ rac32ight)\cdots \left(k+d- rac12ight). 	ag{18} Its consecutive ratio is (k+d+1/2)/(k+1/2), rather than (5) with integer \ell. An overall normalization does not remove this spectral shift. Consequently the successful scalar construction cannot simply be declared to be the standard untwisted spinor mass operator. A different physical twist or composite scalar source requires its own derivation. An exact transfer through a complete Killing-spinor frame does produce a local spinor operator with the scalar spectrum. Its opposite Dirac signs carry adjacent scalar degrees, and its real scalar mass insertion changes the coefficient. This is a distinct operator construction, with its action and physical scope checked separately. Acting on the scalar current changes the nonlinear equation Another possible insertion would let P_d act on the real scalar current J=\psi^\dagger eta\psi. On a closed spatial manifold, consider the explicitly different interaction \mathcal E_P(\psi)= rac{\eta}{2}\int J P_d J\,d\mu. 	ag{19} Self-adjointness gives \delta\mathcal E_P=\eta\int(P_dJ)\,\delta J\,d\mu,\qquad  rac{\delta\mathcal E_P}{\delta\psi^\dagger} =\eta(P_dJ) eta\psi. 	ag{20} The variation is multiplication by P_dJ; it is not P_d\psi. Moreover, P_d1=0,\qquad \int P_dJ\,d\mu=0. 	ag{21} Thus this term annihilates a constant current, including the constant-density local branch. If P_dJ is required to be constant everywhere, (21) forces that constant to vanish. A nonconstant current instead supplies a spatially varying nonlinear coefficient whose complete field equation must be solved. Equation (19) contains derivatives of the current. It is an additional interaction, beyond the written algebraic scalar term tested by the local derivative calculation. Any claim that it arises by eliminating modes must identify those modes of the same master field and retain the induced kinetic normalization. The complete response on a zero-current Killing background provides one exact spatial test of this proposed interaction. Its simplex coefficient enters collective frequencies; any nonzero derivative-current coefficient gives unstable high harmonics on that specified branch. The exact result is therefore a geometric origin for the simplex scalar spectrum, with conformal covariance fixing the integer recurrence. The physical mass-operator problem still requires the actual spatial geometry, a scalar or spinor realization inherited from the master field, a selected harmonic mode, and a justified connection between the resulting frequency or energy and rest mass. Verification conformal_simplex_spectrum_checks.py checks the exact factorizations, the complete conformal commutator on zonal harmonics, the normalized simplex sequence, and independent stereographic differentiation of both zonal and complex angular fields. Exact rational arithmetic covers the assigned degrees without using a fitted spectral polynomial. Separate checks retain the CP3 curvature coefficients, the standard spinorial spectral shift, and the full complex variation of (19). Those operator identities do not select a physical geometry or prove that the master action contains this conformal interaction.

title: Exact local scalar fields with constant spatial density
summary: Five holomorphic polarization fields give an exact constant-density branch of the local scalar Dirac action on the curved mode bundle, while its common coefficient and copy symmetries leave the mass count unselected.
text:
Summary: Five holomorphic polarization fields give an exact constant-density branch of the local scalar Dirac action on the curved mode bundle, while its common coefficient and copy symmetries leave the mass count unselected. Solve the written local interaction The coherent curved-bundle construction gave exact spatial fields for a specified smooth moment interaction. The written local scalar interaction can also be solved exactly on the same kinetic bundle, using a different polarization pattern. Retain the candidate physical CP3 geometry and its undetermined metric radius R. Its six directions are ordinary macroscopic spatial directions. No dimensions are compactified. Set T=T^{1,0}\mathrm{CP}^3,\qquad W=\mathbf1\oplus T\oplus T^*,\qquad E_N=\operatorname{Sym}^N W, 	ag{1} with the natural Hermitian metric and connection. Use the specified canonical Spin^c operator \mathscr D_N=\sqrt2( ar\partial_{E_N}+ ar\partial_{E_N}^{\dagger}), \qquad  eta=(-1)^{	ext{form degree}}, 	ag{2} on all exterior-form components, with degree-zero line twist. The interaction is the local scalar action itself: \mathcal E(\psi)=\langle\psi,\mathscr D_N\psiangle + rac{\kappa}{2}\int(\psi^\dagger eta\psi)^2d
u. 	ag{3} Initially d
u has total spatial volume one. There is no additional spatial response kernel in (3). The bundle and kinetic operator remain specified candidate data; their master-field projection and holonomic interpretation have not been derived. The construction below supplies a nontrivial holomorphic zero-form \chi_N with \|\chi_N(q)\|^2=1 everywhere. Then \mathscr D_N\chi_N=0, its scalar current is constant, and the complete local equation has an exact stationary solution. Five fields whose tangent norms add to a constant Let \sigma_x,\sigma_y,\sigma_z be the Pauli matrices, and define five Hermitian 4 by 4 matrices  egin{aligned} \Gamma_1&=\sigma_x\otimes I_2,& \Gamma_2&=\sigma_y\otimes I_2,\ \Gamma_3&=\sigma_z\otimes\sigma_x,& \Gamma_4&=\sigma_z\otimes\sigma_y,& \Gamma_5&=\sigma_z\otimes\sigma_z. \end{aligned} 	ag{4} They obey \Gamma_a\Gamma_b+\Gamma_b\Gamma_a=2\delta_{ab}I_4. They generate five particular holomorphic projective vector fields on the same physical CP3. Their number does not count spatial dimensions. For a unit homogeneous vector Z=(a,b,c,d), put r_j=Z^\dagger\Gamma_jZ. Direct multiplication gives  egin{aligned} r_1+ir_2&=2( ar a c+ ar b d),\ r_3+ir_4&=2( ar a b- ar c d),\ r_5&=|a|^2+|d|^2-|b|^2-|c|^2. \end{aligned} 	ag{5} Let A=|a|^2+|d|^2 and B=|b|^2+|c|^2. The cross terms cancel in | ar a c+ ar b d|^2+| ar a b- ar c d|^2=AB. Hence  oxed{\sum_{j=1}^5r_j^2=4AB+(A-B)^2=(A+B)^2=1.} 	ag{6} This is the quadratic identity associated with the quaternionic Hopf construction; Baez, Section 3.1 describes its projective setting. Here it is used only as the explicit polynomial identity (5)–(6). It introduces no additional physical space. For any complex matrix A, write X_A for its holomorphic projective vector field. With the common unit-radius tangent normalization, \|X_A(Z)\|^2=Z^\dagger A^\dagger AZ-|Z^\dagger AZ|^2. 	ag{7} In the chart Z_0
e0, it has the holomorphic components X_A^j(z)=(A(1,z))_j-z_j(A(1,z))_0,\qquad j=1,2,3. 	ag{8} Equations (4), (6) and (7) now prove  oxed{\sum_{j=1}^5\|X_{\Gamma_j}(q)\|^2=5-\sum_{j=1}^5r_j(q)^2=4} 	ag{9} at every physical point. The five separate densities vary with position. Their sum is constant. Put the five fields into orthogonal copies already in the carrier The complete tangent-band decomposition shows that E_N contains \lfloor(N-1)/2floor+1 orthogonal parallel copies of T. In particular, it has at least five when N\ge9. An explicit normalized inclusion removes any ambiguity about the metric of these copies. Temporarily let m=\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb C}T; here m=3. In an orthonormal tangent frame, use normalized symmetric occupation notation |s;\alpha;\gammaangle for slack, tangent and cotangent degrees. These are polynomial coefficient labels, not extra particles or spatial coordinates. For \ell\ge0 and 2\ell+1\le N, define  oxed{ \mathcal I_{\ell,N}(v)= \sum_{\substack{n_1+\cdots+n_m=\ell\i=1,\ldots,m}} \sqrt{ rac{n_i+1}{ inom{\ell+m}{m}}}\, v_i\,|N-2\ell-1;\,n+e_i;\,nangle. } 	ag{10} Every term has homogeneous degree N. The identity \sum_{|n|=\ell}(n_i+1)= inom{\ell+m}{m} 	ag{11} gives \langle\mathcal I_{\ell,N}(v),\mathcal I_{\ell,N}(w)angle =v^\dagger w. One proof of (11) takes the coefficient of t^\ell in (1-t)^{-2}(1-t)^{-(m-1)}. Thus the trace insertion has a definite Hockey-Stick normalization, which makes it an isometry. There is also a basis-independent description. Contract one tangent and one cotangent factor with the parallel identity tensor, insert \ell such pairs, and add the remaining slack factors. In formal normalized creation notation, this is \mathcal I_{\ell,N}(v)=  rac{(a_0^\dagger)^{N-2\ell-1} (\sum_i a_i^\dagger b_i^\dagger)^\ell a_v^\dagger|0angle} {\sqrt{(N-2\ell-1)!\,\ell!\,(m+1)_\ell}}, 	ag{12} where (m+1)_\ell=(m+1)\cdots(m+\ell) and the empty product is one. Expanding (12) gives (10). The maps are parallel and holomorphic because the contraction and slack line are parallel. Their images for different \ell are orthogonal: they have different total tangent and cotangent degrees. An exact noncoherent branch of the full local equation For every N\ge9, set  oxed{ \chi_N(q)= rac12\sum_{\ell=0}^4 \mathcal I_{\ell,N} igl(X_{\Gamma_{\ell+1}}(q) igr). } 	ag{13} The five terms are orthogonal at every point. Therefore (9)–(10) give \|\chi_N(q)\|^2=1,\qquad  ar\partial_{E_N}\chi_N=0,\qquad \mathscr D_N\chi_N=0,\qquad  eta\chi_N=\chi_N. 	ag{14} All components of the spatial polarization pattern have been included. The field is not parallel: its separate copy densities vary, even though their sum is constant. For N>9, the field is also noncoherent in the homogeneous carrier. Every occupied term has a positive slack degree, but the pure-slack coefficient is zero. A coherent vector (s,u,v)^{\odot N} with s
e0 has nonzero pure-slack coefficient s^N; with s=0 it has no slack occupations. Neither case equals the nonzero field (13). This proves the distinction at both assigned indices N=12 and 34. The full equation from (3) is i\partial_t\psi =\mathscr D_N\psi+\kappa(\psi^\dagger eta\psi) eta\psi. 	ag{15} Substitution of (14) proves  oxed{\psi(t,q)=e^{-i\kappa t}\chi_N(q),\qquad \omega=\kappa,\qquad \mathcal E(\chi_N)=\kappa/2.} 	ag{16} Restoring physical volume \mathcal V and canonical field norm Q gives  oxed{ \psi(t,q)=\sqrt{ rac Q{\mathcal V}}\, e^{-i\omega t}\chi_N(q),\qquad \omega= rac{\kappa Q}{\mathcal V},\qquad \mathcal E= rac{\kappa Q^2}{2\mathcal V}. } 	ag{17} The common physical tangent normalization is restored with the same metric scale for every N. Holomorphicity and constant density survive that common rescaling. The nonlinear scalar endomorphism on this background is \kappa Q\, eta/\mathcal V. It is a self-consistent constant scalar coefficient of the specified field equation. Its identification with an observed rest mass, rather than merely this equation's carrier frequency, requires further physical justification. Cumulative degree N Carrier rank  inom{N+6}{6} Frequency of (17) 12 18\,564 \kappa Q/\mathcal V 34 3\,838\,380 \kappa Q/\mathcal V The same normalized spatial field is carried from E_{12} to E_{34} by the natural cumulative inclusion, which adds slack occupation while preserving each existing degree block. This exact solution therefore does not turn the larger carrier rank into a larger scalar coefficient. The sufficient construction threshold N\ge9 is not a particle mode-selection rule or a claim that it is the smallest possible threshold. Why a nontrivial coherent field cannot use this constant source There is a precise result for the same degree-zero line twist. Suppose s is a nonzero holomorphic section of E_N, with N\ge1, which is pointwise coherent and has a constant positive norm. Locally, s has a holomorphic root w satisfying s=w^{\odot N}. This follows by choosing a nonzero component of the coherent generating line, taking a local Nth root of its pure coefficient, and recovering the other components from the mixed coefficients. On overlapping charts, two such roots differ by a constant Nth root of unity. CP3 is simply connected: the homotopy sequence of S^1	o S^7	o\mathrm{CP}^3 gives \pi_1(\mathrm{CP}^3)=0. The finite root covering therefore has a global branch. Thus w is a global holomorphic section of W, with constant norm. The holomorphic sections of W have the form w=(c,X_A,0). 	ag{18} Here c is constant, H^0(T^*)=0, and all holomorphic tangent fields are projective matrix fields. These facts follow from the Euler sequence or the degree-one cases of the tangent-band calculation. Every complex matrix A has an eigenvector. At its projective eigenline, X_A vanishes. Since \|w\|^2=|c|^2+\|X_A\|^2 is constant, that zero forces X_A to vanish everywhere. Consequently,  oxed{ 	ext{A constant-norm coherent holomorphic section of }E_N 	ext{ is a pure-slack section.} } 	ag{19} The statement is restricted to this bundle and its degree-zero line twist. It does not classify nonlinear fields with complementary Dirac components or nonzero twists. The real-source preservation criterion shows why (19) matters: an exact local scalar branch that remains on a holomorphic zero line requires constant density. The nontrivial solution (13) meets that condition through its full multiplet. The local action leaves copy norms and pattern choices free Each parallel projector onto an isomorphic T copy commutes with \mathscr D_N and  eta. Writing \psi_a for the full spinor in copy a, the local equation gives  rac d{dt}\langle\psi_a,\psi_bangle=0. 	ag{20} Indeed, both copies evolve with the same instantaneous self-adjoint operator \mathscr D_T+\kappa J(q,t) eta. Its contributions to the derivative of the inner product cancel. This includes a spatially varying self-consistent current and both form parities. The action has a common unitary symmetry mixing the five equivalent copies. Such mixing preserves the total pointwise density, holomorphicity and the frequency in (16). For the particular field (13), every copy has norm 1/5: unit projective measure gives \int r_j^2d
u=\operatorname{Tr}(\Gamma_j^2)/(4\cdot5)=1/5, so \int\|X_{\Gamma_j}\|^2d
u=4/5. These equal copy weights describe the constructed solution; the action does not dynamically enforce them on arbitrary initial fields. This is a symmetry of the specified kinetic and local scalar action. It is not an identification with an observed gauge symmetry. A master projection could impose additional constraints or terms that change it. The physical derivative calculation is one reason to distinguish independent coefficient sections from derivatives of the master field. Full spatial stability remains a separate calculation Constant background density does not freeze the density of a perturbation. At unit norm and volume, put \psi=e^{-i\kappa t}(\chi_N+\eta). Retaining the complete variation of (15) gives i\partial_t\eta =\mathscr D_N\eta+\kappa( eta-I)\eta +2\kappa\chi_N\operatorname{Re}(\chi_N^\dagger\eta). 	ag{21} The last term responds to every local density perturbation, and \chi_N has a nonconstant spatial polarization. Replacing (21) by a frozen linear massive Dirac operator would omit that response. No complete spectral or nonlinear stability theorem is established here. The earlier line-bundle stability result uses a different spatial source closure and does not transfer automatically. The graph contact action would multiply the scalar coefficient by D_N if adopted separately. The construction above solves the written local scalar action before that extra premise. It establishes a possible exact spatial source, while leaving the master interaction, the count enhancement, state selection and observed mass identification unresolved. Verification constant_density_bundle_checks.py proves (6) by symbolic expansion in all eight real homogeneous coefficients. Direct occupation sums and independent repeated pair creation verify (10)–(12), including their complete complex connection intertwining. Spatial chart changes, physical tangent norms and full Dolbeault derivatives check (13)–(14) at N=9,12,34. The diagnostic also checks the scalar stationary equation with different common norms and volumes, both signs of the scalar coefficient, and the distinction between energy and frequency. The copy-charge cancellation is independently checked with full complex fields and both spin parities; that finite identity test is not a spatial stability calculation. Matrix eigenlines verify the elementary zero used in (19). The global root-covering argument itself is a mathematical proof, not a numerical test.

title: Local scalar contact on physical field derivatives
summary: Prolonging the written local scalar interaction to physical field derivatives repeats its local source blocks without generating a simplex coupling, and finite derivative data do not close the spatial kinetic equation.
text:
Summary: Prolonging the written local scalar interaction to physical field derivatives repeats its local source blocks without generating a simplex coupling, and finite derivative data do not close the spatial kinetic equation. Test the local interaction before changing its action The mass-operator construction identifies the filtered derivative symbols of the physical field with a cumulative symmetric carrier. That identification gives the correct Hockey-Stick rank. It does not yet determine how the written interaction acts on those derivatives. This calculation applies the actual product rule to the local scalar term. It uses the same smooth physical spinor field throughout. Its coordinate directions are ordinary spatial directions on Q_d; Taylor coefficients introduce no additional physical dimensions and require no compactification. The result is local and does not choose a global spatial topology. In a local orthonormal spin frame, write \mathcal E_{m sc} = rac{\kappa}{2}\int(\psi^\dagger eta\psi)^2d\mu,\qquad \mathcal N(\psi)=\kappa(\psi^\dagger eta\psi) eta\psi, \qquad  eta^\dagger= eta,\quad eta^2=I. 	ag{1} The metric,  eta and \kappa are fixed background data in the variation. The full equation also contains its spatial Dirac operator. No occupied profile or physical mass follows from the algebraic source alone. Derivative counting and its exact product rule Choose local real coordinates centred at q. For a multiindex \alpha=(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_d), put |\alpha|=\sum_j\alpha_j and \alpha!=\prod_j\alpha_j!. The divided Taylor coefficients through order N are c_\alpha= rac{\partial^\alpha\psi(q)}{\alpha!}, \qquad j_N\psi=(c_\alpha)_{|\alpha|\le N}. 	ag{2} The name jet means this finite collection of derivatives. A field of such coefficients is holonomic when the coefficients actually are the derivatives of one field. At one point, arbitrary finite coefficients can be realized by a polynomial; across space they obey derivative compatibility conditions. The coordinate-independent jet definition and its Taylor description are given in Kolář, Michor and Slovák, Sections 12.1–12.5. Per spinor component, the rank is exactly D_{N,d}=\sum_{k=0}^N inom{k+d-1}{d-1}= inom{N+d}{d}. 	ag{3} For a fixed smooth real scalar current J, denote its divided derivatives by J_\gamma. The Leibniz rule gives [j_N(J\psi)]_\alpha =\sum_{\gamma+\delta=\alpha}J_\gamma c_\delta. 	ag{4} Thus multiplication induces a truncated convolution matrix [M_N[J]]_{\alpha\delta}=  egin{cases} J_{\alpha-\delta},&\delta_j\le\alpha_j\ 	ext{for every }j,\ 0,&	ext{otherwise}. \end{cases} 	ag{5} Order the indices by total degree. Every diagonal entry is J_0=J(q); every other nonzero entry raises degree. Consequently M_N[J]=J_0I+K,\qquad K^{N+1}=0, 	ag{6} and  oxed{ \det(\lambda I-M_N[J])=(\lambda-J_0)^{D_{N,d}}, \qquad \operatorname{tr}(M_N[J]^r)=D_{N,d}J_0^r. } 	ag{7} The integer in (3) appears as a multiplicity and in a trace. The sole scalar eigenvalue remains J_0. When J_0
e0, the jet multiplier has full rank. Equation (7) is a statement about this particular local operator; it does not bound a separately derived spatial effective action. Changing to coherent coordinates preserves this distinction Using unscaled derivatives instead of (2) conjugates (5) by the diagonal matrix with entries \alpha!. The usual degree-N homogeneous coherent normalization is another invertible diagonal transformation, S_\alpha=\sqrt{ rac{N!\,\alpha!}{(N-|\alpha|)!}}, \qquad \widetilde c_\alpha=S_\alpha c_\alpha,\qquad \widetilde M=SM_N[J]S^{-1}. 	ag{8} It leaves (7) unchanged. It is a change of coefficient coordinates, not a derivation of their kinetic metric. There is a useful exact complex example. With fixed spinor u, amplitude a and real spatial wavevector k, let \psi(x)=aue^{ik\cdot x},\qquad c_\alpha=au rac{(ik)^\alpha}{\alpha!}. 	ag{9} At the coordinate origin, (8) turns the scalar coefficient sequence into the homogeneous coherent occupation sequence generated by (1,ik). Its squared coefficient norm is proportional to (1+|k|^2)^N, rather than being an independent physical norm of the original field. Retaining the conjugate phase gives J(x)=|a|^2u^\dagger eta u,\qquad J_\gamma=0\quad(|\gamma|>0), 	ag{10} because the derivative sum in every coordinate contains \sum_{\ell=0}^r(-1)^\ell inom r\ell=\delta_{r0}. 	ag{11} Therefore the complete source satisfies  oxed{j_N\mathcal N(\psi)=\kappa J_0\, eta\,j_N\psi} 	ag{12} at every retained order, before and after (8). This local plane wave is an operator example, not a proposed localized particle. At the assigned six-dimensional cumulative indices: Degree N Coefficient slots per spinor component Scalar coefficient in (12) 12 18\,564 \kappa J_0 34 3\,838\,380 \kappa J_0 This comparison holds the physical background fixed; a separate nonlinear branch could have a different current profile. Include the full variation of the self-consistent current For the nonlinear source in (1), the current is not fixed. Its actual Taylor coefficients and those of its source are J_\alpha=\sum_{\gamma+\delta=\alpha}c_\gamma^\dagger eta c_\delta, \qquad \mathcal N_\alpha =\kappa\sum_{\gamma+\delta=\alpha}J_\gamma eta c_\delta. 	ag{13} All J_\alpha are real; conjugate terms pair under \gamma\leftrightarrow\delta. Define v_\alpha= eta c_\alpha. The complete complex variation has coefficient matrices  egin{aligned} A_
u&=\kappa\left[ J_
u eta+\sum_{\gamma+\delta=
u}v_\gamma v_\delta^\dagger ight],\ B_
u&=\kappa\sum_{\gamma+\delta=
u}v_\gamma v_\delta^{\mathsf T},\ \delta\mathcal N_\alpha &=\sum_{
u+\delta=\alpha} \left(A_
u\eta_\delta+B_
u\overline{\eta_\delta}ight). \end{aligned} 	ag{14} This retains every spin polarization and both complex variation blocks. The B term and the additional term in A are the response of the current itself. Freezing the current would omit them. For any matrices A,B, the real matrix of \eta\mapsto A\eta+B ar\eta, using real and imaginary parts, is \mathcal R(A,B)=  egin{pmatrix} \operatorname{Re}(A+B)&-\operatorname{Im}(A-B)\ \operatorname{Im}(A+B)&\operatorname{Re}(A-B) \end{pmatrix}. 	ag{15} Interleave the real and imaginary parts at each derivative index. Equation (14) is block lower triangular, with the same local block \mathcal R_0=\mathcal R(A_0,B_0) on every diagonal. Hence the full real source Jacobian \mathcal J_N obeys  oxed{ \det(\lambda I-\mathcal J_N) =\det(\lambda I-\mathcal R_0)^{D_{N,d}}. } 	ag{16} Again the count repeats local response eigenvalues. Spatial derivatives appear in the off-diagonal blocks and can change Jordan structure. Neither this algebraic source Jacobian nor (7) is the full time-evolution generator, which also includes multiplication by -i, the spatial Dirac term, and any rotating-frame subtraction. The local eigenvalues can also be written explicitly. Let the complex +1 and -1 eigenspaces of  eta have dimensions r_+ and r_-, both positive, and set Q_0=c_0^\dagger c_0,\qquad S_0=c_0^\dagger eta c_0. In real coordinates the source derivative is \kappa[S_0 eta_{\mathbb R}+2v_{\mathbb R}v_{\mathbb R}^{\mathsf T}]. Its eigenvalues are  egin{array}{c|c} 	ext{Eigenvalue}&	ext{Multiplicity}\ \hline \kappa S_0&2r_+-1\ -\kappa S_0&2r_--1\ \kappa\left(Q_0+\sqrt{Q_0^2+3S_0^2}ight)&1\ \kappa\left(Q_0-\sqrt{Q_0^2+3S_0^2}ight)&1 \end{array}. 	ag{17} To derive the last two values, remove the directions orthogonal to the positive and negative parts of c_0. Their squared norms are (Q_0+S_0)/2 and (Q_0-S_0)/2. On the remaining real two-dimensional span, the trace is 2\kappa Q_0 and the determinant is -3\kappa^2S_0^2. Formula (17) also holds by continuity when one part vanishes. At a scalar-null field, S_0=0, the only nonzero local eigenvalue is 2\kappa Q_0. A sign of  eta or an eigenvalue in (17) is not an assignment of particle versus antiparticle. Curvature and the physical kinetic norm On a curved spatial manifold, a connection splits the finite derivative filtration into symmetrized covariant derivatives. The change from ordinary coordinate derivatives to this splitting is triangular and invertible, with the same highest-order symbols. A connection preserving the spinor pairing obeys the covariant product rule. The associated graded operator of scalar multiplication remains J(q) on every degree, so (7) survives. The full source variation transforms with the same fixed linear change of jet coordinates, preserving (16). Curvature does not turn a coordinate transformation into a new scalar coupling. There is a useful warning about the norm implicit in such a rewriting. If some retained derivative of J is nonzero, K in (6) is a nonzero nilpotent matrix. Then M_N[J] is not diagonalizable and cannot be self-adjoint in any positive definite metric on the independent finite jet fibre. For example, at d=N=1 and J=1+x, M= egin{pmatrix}1&0\1&1\end{pmatrix}. 	ag{18} The equation GM=M^\dagger G forces G_{22}=0, which excludes a positive definite G. Ordinary real multiplication on the physical L^2 field space is nevertheless self-adjoint. There is no contradiction: the Taylor map is not a unitary identification of that space with an independent finite coefficient fibre at one point. The original canonical norm remains Q[\psi]=\int\psi^\dagger\psi\,d\mu. 	ag{19} Expressing its field through holonomic derivatives does not replace (19) with an independent sum over all derivative slots. A positive norm that weights all spatial derivatives defines a different, usually Sobolev, metric; its induced operator and constraints must be transformed as well. The canonical normalization calculation explains why the physical kinetic metric must accompany a projected interaction. There is also a kinetic closure issue. Already for a flat first-order Dirac operator \mathscr D=-i\sum_j\mathsf a_j\partial_j, [j_N(\mathscr D\psi)]_\alpha =-i\sum_j\mathsf a_j(\alpha_j+1)c_{\alpha+e_j}. 	ag{20} The highest retained derivative needs order N+1 of the field. For example, \psi_1=u and \psi_2=u+\epsilon x_1^{N+1}v have identical N-jets at zero, but their degree-N Dirac jets differ by -i\epsilon(N+1)\mathsf a_1v. Thus a finite jet at one point does not define a closed algebraic kinetic matrix. A spatial PDE on jet fields can retain their derivatives and compatibility equations; a finite oscillator reduction instead needs an actual projection and control of its complementary spatial modes. Consequence for the mass-operator derivation The count in (3) is exact. The prolonged local action gives (13) and (14), rather than the auxiliary rank-one contact. Deriving the latter requires an additional physical reduction, such as a specific source pairing and its canonical normalization. The defined graph pairing supplies one conditional action with a simplex coefficient, but its kernel is an additional premise. This also clarifies the scope of the coherent curved mode-bundle fields and their physical contact spectrum. Those calculations use sections of a specified independently twisted kinetic bundle. Realizing them as derivatives of the master field would require the holonomic constraints and the actual induced kinetic operator. Equality of carrier ranks alone does not provide that realization. The result concerns the written local scalar term and changes of its derivative coordinates. It does not exclude different nonlinear spatial branches, a derived interaction from complementary modes of the same field, or a different master term. It leaves the assigned particle dimensionalities and mode indices unchanged. Verification local_current_jet_checks.py compares (13) with independently expanded complex spatial polynomials. It checks the complete real-linear variation, trace identities, both signs of  eta, scalar-null fields, and covariance when all spin data are rotated together. The largest explicit real Jacobian has dimension 448, retaining every derivative through order two in six dimensions for an eight-component spinor. A nonflat metric-compatible connection is checked in two independent ways: symmetrized ordered covariant differentiation and a matrix exponential along radial lines. Their current jets and full nonlinear variations agree. Exact binomial identities verify the plane-wave cancellation at arbitrary multiindices through the assigned degrees, without constructing millions of coefficient entries. Symbolic differentiation also verifies the kinetic counterexample (20).

title: Physical contact on the tangent-mode band
summary: The complete holomorphic tangent-mode band has an exact polarization-dependent physical point-contact spectrum, whose largest eigenvalue differs from the auxiliary simplex count.
text:
Summary: The complete holomorphic tangent-mode band has an exact polarization-dependent physical point-contact spectrum, whose largest eigenvalue differs from the auxiliary simplex count. Project the actual spatial sections The coherent spatial mode-bundle construction puts the tangent-mode carrier and the spatial Dirac field on the same curved geometry. Its natural spatial evaluation map can now be computed, including the full holomorphic coefficient space and its kinetic norm. The fixed-line spatial spectral band is a distinct construction: it adds nonholomorphic spatial harmonics on one line bundle. That band has a different evaluation spectrum and an exact simplex dimension up to a constant. Matching a dimension does not identify it with the tangent-mode bundle considered here. Use the specified physical geometry Q=\mathrm{CP}^m, with m=3 for six ordinary macroscopic spatial directions. The radius R remains undetermined, and no dimensions are compactified. Formulas at other m\ge2 are conditional geometric comparisons, not particle identifications. Let T=T^{1,0}Q, and retain W=\mathbf1\oplus T\oplus T^*,\qquad E_N=\operatorname{Sym}^N W,\qquad F_{N,L}=\mathcal O(L)\otimes E_N,\qquad L\ge0. 	ag{1} The connection and Hermitian metric are induced by the spatial geometry. The fixed line degree L and cumulative mode degree N are different data. The carrier rank remains D_{N,2m}= inom{N+2m}{2m}. 	ag{2} For the canonical Spin^c operator twisted by F_{N,L}, define \mathcal H_{N,L}=H^0(Q,F_{N,L}). 	ag{3} This is its complete holomorphic zero-form channel. The full Dirac kernel also contains the higher Dolbeault cohomologies H^j(Q,F_{N,L}), which need not vanish. A scalar multiplication source acting on a zero-form remains a zero-form, so (3) is its full projection onto the Dirac kernel. The operator calculation below does not bound all the other form channels or replace a continued nonlinear spatial solution. Use unit spatial measure d
u first. At q\in Q, let \operatorname{ev}_q:\mathcal H_{N,L}\longrightarrow F_{N,L,q}, \qquad s\longmapsto s(q),\qquad C_{N,L}(q)=\operatorname{ev}_q\operatorname{ev}_q^\dagger. 	ag{4} The physical point form on the global section space is T_q=\operatorname{ev}_q^\dagger\operatorname{ev}_q. Its nonzero eigenvalues are precisely those of C_{N,L}(q). For a specified unit fibre polarization \xi, the polarized point form is rank one, with nonzero eigenvalue \langle\xi,C_{N,L}(q)\xiangle when that number is nonzero. The physical position q is not an auxiliary mode-phase ray. Decompose every tangent-mode component The slack component in (1) gives the orthogonal parallel decomposition E_N= igoplus_{k+j\le N}\operatorname{Sym}^k T \otimes\operatorname{Sym}^j T^*. 	ag{5} Contracting one tangent and one cotangent index decomposes each summand into trace-free pieces. Write p=k-\ell, q=j-\ell, where 0\le\ell\le\min(k,j). Use q as an integer label in the formulas below, rather than as the spatial point in (4). The trace-free piece has fibre rank r_{p,q}^{(m)} = inom{p+m-1}{m-1} inom{q+m-1}{m-1} - inom{p+m-2}{m-1} inom{q+m-2}{m-1}, 	ag{6} where the second term is zero if p=0 or q=0. Its multiplicity in E_N is 
u_{N,p,q}=\left\lfloor rac{N-p-q}{2}ightfloor+1, \qquad p,q\ge0,\quad p+q\le N. 	ag{7} The contraction and trace insertion are parallel maps, so these are holomorphic orthogonal subbundles with the induced metric. Their ranks satisfy \sum_{p+q\le N}
u_{N,p,q}r_{p,q}^{(m)}=D_{N,2m}. 	ag{8} An independent character identity checks the complete decomposition, not only its rank. If h_p(x) is the complete symmetric polynomial in m variables, the trace-free character is h_p(x)h_q(x^{-1})-h_{p-1}(x)h_{q-1}(x^{-1}). Multiplying by the line character to power p-q and summing with (7) reproduces the degree-N symmetric character of all 2m+1 entries of W. Holomorphic sections fix the evaluation eigenvalues Let \mathcal Q be the rank-m tautological quotient bundle on projective space. The Euler sequence gives T=\mathcal O(1)\otimes\mathcal Q. The trace-free piece labelled by (p,q) consequently has the quotient-bundle highest weight (p,0,\ldots,0,-q) and line twist t=L+p-q. For the Borel–Weil–Bott calculation, its complete weight and shift are \lambda=(p,\underbrace{0,\ldots,0}_{m-2},-q,-t), \qquad \varrho=(m,m-1,\ldots,0). 	ag{9} If \lambda+\varrho has a repeated entry, all cohomology vanishes. Otherwise sorting those entries gives the unique cohomology degree; subtracting \varrho gives the corresponding highest weight. This is the homogeneous-bundle cohomology rule, with the dual and quotient conventions described in Marian, Oprea and Sam, Section 2.3.2. The explicit application (9) is also checked against the independent Euler index below. There are holomorphic sections precisely when (9) is already dominant:  oxed{L+p\ge2q.} 	ag{10} When (10) holds, the Weyl dimension formula divides into the fibre dimension (6) and the factors involving the last weight in (9):  oxed{ b_{p,q,L}^{(m)} = rac{(L+p-2q+1)(L+2p-q+m)}{m!} \prod_{j=2}^{m-1}(L+p-q+j). } 	ag{11} The product is empty for m=2. More explicitly, \dim H^0(F_{p,q,L})=r_{p,q}^{(m)}b_{p,q,L}^{(m)}. This follows directly by separating the factors with last index m+1 in \prod_{i<j}(\lambda_i-\lambda_j+j-i)/(j-i). Spatial homogeneity makes the diagonal evaluation operator on each irreducible fibre block a scalar. Its trace integral is the dimension of the global section space. Since the measure has total volume one, that scalar is the dimension divided by the fibre rank, namely (11). Thus the complete nonzero spectrum of C_{N,L} is  oxed{b_{p,q,L}^{(m)} \quad	ext{with multiplicity }
u_{N,p,q}r_{p,q}^{(m)}, \quad p+q\le N,\quad L+p\ge2q.} 	ag{12} The other fibre blocks have zero evaluation. On the global section space, T_q has these same nonzero eigenvalues and its remaining kernel. Equivalent copies in (7) remain orthogonal copies with the same scalar; their number does not multiply the eigenvalue on one copy. The sharp physical contact strength All positive factors in (11) are maximized at p=N, q=0. Therefore  oxed{ \|T_q\|=\|C_{N,L}(q)\|=B_{N,L}^{(m)} = rac{L+2N+m}{m} inom{L+N+m-1}{m-1}. } 	ag{13} For fixed L, this grows as 2N^m/m!. It differs from the auxiliary mode-fibre point-contact eigenvalue D_{N,2m}, which grows as N^{2m}/(2m)!. They are evaluations on different spaces with different metrics and sections. There is also a particularly simple coherent polarization: the pure slack vector e_0^{\odot N}. Its physical evaluation strength is  oxed{ \langle e_0^{\odot N},C_{N,L}e_0^{\odot N}angle = inom{L+m}{m}, } 	ag{14} independent of N. The auxiliary isotropic ray contact instead assigns D_{N,2m} to that coherent ray as well. The natural spatial connection does not supply the larger isotropy of the homogenized mode fibre. For the six-dimensional candidate with L=0: Cumulative degree N Carrier rank D_{N,6} Largest physical point eigenvalue B_{N,0}^{(3)} Physical slack eigenvalue 12 18\,564 819 1 34 3\,838\,380 14\,910 1 These are normalized operator eigenvalues, not particle masses. A different fibre polarization can have a smaller point expectation. The table does not establish that no independently selected pair of physical states could fit a particular finite ratio, nor does it compare alternative particle dimensionalities. It shows that this specified physical projection does not itself produce the isotropic simplex operator. With physical volume \mathcal V, every value in (12)–(14) gains the same factor 1/\mathcal V. A common sector scale cannot remove their different dependence on N. An explicit spatial field attains the bound The largest value in (13) has an independent spatial realization. Let X be the holomorphic projective vector field induced by the matrix E_{10}. For unit homogeneous coordinates, put p_j=|Z_j|^2. The tangent metric gives \|X\|^2=p_0(1-p_1),\qquad s_{N,L}=Z_0^L X^{\odot N},\qquad \|s_{N,L}\|^2=p_0^{L+N}(1-p_1)^N. 	ag{15} This is a global section in the \operatorname{Sym}^N T component, including its zeros. It is pointwise coherent where it is nonzero. At the coordinate pole Z=e_0, its squared norm is one. Under unit FS measure, p_1 has beta distribution (1,m), while p_0/(1-p_1) conditionally has beta distribution (1,m-1). Hence  egin{aligned} \int\|s_{N,L}\|^2d
u &= rac{m}{L+2N+m}  rac{(m-1)!(L+N)!}{(L+N+m-1)!}\ &= rac1{B_{N,L}^{(m)}}. \end{aligned} 	ag{16} Thus \sqrt{B_{N,L}^{(m)}}s_{N,L} has unit norm and squared value B_{N,L}^{(m)} at the pole, attaining (13). No representation dimension formula is used in this integral. The same field's normalized local quartic is  oxed{ \intho_{N,L}^2d
u = rac{(B_{N,L}^{(m)})^2}{B_{2N,2L}^{(m)}}. } 	ag{17} More generally, every unit section in (3) obeys ho(q)\le B_{N,L}^{(m)} and therefore \intho^2d
u\le B_{N,L}^{(m)}. This is a bound on the stated holomorphic channel. A finite nonlinear branch with complementary Dirac components has to be solved separately. The source-preservation criterion continues to distinguish an occupied expectation from an exact linear stationary frequency. Check the higher forms through an independent index The Euler sequence gives the K-theory class [W]=(m+1)[\mathcal O(1)]+(m+1)[\mathcal O(-1)]-[\mathbf1]. If H is the hyperplane class and z is a formal counting variable, the symmetric-power character is \sum_{N\ge0}\operatorname{ch}(E_N)z^N = rac{1-z}{(1-ze^H)^{m+1}(1-ze^{-H})^{m+1}}. 	ag{18} Taking its coefficient and using \chi(\mathcal O(k))=\prod_{j=1}^m(k+j)/m! gives an independent Euler characteristic, including negative line degrees. It agrees with the alternating sum of all cohomology groups from (9). Serre duality also gives h^j(E_N(L))=h^{m-j}(E_N(-L-m-1)), because E_N is self-dual. For CP3 the result simplifies exactly:  oxed{ \chi(E_N(L)) = inom{N+6}{6}\chi(\mathcal O(L)) +4(L+2) inom{N+7}{8}. } 	ag{19} To see the second term, expand the cubic polynomial \chi(\mathcal O(L+k)). Symmetry between the positive and negative line summands makes its odd k moments cancel. The coefficient of k^2 is (L+2)/2, and (18) gives second moment 8 inom{N+7}{8}. This separates the carrier rank from the contribution of its curvature. For example, at N=2, L=0, the Dolbeault cohomology dimensions in form degrees zero through three are (101,1,0,0), with index 100. At N=12 they are (840\,636,35\,106,11\,873,194\,183), with index 623\,220. The holomorphic section count alone is therefore not the entire Dirac zero-mode count or its chiral index. Verification and consequence for the master projection tangent_band_contact_checks.py checks complete characters and ranks, the full cohomology algorithm, the independent Euler index, Serre duality, every point eigenvalue and the explicit extremizer integrals. A separate spatial calculation constructs all 15 holomorphic tangent vector fields on CP3 from traceless matrices. Direct integration normalizes their Gram matrix and gives three point eigenvalues equal to 5. Their 120 symmetric products have an integrated Gram matrix of rank 84. Using its inverse on that support gives six physical point eigenvalues equal to 14, in agreement with (13) at N=2. The calculation retains the product relations and uses two independent spatial cubature orders. Counting all 120 generators as orthonormal sections would give the wrong operator. The natural cumulative inclusions preserve the existing degree blocks and their connections, as required by consistent band contacts. This spatial projection is also distinct from the flat oscillator point form, whose spatial profiles and metric are different. The calculation derives the evaluation operator once the specified spatial point form and kinetic bundle are adopted. A smooth local scalar current still does not itself impose a point insertion. Deriving the master field's actual interaction, projection and canonical normalization remains necessary before the auxiliary simplex eigenvalue can be identified with a physical mass.

title: Coherent spatial mode-bundle fields
summary: Pointwise coherent fields on the curved tangent-mode bundle can have balanced spatial moments, but local contact and a transported graph pairing retain different band-dependent normalizations.
text:
Summary: Pointwise coherent fields on the curved tangent-mode bundle can have balanced spatial moments, but local contact and a transported graph pairing retain different band-dependent normalizations. Keep the physical field and its mode bundle together The balanced spatial construction gives exact linear frequencies for a specified first-moment interaction. Its field is a section of a spatial line twist. The mass-counting construction uses a second object: the cumulative tangent-mode bundle. Compatibility requires a field on that bundle with its actual connection. An arbitrary constant array of coefficients cannot replace the connection of the curved tangent directions. Use the specified physical CP3 geometry, with undetermined Fubini–Study radius R. Its six directions remain ordinary macroscopic spatial directions, without compactification. The following complex bundle types describe that same real tangent geometry; they do not partition the six directions into preferred real subspaces. Write T=T^{1,0}\mathrm{CP}^3. The Kähler metric gives a parallel complex linear identification of the (0,1) cotangent bundle with T. Thus the homogenized mode bundle and its degree-N carrier have the holomorphic descriptions W=\mathbf1\oplus T\oplus T^*,\qquad E_N=\operatorname{Sym}^N W,\qquad \operatorname{rank}E_N=D_N= inom{N+6}{6}. 	ag{1} The natural connection is the direct-sum and symmetric-power connection induced by the spatial Levi–Civita connection. On a Kähler manifold the tangent Chern connection equals the Levi–Civita connection; its (0,1) part in a holomorphic frame is  ar\partial. See Calegari, Section 1.5. The calculation below retains this connection rather than trivializing E_N. Specify the canonical Spin^c field bundle and Dirac operator \Sigma_N=\Lambda^{0,*}\otimes E_N,\qquad \mathscr D_N=\sqrt2( ar\partial_{E_N}+ ar\partial_{E_N}^{\dagger}), \qquad  eta=(-1)^{	ext{exterior degree}}. 	ag{2} This is the degree-zero line twist of the spatial Dirac comparison, with E_N now retained. It is an explicit kinetic candidate. Its occurrence in the master spinor projection, the independence or derivative constraints of its coefficient fields, and the canonical metric inherited from that projection still need derivation. Equation (1) alone supplies a bundle, not those physical conclusions. A global coherent field with the full connection A complex matrix A induces a holomorphic vector field on projective space. For diagonal A=\operatorname{diag}(a_0,a_1,a_2,a_3), its expression in the chart Z_0

u = rac{6(2a)!(2b)!}{(2a+2b+3)!}. 	ag{10} For example, u has the beta distribution with parameters (2,2); conditionally, x/u and y/(1-u) are independent uniform variables on [-1,1]. Their elementary integrals prove (10). Expanding h^N gives  oxed{\mathcal Z_N= \sum_{a+b\le N}(-1)^{a+b}  rac{N!\,2^{N-a-b}}{a!b!(N-a-b)!}  rac{6(2a)!(2b)!}{(2a+2b+3)!}.} 	ag{11} In particular, \mathcal Z_0=1, \mathcal Z_1=9/5, and \mathcal Z_2=49/15. For N\ge1, Jensen's inequality and (8) give \left( rac95ight)^N\le\mathcal Z_N\le2^N. 	ag{12} The same fixed geometry and vector field therefore produce a definite, nontrivial dependence of the canonical normalization on N. This construction removes a possible incompatibility between the curved mode bundle, its coherent field, and the balanced spatial source. It does not derive g_N or K_1. u= rac{\mathcal Z_{2N}}{\mathcal Z_N^2},\qquad \|(ho_N-A_N)\chi_N\|^2 = rac{\mathcal Z_{3N}}{\mathcal Z_N^3}-A_N^2. 	ag{15} Both the nonconstant density and its derivative matter. Thus ho_N\chi_N leaves the full holomorphic zero space for N>0. An independent differential quantity is  egin{aligned} |

It gives a direct test of leakage from the whole zero space, without restricting the spatial perturbations to a chosen radial basis. The assigned cumulative indices give the following diagnostic values. A_N is an interaction expectation on the specified field, not a mass or the frequency of a solved local-contact branch. Cumulative degree N Mode rank D_N Canonical norm factor \mathcal Z_N Local contraction A_N 12 18\,564 1694.763120675 1.509635753 34 3\,838\,380 3.391520233	imes10^9 2.835194788 A transported graph pairing is a distinct action The local graph pairing uses the coincident coherent overlap and gives D_NJ^2 at one physical point. It preserves the parallel slack line. On the positive-chirality coefficient fields under consideration, the transported graph extension is the well-defined quartic \mathcal E_{\mathrm{pair}}(\psi)=  rac{\kappa D_N}{2}\int\!\int K_1(q,q') |\langle\psi(q),U_{q\leftarrow q'}\psi(q')angle|^2d

u(q'). 	ag{18} This operator contraction differs from multiplying \psi(q) by the convolution of its scalar density. That distinction remains even when the scalar spatial moment is balanced. This is a necessary occupied equation, not a proof that the other equations admit that profile. The strictly increasing \mathcal Z_N prevents a common frequency-to-count coefficient on these fields for this particular action. title: Balanced spatial branches with an exact linear frequency
summary: Balanced holomorphic fields on the specified physical CP3 geometry have an exact normalized linear frequency for the smooth moment kernel and no exponential modes in their complete spatial linearization.
text:
Summary: Balanced holomorphic fields on the specified physical CP3 geometry have an exact normalized linear frequency for the smooth moment kernel and no exponential modes in their complete spatial linearization. A spatial solution of the normalization problem A nonconstant spatial field can produce a constant scalar potential without requiring the interaction kernel itself to be constant. The distinction matters for the source-preservation theorem: its whole-band degeneracy conclusion assumes a coherent holomorphic section. Certain noncoherent holomorphic superpositions instead balance their source moments and preserve an exact linear branch for the already specified smooth spatial moment kernel. The result below constructs such fields and treats their complete spatial linearization, including the entire holomorphic multiplet and the excited source modes. It solves a conditional spatial normalization and spectral stability problem. The kernel's origin in the master action and its causal completion remain open. Use the specified physical CP3 geometry, with its undetermined Fubini–Study radius R. Its six spatial directions are ordinary and macroscopic; there is no compactification. The calculation uses the canonical Spin^c bundle \Lambda^{0,*}\otimes\mathcal O(L) and spatial Dirac operator \mathscr D_L=\sqrt2( ar\partial_L+ ar\partial_L^\dagger). The degree L is a geometric input, not the cumulative mass-band label N=n-1. No identification of L with the electron or muon mode index is made. Write m=3 and r=m+1=4 for CP3; the mathematical formulas extend to CPm. Work first in radius units and unit spatial measure d
u. For the one field, define  egin{aligned} \sigma_\psi&=\psi^\dagger eta\psi,& M_\psi&=\int P_Z\sigma_\psi(Z)\,d
u(Z),& P_Z&= rac{ZZ^\dagger}{Z^\dagger Z},\ \mathcal E_g(\psi)&=\langle\psi,\mathscr D_L\psiangle + rac{gr}{2}\operatorname{Tr}(M_\psi^2),& V_\psi(Z)&=r\operatorname{Tr}(P_ZM_\psi),&  eta&=(-1)^{	ext{exterior degree}}. \end{aligned} 	ag{1} Its exact equation is i\partial_t\psi=(\mathscr D_L+gV_\psi eta)\psi. The matrix M_\psi is a moment of this same spatial field. It is not an independent interaction field or a mediator particle. Equation (1) is the normalized kernel K_1(Z,W)=r|Z^\dagger W|^2 on unit homogeneous representatives, with the physical measure understood as above. Balanced holomorphic sections give exact branches Let H_L=H^0(\mathcal O(L)) be the complete holomorphic zero space. For a unit section \chi\in H_L, impose the balance condition  oxed{M_\chi= rac{I_r}{r}.} 	ag{2} Then V_\chi=1 at every spatial point, while \mathscr D_L\chi=0 and  eta\chi=\chi. Consequently  oxed{\psi(t)=e^{-igt}\chi,\qquad \|\psi\|^2=1,\qquad \omega=g,\qquad \mathcal E_g(\chi)= rac g2.} 	ag{3} This is an exact nonlinear spatial solution for every real g, not a small-coupling expansion or a frozen-potential calculation. Perturbations must still vary M_\psi through the same equation. An explicit balanced section exists at every integer L\ge2:  oxed{\chi_F(Z)=\sqrt{ rac{D_L}{r}} \sum_{i=1}^r Z_i^L,\qquad D_L= inom{L+r-1}{r-1}.} 	ag{4} The expression in (4) is a homogeneous polynomial representing a line section, not a globally single-valued scalar function. Its pointwise squared norm divides the squared polynomial by (Z^\dagger Z)^L. The projective monomial identity \int Z^\alpha\overline{Z^ eta}\,d
u = egin{cases} \displaystyle rac{(r-1)!\prod_i\alpha_i!}{(s+r-1)!}, &\alpha= eta,\quad |\alpha|=| eta|=s,\ 0,&\alpha
e eta \end{cases} 	ag{5} uses unit representatives and applies to the phase-invariant integrand. It gives unit norm in (4). Each diagonal entry of M is 1/r. An off-diagonal moment changes one occupation in each monomial; for L\ge2, it cannot match two distinct pure powers Z_i^L,Z_j^L. Thus every off-diagonal moment vanishes, proving (2). The case L=1 does not satisfy this argument. For any pure degree-one section, the moment is (I_r+aa^\dagger)/(r+1) with a unit, so it is not isotropic when r>1. Balance does not make the field density spatially constant. At a coordinate pole its density is D_L/r, whereas at Z=(1,e^{i\pi/L},0,\ldots,0)/\sqrt2 the polynomial in (4) vanishes. The higher spatial harmonics retain a definite shape. Physical unitary isometries rotate that shape while preserving (2). Spatial source maps on the full holomorphic multiplet Use traceless Hermitian matrices T_a, a=1,\ldots,r^2-1, with \operatorname{Tr}(T_aT_b)=\delta_{ab}. Their real spatial functions are f_a(Z)=\operatorname{Tr}(P_ZT_a),\qquad u_a=f_a\chi. Let P_0 project onto all of H_L and set v_a=P_0u_a, w_a=(I-P_0)u_a. The normalized occupation basis for homogeneous polynomials gives P_0(f_T\chi)= rac{\mathcal R(T)+\operatorname{Tr}(T)I}{L+r}\chi, \qquad \mathcal R(T)=\sum_{ij}T_{ij}a_j^\dagger a_i. 	ag{6} Here creation and annihilation notation describes finite polynomial representations. It does not introduce constituent particles, field statistics or additional physical dimensions. The index order in (6) matches f_T=Z^\dagger TZ on holomorphic polynomials. It follows directly from (5), including the normalization of each monomial. Balance means \langle\chi,\mathcal R(T_a)\chiangle=0. The complete spatial derivative satisfies \mathscr D_L^2(f_T\chi) =4\left[(L+r)f_T\chi- (\mathcal R(T)+\operatorname{Tr}(T))\chiight]. 	ag{7} One can verify (7) in a physical projective chart by differentiating f_T and the holomorphic polynomial with the Chern connection. Together with (6), it gives  oxed{\mathscr D_L^2w_a=\lambda^2w_a, \qquad \lambda^2=4(L+r).} 	ag{8} Each w_a is a zero-form section; its Dirac image is an exact one-form. No further form component is generated when applying the Dirac operator again. Hence the span of H_L, the w_a, and their Dirac images is an exact invariant source space. This is a spatial closure of the linearized source, not a restriction to radial perturbations. Exact source Gram matrices Define G_{ab}=\langle u_a,u_bangle,\qquad (G_0)_{ab}=\langle v_a,v_bangle,\qquad G_1=G-G_0. 	ag{9} The full G is real and symmetric because f_a,f_b are real functions. The imaginary part of G_0 is a commutator expectation of the operators in (6). It vanishes at a balanced state. All three Gram matrices can therefore be treated as real symmetric matrices without discarding any complex field perturbation. Applying (5) to two spatial moment functions gives, for traceless Hermitian T,U at a balanced section, \langle f_Tf_Uangle_\chi = rac{\operatorname{Re}\langle\mathcal R(T)\chi, \mathcal R(U)\chiangle+(1+L/r)\operatorname{Tr}(TU)} {(L+r)(L+r+1)}. 	ag{10} The terms linear in a generator vanish by balance. The remaining symmetrized quadratic generator term and the scalar contraction in (10) come from the two possible contractions of the added coordinate factors. Together with (6), this yields  oxed{G= rac{(L+r)G_0+I/r}{L+r+1},\qquad G_1= rac{I/r-G_0}{L+r+1}.} 	ag{11} The complement has strictly positive norm for every nonzero traceless T. Otherwise f_T\chi would be holomorphic, and the real source-preservation theorem would force f_T to be constant. That is impossible for nonzero traceless T. Since G_0\ge0, each eigenvalue \gamma of G_1 consequently obeys  oxed{0<r\gamma\le rac1{L+r+1}<1.} 	ag{12} This bound controls the complete source spectrum without choosing one polarization or one angular harmonic. For the explicit section (4) and L\ge3, G_0 has eigenvalues  rac{L^2}{r(L+r)^2}\quad(r-1	ext{ copies}),\qquad  rac{L}{r(L+r)^2}\quad(r(r-1)	ext{ copies}). 	ag{13} Diagonal generators and off-diagonal generators give these two values. For L=2, the nonzero value is 4/[r(L+r)^2] with multiplicity (r-1)(r+2)/2; zero has multiplicity r(r-1)/2. The zero directions are the real orthogonal symmetries of the quadratic polynomial. Equation (11) gives the complementary eigenvalues in all cases. The complete spatial linearization has no exponential modes Linearize the field in the rotating frame of (3). Let U have columns u_a in orthonormal spatial source coordinates, with \chi embedded in the full retained zero space. The ordinary and conjugate variations are  egin{aligned} i\dot\eta&=A\eta+B ar\eta,\ A&=\mathscr D_L+g eta-gI+g\chi\chi^\dagger+grUU^\dagger,\ B&=g\chi\chi^T+grUU^T. \end{aligned} 	ag{14} The \chi terms retain the response of the scalar trace, including changes of the total norm. The U terms retain every traceless spatial moment and both quadratures. Freezing the moment matrix would remove these terms and give an incomplete stability test. Because the source Gram matrices are real, choose orthonormal coordinates in which their source vectors are real. On a first excited zero-form and its Dirac one-form partner, the free rotating operator is A_0= egin{pmatrix}0&\lambda\\lambda&-2g\end{pmatrix}. 	ag{15} The real quadrature in the retained zero space is constant under the linearized evolution. For a nonzero-frequency mode it must therefore vanish. Its conjugate quadrature can still respond; it is retained in (14). After diagonalizing G_1, the remaining pair at eigenvalue \gamma has squared-frequency matrix A_0\left[A_0+2gr\gamma  egin{pmatrix}1&0\0&0\end{pmatrix}ight]. Its two eigenvalues are  oxed{\Omega_\pm^2=\lambda^2+2g^2 \pm2|g|\sqrt{g^2+(1-r\gamma)\lambda^2}.} 	ag{16} By (12), the square root is real. The sum of the two eigenvalues is positive and their product is \lambda^4+4g^2r\gamma\lambda^2>0, so both are positive. Thus all nonzero source modes oscillate rather than grow exponentially, at every real coupling g. Norm, phase, polarization and possible Jordan directions remain at zero frequency; this is not a claim that every linear perturbation stays bounded for all time. Finally, the orthogonal complement of the exact source space in (8) has zero linear scalar-moment source. Self-adjointness of \mathscr D_L and invariance under  eta make it a reducing subspace. Its evolution is generated by the self-adjoint operator \mathscr D_L+g eta-gI. It therefore cannot add an exponential mode. This includes the other spatial harmonics and form polarizations omitted by a radial ansatz. The conclusion concerns the complete spatial linearization of (1). What is now available for the mass calculation These balanced fields have a common normalized frequency \omega=g without a profile-dependent cubic or higher-order correction. They therefore satisfy the spatial source-preservation requirement identified by the nonlinear reduction, and their complete linear spectrum passes the stability test above. Restoring the physical volume \mathcal V and a fixed canonical norm Q, the normalized moment convention gives \omega_{\mathrm{physical}}= rac{g_{\mathrm{physical}}Q}{\mathcal V}, \qquad E_{\mathrm{physical}}= rac{g_{\mathrm{physical}}Q^2}{2\mathcal V}. 	ag{17} If an independent master derivation supplied g_{\mathrm{physical},N}=\kappa D_N, this spatial family would preserve its linear count dependence at common Q and \mathcal V. That premise has not been supplied by this calculation. Compatibility with the occupied auxiliary coherent-ray prescription must also be established; coherence of that mode-bundle ray is distinct from coherence of a holomorphic spatial section on CP3. The frequency-energy distinction remains visible in (17). The observed rest mass, physical metric scale, occupied section degree, causal master kernel and nonlinear orbital stability are not determined here. Balance supplies a family of spatial shapes, not selection of a unique particle. Its isotropic first moment leaves higher spatial harmonics intact; their role in a reciprocal interaction must be calculated with the appropriate same-field source. The coherent spatial mode-bundle construction retains the curved tangent-mode carrier and gives a separate family with pointwise mode coherence and balanced spatial moments. Its exact norm makes the distinction between scalar and transported graph contractions explicit. That larger field bundle has a different spatial response, so the linear stability theorem above is not automatically its theorem. Verification balanced_spatial_mass_checks.py uses independent projective monomial integrals for the norm, balance, Toeplitz projection and full fourth-moment Gram matrix. A separate physical-chart derivative checks (7). The diagnostic assembles (14) with the entire holomorphic zero multiplet and both excited form components, then compares every nonzero eigenfrequency with (16), retaining the zero-frequency directions. The CP3 controls use L=2,3,4,6, including a complex spatial rotation of the quadratic field. Lower-complex-dimension controls test the general identities without reassigning any particle depth. The calculation is finite because the linear source closes exactly; the free orthogonal spatial complement is handled by the self-adjoint argument above.

title: Spatial source preservation for an exact linear branch
summary: Exact preservation of a holomorphic spatial section forces a constant real scalar potential. If a covariant kernel preserves a coherent section, every normalized section in that band has the same frequency.
text:
Summary: Exact preservation of a holomorphic spatial section forces a constant real scalar potential. If a covariant kernel preserves a coherent section, every normalized section in that band has the same frequency. The spatial condition behind exact linearity The nonlinear mass reduction gives, for a normalized analytic chiral branch, \omega(g)=gA-4g^3C+O(g^5),\qquad C=A\|\eta\|^2+\langle\eta,V_\chi\etaangle, \quad \eta=-\mathscr D_\perp^{-1}(I-P)(V_\chi\chi). 	ag{1} Here P retains the whole zero space in the stated problem. Under A>0 and V_\chi\ge0, C=0 precisely when the complementary source vanishes. An exact linear frequency near g=0 must therefore satisfy that source-preservation condition. This note determines its spatial meaning for the specified CP3 Dirac geometry. The physical electron directions remain six ordinary macroscopic spatial directions. CP3 and its Fubini–Study metric are conditional hypotheses about their global spatial geometry, with an undetermined physical radius. There is no compactification. Its holomorphic section degree L is an input to this comparison and is not the cumulative mass-band label N=n-1. Use the canonical Spin^c bundle \Lambda^{0,*}\otimes\mathcal O(L), L\ge0, and \mathscr D_L=\sqrt2( ar\partial_L+ ar\partial_L^\dagger). For the following formulas the geometry is CPm, with m=3 in the six-dimensional comparison. The zero space is the positive-chirality holomorphic section space H_L=H^0(\mathcal O(L)). Use unit spatial measure d
u and unit norm for \chi\in H_L. The radius, physical volume and canonical norm are restored as in the spatial branch note. Preserving a holomorphic section forces a constant potential Let V be a smooth real scalar function on this connected spatial manifold, and let \chi be a nonzero holomorphic section. Then  oxed{V\chi\in H_L\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad V 	ext{ is spatially constant}.} 	ag{2} To prove the nontrivial direction, take a local holomorphic frame away from the zero set of \chi. There 0= ar\partial_L(V\chi)=( ar\partial V)\chi, so  ar\partial V=0. Because V is real, its conjugate derivative also vanishes. A nonzero holomorphic section has a zero set with empty interior. Smoothness therefore extends dV=0 over that set, and connectedness makes V constant globally. The converse is immediate. The argument concerns a scalar multiplication operator on actual spatial sections, not an arbitrary matrix on their coefficient space. Suppose now that V=K|\chi|^2, where K is real, reciprocal and normalized by K1=1. Reciprocity and unit norm imply \int V\,d
u=\langle1,K|\chi|^2angle =\langle K1,|\chi|^2angle=1. Thus the constant in (2) must be one. The unchanged field then solves (\mathscr D_L+gV eta)\chi=g\chi,\qquad \omega=g,\qquad \mathcal E_g(\chi)= rac g2. 	ag{3} For local contact K=I and L>0, this cannot hold: every nonzero holomorphic section of this line bundle has zeros. Restrict its homogeneous polynomial to a projective line on which it is not identically zero; a positive-degree homogeneous polynomial in two complex coordinates has a projective zero. Its squared norm therefore cannot be a positive spatial constant. The field must acquire a complementary spatial response if it continues as a stationary solution of that local equation. Equation (2) does not say that the kernel itself must be spatially constant. A nonconstant kernel can send a particular source to a constant. Its action on the full source family is the next question. Preserving a coherent section with a covariant kernel makes the band degenerate Assume K commutes with all physical Fubini–Study isometries. On scalar spatial harmonics it has real multipliers k_\ell: K=\sum_{\ell\ge0}k_\ell\Pi_\ell,\qquad k_0=1. 	ag{4} The spatial harmonic calculation derives their dimensions, normalized zonal functions and coherent convolution eigenvalues. Define  egin{aligned} h_\ell&= inom{\ell+m}{m}^2- inom{\ell+m-1}{m}^2, \quad h_0=1,\ Z_\ell(t)&= rac{P_\ell^{(m-1,0)}(2t-1)}{ inom{\ell+m-1}{\ell}},\ b_\ell(L)&= rac{L!(L+m)!}{(L-\ell)!(L+m+\ell)!} \quad(0\le\ell\le L), \end{aligned} 	ag{5} with b_\ell(L)=0 for \ell>L. For a normalized coherent section centered at the spatial point a, put t=|a^\dagger Z|^2 using unit representatives. Its density has the complete expansion ho_a(Z)=D_Lt^L =\sum_{\ell=0}^Lh_\ell b_\ell(L)Z_\ell(t),\qquad D_L= inom{L+m}{m}. 	ag{6} This follows from the zonal orthogonality \int Z_\ell^2d
u=1/h_\ell and the beta integral giving b_\ell(L). Every coefficient through L is nonzero. Consequently  oxed{Kho_a=1\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad k_1=k_2=\cdots=k_L=0.} 	ag{7} Covariance makes this condition independent of the chosen center a. More strongly, the density of every \varphi\in H_L lies in scalar harmonics 0 through L: it is the restriction of a polynomial of bidegree (L,L), with successive traces giving those harmonic degrees. Therefore (7) implies K|\varphi|^2=\|\varphi\|^2, \qquad \mathcal E_{\mathrm{int}}(\varphi)= rac g2\|\varphi\|^4 \quad (\varphi\in H_L). 	ag{8} Every unit holomorphic shape is then an exact branch with the same frequency and energy. This interaction cannot select a coherent shape from other complex superpositions in that band. It may still act nontrivially on higher spatial harmonics outside the band's densities. The coherent-section assumption in (7) matters. A noncoherent holomorphic section can have vanishing low harmonic moments even when the kernel retains those harmonics. Its potential can then be constant without forcing the kernel to annihilate every other section's density. Equation (2) still applies, but the whole-band degeneracy conclusion need not. The balanced spatial branch realizes this possibility explicitly for the smooth first-moment kernel. Noncoherent holomorphic sections with an isotropic spatial moment give exact linear frequencies, and their complete spatial linearization has no exponential modes. Their density remains nonconstant. For example, K(Z,W)=1+\alpha Z_{L+1}(|Z^\dagger W|^2),\qquad 0<\alpha<1, 	ag{9} is positive pointwise because |Z_\ell|\le1. It is a nonconstant, reciprocal, covariant kernel satisfying (7). Its only nonzero multiplier above the constant is \alpha/h_{L+1}. This example prevents inferring that preservation of one finite band forces K=\Pi_0 everywhere. title: Scalar gap with canonical normalization
summary: A specified global scalar interaction admits a self-consistent gap and an exact collective response frequency, while canonical normalization determines whether a cumulative mode count enhances either quantity.
text: Summary: A specified global scalar interaction admits a self-consistent gap and an exact collective response frequency, while canonical normalization determines whether a cumulative mode count enhances either quantity. One scalar response from the same field The nonlinear spatial reduction determines how complementary modes alter a proposed linear mass coefficient. A separate constructive question is whether a summed occupied-mode response can itself generate a count-dependent coefficient. The following model makes that question exactly solvable, including its dynamical response. Use one classical complex field with a fixed physical spatial measure, canonical time-kinetic term and energy \begin{aligned} \mathcal E(\psi)&=\langle\psi,\mathscr D\psi\rangle +\frac{\kappa}{2}S(\psi)^2,& S(\psi)&=\langle\psi,\beta\psi\rangle,\\ \mathscr D^\dagger&=\mathscr D,& \beta^\dagger&=\beta,\quad \beta^2=I,\quad \{\mathscr D,\beta\}=0,\quad \kappa>0. \end{aligned} \tag{1} This is a specified global scalar kernel on that spatial domain. For a probability-normalized spatial mean, its coefficient includes the inverse physical volume. Neither its magnitude nor its equality between different spatial sectors is derived here. The global instantaneous kernel also has the causality limitation of that class of effective models. It is not a completed local master law. The positive quartic sign is retained. The field is not silently replaced by a fermionic vacuum or a filled quantum sea; the scalar exchange calculation explains why those would be additional assumptions. All modes below are components of the same field, with no additional mediator particle. The exact equation and conserved positive norm are i\partial_t\psi=(\mathscr D+M(t)\beta)\psi,\qquad M(t)=\kappa S(\psi(t)),\qquad Q=\|\psi\|^2. \tag{2} Immediately, |S|\le Q and hence |M|\le\kappa Q. This bound holds for every solution, without choosing a mode basis or a stationary state. Conserved spectral sectors and the gap equation First work in a finite invariant collection of nonzero kinetic pairs. In each pair choose a basis with \mathscr D_j=\epsilon_j\sigma_x\otimes I_{r_j},\qquad \beta_j=\sigma_z\otimes I_{r_j},\qquad \epsilon_j>0. \tag{3} The r_j complex polarizations are retained. Their rank counts field components, not extra physical spatial dimensions. The norm q_j of the entire pair is conserved because its projector commutes with both operators in (2). Within a degenerate shell this is a basis-independent total norm. Equal amplitudes in one chosen polarization basis are not an invariant occupation prescription. For a constant M>0, let v_j^+(M) be a unit positive eigenvector of \epsilon_j\sigma_x+M\sigma_z, with eigenvalue E_j=\sqrt{\epsilon_j^2+M^2}. For arbitrary fixed unit complex vectors z_j\in\mathbb C^{r_j} and phases, the candidate field is \psi_j(t)=\sqrt{q_j}\,e^{-iE_jt} \bigl(v_j^+(M)\otimes z_j\bigr). \tag{4} Its integrated scalar source is time independent even when the E_j differ. Orthogonality of the kinetic pairs and the block structure of \beta remove the integrated cross terms. A local density can still have spatial interference; this exact reduction uses the global kernel. Since \langle v_j^+,\sigma_zv_j^+\rangle=M/E_j, (2) becomes M=\kappa\sum_j\frac{q_jM}{E_j},\qquad \boxed{\frac1\kappa=\sum_j\frac{q_j}{\sqrt{\epsilon_j^2+M^2}}} \quad (M>0). \tag{5} The right side decreases strictly from \sum q_j/\epsilon_j to zero. Thus there is exactly one positive branch if and only if \kappa\sum_j\frac{q_j}{\epsilon_j}>1. \tag{6} There is also the reflected scalar branch at -M and the zero solution of the original self-consistency equation. These are scalar branches; no antiparticle interpretation is assigned to their signs. Near threshold, write H_s=\sum q_j/\epsilon_j^s. Expanding (5) gives M^2=\frac{2(H_1-1/\kappa)}{H_3} +O\bigl((H_1-1/\kappa)^2\bigr). \tag{7} A populated zero-kinetic sector removes the finite threshold: its term q_0/M diverges as M\downarrow0. A field supported entirely at zero kinetic energy instead has the exact coefficient M=\kappa Q. The nonzero-kinetic response theorem below must not be applied unchanged to that limiting case. A constrained energy maximum and its full response At fixed pair norms the phase space is a product of finite spheres. Introduce a real variational parameter m through the exact identity \frac\kappa2 S^2=\max_m\left(mS-\frac{m^2}{2\kappa}\right). Maximizing first over the field at fixed m gives \max_{\|\psi_j\|^2=q_j}\mathcal E(\psi) =\max_m F(m),\qquad F(m)=\sum_j q_j\sqrt{\epsilon_j^2+m^2}-\frac{m^2}{2\kappa}. \tag{8} The parameter m is only an algebraic device for this extremization. For (6), F has maxima at \pm M. Its maximizing fields are (4), including the full degenerate polarization and phase families. Conservation of energy gives orbital stability of each maximizing family on this finite fixed-norm manifold. It is an energy maximum, and therefore does not establish a passive ground state.
