Recoil and polarization are different currents For a hydrogen pair with electron charge −e, nuclear charge +e, positions x_e and R_N, and relative coordinate r = x_e−R_N, d_{\rm charge}=eR_N-ex_e=-er. This identity is independent of the origin and the two masses. Nuclear recoil changes the relative dynamics and kinetic reduced mass, but is not an opposite dipole that cancels −er. In the center-of-mass frame the two particles move in opposite directions, so their oppositely signed charges produce current contributions in the same direction. This identity applies to arbitrary relative trajectories, not only circles. It is conditional on the ordinary point/centroid charge assignment, not the demo's raw detector map being physical position. An induced internal nuclear dipole p_N is additional: d_total = −er+p_N. For a general extended V2 source, calculate the two charge-density first moments instead of assigning either centroid from an image. The total net-neutral dipole remains origin independent. Combined radiation, not separate powers At leading electric-dipole order in ordinary electromagnetism, \langle P_{\rm rad}\rangle =\frac{\langle|\ddot d_e+\ddot p_N|^2\rangle}{6\pi\epsilon_0c^3}. The interference term matters. Adding electron-only and nucleus-only powers would miss it. The formula and approximation are derived in UT Austin's dipole-radiation notes. Cancellation of one harmonic requires the nuclear dipole to have the same amplitude and opposite phase in that channel. It does not eliminate other harmonics, magnetic dipole/electric quadrupole emission, or internal absorption. The source dimensions must also be small compared with the wavelengths retained in the dipole approximation. The feedback simulation postprocesses this squared acceleration for the combined scalar dipole and compares it with the electron contribution along the same coupled trajectory. For κ = +0.7 the ratios are approximately 5.29, 5.42, and 5.48 for the two-, four-, and six-petal initial preparations; for κ = −0.7 they are 1.90, 1.86, and 1.84. These are dimensionless transient test results, not physical atomic power estimates. Initial nuclear relaxation was not assumed; the induced free oscillation contributes. Reversing the coupling sign changes interference without changing the electron state. The simulation does not include radiative backreaction itself. A fixed-radius proton benchmark For an illustrative ordinary electron at fixed distance R from a small proton, its quasistatic field at the proton is E_e = e r̂/(4πε₀R²), whereas its relative dipole is d_e = −eR r̂. Define the nuclear electric polarizability volume α_V by p_N = 4πε₀α_V E_e. In the static-response regime, p_N=-\frac{\alpha_V}{R^3}d_e,\qquad d_{\rm total}=\left(1-\frac{\alpha_V}{R^3}\right)d_e. This is the favorable sign for partial electric-dipole cancellation. As a versioned benchmark, the PDG 2024 proton listing gives α_V = (11.2±0.4)×10⁻⁴ fm³. The NIST CODATA 2022 table gives a₀ = 5.29177210544×10⁴ fm. Their central values give \frac{\alpha_V}{a_0^3}=7.56\times10^{-18}. Thus ordinary static proton polarization is much too small to cancel an ordinary fixed-radius Bohr-scale electron dipole in this benchmark. This is an amplitude ratio, not the size of every nuclear correction to atomic spectroscopy. It is not a prediction that the atomic electron follows a classical Bohr circle. The older versioned polarizability is used solely for reproducibility of an order-of-magnitude comparison, not as a claim of the latest recommended average. Limits of that estimate Do not average R^{-3} over the ideal displayed petal center crossings: the detector map has not been identified as electric charge position, and the point-source/nuclear-dipole approximations fail at nuclear overlap. A proper calculation uses the finite source, spatially varying nuclear response, physical frequency dependence, and the electromagnetic propagator. Near nuclear resonances, static polarizability is insufficient and absorption must be included. Magnetic and spin channels have not been bounded here. If V2 predicts a much stronger response through its extra-dimensional projection, it must derive that enhancement and check it against nuclear response and atomic measurements. The existence of feedback is established within the candidate model; the enhancement and orbit stabilization are not. Reproduction and related nuclear_feedback_checks.py checks the neutral-pair dipole identity, interference algebra, and the versioned fixed-radius numerical ratio, separately from its dimensionless simulations. Nuclear response feedback — reciprocal action and coupled electron–nucleus evolution. Orbit electromagnetic spectrum — why a detector trajectory cannot automatically be used as an electromagnetic point source. Research status — current proof boundaries and correction routes.

title: Nuclear response feedback
summary: A reciprocal electron–nuclear polarization model produces retarded feedback and coupled modes, with energy-checked evolution of circular and petalled preparations.
text: Physical premise (IDWT): There is one infinite-dimensional physical manifold. All sectors form one nested chain of submanifolds within it. Summary: A reciprocal electron–nuclear polarization model produces retarded feedback and coupled modes, with energy-checked evolution of circular and petalled preparations. Scope and missing physical input This is a possible feedback extension of the already existing orbit-plus-precession construction, not the origin of its petals. The unperturbed h₀ below already supplies the selected exchange and clock; the induced response perturbs that prescribed motion. These calculations do not derive the precession lock from Coulomb binding or establish that nuclear feedback is necessary for it. In particular, this electric-dipole model does not calculate induced magnetic feedback; that requires a magnetic/current response and its reciprocal coupling. This extends the actual-orbit coefficient dynamics with a responding nuclear electric dipole. It is a semiclassical mean-field model: c describes the electron's section amplitudes and p a collective nuclear polarization. It is not a microscopic proton calculation or a replacement by stationary orbitals. Magnetic/spin response, nuclear recoil, and radiative damping need distinct terms; the recoil and combined-source issues are treated separately. The nucleus responds to the electron's local electric field, not necessarily to its far-field dipole. Let F_i be the Hermitian matrix for that local field in the full retained electron section space, so E_{e,i} = c†F_i c. Once the physical observer charge matrix R(x) is known, a quasistatic nonoverlapping source would give F_i=\frac1{4\pi\epsilon_0}\int R(x)\frac{(R_N-x)_i}{|R_N-x|^3}\,d^3x. Finite nuclear size and overlapping charge require a regularized source calculation. Retardation requires the electromagnetic Green function and current, not this instantaneous Coulomb expression. The V2 current map still has to determine F_i; it cannot generally be inferred from a dipole matrix D_i alone. For the explicit diagnostic below we assume one channel F = κD and leave κ uncalibrated. One reciprocal action For one nuclear electric-polarization component, choose strength s_N > 0 and frequency Ω_N > 0. Its static polarizability is α_N(0) = s_N/Ω_N². With c†c = 1, the action is S=\int dt\left[i\hbar c^\dagger\dot c-c^\dagger h_0c +\frac{\dot p^2-\Omega_N^2p^2}{2s_N}+p\,c^\dagger Fc\right]. Both equations follow from the same interaction: i\hbar\dot c=(h_0-pF)c,\qquad \ddot p+\Omega_N^2p=s_Nc^\dagger Fc. Thus the nucleus is driven by the electron, while its induced dipole enters the electron Hamiltonian as −pF. Keeping only the first effect would not be a backreaction model. The conserved energy is E=c^\dagger h_0c+\frac{\dot p^2+\Omega_N^2p^2}{2s_N} -p\,c^\dagger Fc. In the static mean-field limit, minimizing over p gives p = α_N(0)⟨F⟩ and energy shift −α_N(0)⟨F⟩²/2. The factor one half is required because energy is stored in the polarized nucleus. This is not the operator shift −α_N(0)F²/2 obtained in a suitable fast, quantized oscillator elimination: electron–nuclear correlations and fluctuations distinguish that quantum treatment from the present mean-field model. Adding an internal damping term γ_N ṗ with γ_N ≥ 0 gives Ė = −γ_N ṗ²/s_N. Nuclear polarization does not provide an inexhaustible energy supply. This phenomenological damping is not the coherent radiation reaction of the complete atom, which must be derived from the combined source. Induced charge and current A nuclear polarization density P_N(x,t) = p(t)G_N(x−R_N) along the selected axis, with a normalized centered finite profile G_N, supplies ρ_pol = −∇·P_N and j_pol = ∂_tP_N. These satisfy continuity identically and carry zero net charge but dipole p. For a moving R_N, differentiating the full translated profile includes its motion. The nuclear net charge and center-of-mass current are additional sources, not part of this zero-net-charge polarization term. A magnetic response would add ∇×M_N to the current and require its own response function. Retarded response and return field With e^{-iωt} convention, the nuclear susceptibility is \alpha_N(\omega)=\frac{s_N}{\Omega_N^2-\omega^2-i\gamma_N\omega}. For positive ω and nonnegative damping its imaginary part is nonnegative. A harmonic local field F_ω deposits average power ω Im(α_N)|F_ω|²/2 in this damped oscillator. Resonant enhancement therefore cannot be considered without phase, absorption, and backreaction. On the unperturbed actual orbit, the electron's response to −pF is \chi_{FF}(t,s)=\frac{i}{\hbar}c_0^\dagger[F(t),F(s)]c_0, \qquad \delta\langle F\rangle=\chi_{FF}*p. Here the star denotes the causal time integral. Hence p = α_N*(F₀+χ_FF*p). The companion expression δd_i = χ_{D_iF}*p gives the change in the electron's measured dipole. For a nonstationary orbit these are generally two-time kernels. A scalar frequency denominator is justified only for a time-translation-invariant channel, a justified orbit-phase average, or a Floquet generalization. In the scalar stationary channel F = κD, write the electron susceptibility as χ_e. Solving the two response equations gives p=\frac{\alpha_N\kappa}{1-\alpha_N\kappa^2\chi_e}\,d_0, \qquad d_{\rm total}=\frac{1+\alpha_N\kappa}{1-\alpha_N\kappa^2\chi_e}\,d_0. The denominator determines feedback and coupled poles. The numerator determines electron–nucleus electric-dipole interference. They are distinct: changing κ to −κ leaves the feedback denominator unchanged but changes the radiation amplitude. Any use of this formula also needs the physical conversion between local field and dipole represented by κ. Coupled frequencies and stability are calculable, not automatic For a positive-response oscillator approximation χ_e = s_e/(Ω_e²−ω²), s_e > 0, and zero damping, the coupled frequencies obey \omega_\pm^2=\frac{\Omega_e^2+\Omega_N^2 \pm\sqrt{(\Omega_e^2-\Omega_N^2)^2+4\kappa^2s_es_N}}2. Both squared frequencies are positive precisely when κ²s_es_N < Ω_e²Ω_N². Near resonance the modes mix; at stronger coupling this particular quadratic model becomes unstable. Conservative mode mixing does not by itself attract preparations into a preferred locked orbit. The previously calculated electron response can have either sign depending on its prepared occupations, so positivity of s_e must not be assumed for every orbit channel. Direct reciprocal evolution on the actual section model The executable diagnostic uses the full section spaces at L = 1, 2, 3, not just the four initially occupied modes. Its h₀ = ℏνĜ_L and D = (T_34+T_43)/2 in chosen dipole units are the earlier geometric candidate. It also initializes the three-state ring embedded at degree 2. No field frequencies are fitted to experimental lines. Illustrative dimensionless parameters are ℏ = ν = 1, Ω_N = 1.3, s_N = 0.8, κ = ±0.7, γ_N = 0. The initial polarization and its velocity are zero. These parameters are deliberately visible-response test values, not estimates of the proton's response. Evolution runs to t = 20. The integrator alternates exact half-steps of the free electron/nucleus flow and an exact coupling step. During the latter p is fixed and ⟨F⟩ is conserved, so c → exp(iΔt pF/ℏ)c and ṗ → ṗ+s_NΔt⟨F⟩. This preserves coefficient norm; the second-order splitting's energy error is checked by halving the step from 0.02 to 0.01. preparation maximum nuclear dipole magnitude final 1−fidelity to unforced orbit maximum energy error two petals 0.102915 0.0003331 5.2×10⁻⁸ four petals 0.122709 0.0016087 7.4×10⁻⁸ six petals 0.129525 0.0023806 8.3×10⁻⁸ ring embedded at degree 2 0.122709 0.0016087 7.4×10⁻⁸ The degree-2 ring and four-petal preparations give the same active clock response for this particular single-channel probe; it does not distinguish their spectator amplitude occupations. That is a property of the chosen coupling, not an identification of their actual orbits. Changing κ's sign gives the same evolved electron state and opposite nuclear dipole. Postprocessing the combined dipole acceleration changes the radiation diagnostic, as expected. Both signs give nonzero radiation diagnostics in these transient runs; no cancellation or attracting stable atom is found. Radiation is not fed back into this conservative integrator, so its excellent energy conservation must not be presented as proof of radiative stability. Outcome This provides a reciprocal, energy-audited electric-polarization feedback model. It can shift and mix modes and change the combined radiation. Whether it selects V2's observed orbit families depends on the actual nuclear susceptibility, local-field matrices, and radiation reaction. The companion benchmark tests the scale of ordinary proton polarization without claiming it bounds every multidimensional source map. Reproduction and related nuclear_feedback_checks.py checks the feedback algebra, passive nuclear response, coupled-mode threshold, four orbit integrations, norm/energy convergence, sign reversal, and total-dipole diagnostics. No microscopic nuclear response is derived by these tests. Geometric probe selection — section-space matrices used for the explicit diagnostic. Nuclear radiation benchmark — recoil, source interference, and a sourced proton-scale comparison. Ring section embedding — three-state circular preparation in the degree-2 carrier. Research status — current proof boundaries and correction routes.

title: Nuclear stability test
summary: Coherent radiation and passivity impose a precise dark-mode condition for persistent dipole motion, while the ordinary proton benchmark falls far short of cancellation.
text: Physical premise (IDWT): There is one infinite-dimensional physical manifold. All sectors form one nested chain of submanifolds within it. Particle depth counts ordinary, literal macroscopic spatial dimensions. “Observed” and “unobserved” describe an observer's access to those dimensions, not different kinds of physical dimension. Summary: Coherent radiation and passivity impose a precise dark-mode condition for persistent dipole motion, while the ordinary proton benchmark falls far short of cancellation. Question and present verdict This is a conditional radiation/polarization test, not a test of whether precession can produce petals: the visualization already contains that construction. It also does not evaluate induced nuclear magnetic feedback. Its dipole cancellation conditions must not be promoted to necessary conditions for every physical realization of the 6D precessing orbit. Can the induced nuclear response stabilize V2's actual electron orbits? The preceding simulations demonstrated feedback but did not establish this. This note adds coherent electric-dipole radiation to the harmonic response equations and tests necessary conditions for persistent passive motion. It is not a fully nonlinear Maxwell–Dirac–nucleus solution. The ordinary, low-frequency, fixed-Bohr-radius proton-polarization mechanism is too weak to cancel that benchmark electron dipole. A nonradiating coupled mode is mathematically possible in the ideal two-dipole model, but requires specific matching and absence of loss. Existing V2 equations have not selected those conditions or supplied the physical local-field matrix and nuclear susceptibility. Thus this is a conditional exclusion plus an exact target for the remaining calculation, not a general no-go for 6D orbits. Periodic motion must pass an energy test For a passive isolated system with no incident power, Poynting balance gives \Delta E_{\rm recoverable} =-\int_0^T(P_{\rm outward}+P_{\rm internal\ loss})\,dt. Take a sphere surrounding the source in the radiation zone and a complete period, so periodically stored near-field energy returns to its original value. A genuinely periodic state with the same stored energy after T requires zero average outgoing radiation and zero irreversible internal loss. Nuclear feedback can exchange energy within the system, but cannot replace energy escaping to infinity indefinitely. A metastable orbit with slow decay is a different target; it needs a calculated lifetime. This argument does not forbid a moving multidimensional state whose physical electromagnetic source is nonradiating. It also does not apply classical moving-charge radiation to a stationary quantum atomic source. The physical current, rather than the visual outline, is what matters. Coherent radiative response Use one spatial dipole channel with electron dipole d and nuclear dipole p, and time dependence Re[(d,p)e^{-iωt}]. For a passive two-oscillator diagnostic, let s_e,s_N > 0, bare frequencies Ω_e,Ω_N, real reciprocal coupling κ, and internal damping γ_e,γ_N ≥ 0. Neither susceptibility here already includes radiative damping. To leading electric-dipole order, both sources radiate through d+p. Define r_rad = 1/(6πε₀c³). The inverse response is M(\omega)= \begin{pmatrix} (\Omega_e^2-\omega^2-i\gamma_e\omega)/s_e&-\kappa\\ -\kappa&(\Omega_N^2-\omega^2-i\gamma_N\omega)/s_N \end{pmatrix} -ir_{\rm rad}\omega^3 \begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}. The last term is the common dipole radiation field, not two independent radiative damping terms. It retains electron–nucleus interference. This frequency-domain test avoids integrating an unregularized third-derivative radiation-reaction equation with runaway solutions. Finite spatial phase, higher multipoles, and the full causal high-frequency response are outside this leading-order model. For v = (d,p), direct multiplication gives -\operatorname{Im}(v^\dagger Mv) =r_{\rm rad}\omega^3|d+p|^2 +\frac{\gamma_e\omega}{s_e}|d|^2 +\frac{\gamma_N\omega}{s_N}|p|^2. Multiplication by ω/2 yields the time-averaged radiated and absorbed power. The radiation normalization agrees with the dipole-power derivation in UT Austin's radiation notes. Every term is nonnegative for positive ω. Therefore a real-frequency source-free mode Mv = 0 must have d+p = 0 and no internal loss in either occupied component. If γ_N > 0, a nonzero nuclear cancellation dipole cannot give an exactly persistent passive mode in this model. This positivity calculation is for passive positive-response electron and nuclear oscillators. Some prepared section-space electron responses have population-dependent signs; those require their full dynamical treatment. The isolated-system energy requirement remains applicable without assuming an equilibrium susceptibility. An exact dark-mode condition Set γ_e = γ_N = 0 and p = −d ≠ 0. The remaining real equations require \omega_d^2=\Omega_e^2+\kappa s_e =\Omega_N^2+\kappa s_N>0. Equivalently, Ω_e²−Ω_N²+κ(s_e−s_N) = 0. A positive-definite conservative energy and this matching condition admit a dipole-dark normal mode. The diagnostic constructs one explicitly, then shows that changing a frequency or adding nuclear absorption destroys that exact dark solution. This proves mathematical possibility, not physical selection or attraction. Even a perfect dipole-dark mode can radiate through omitted multipoles. It is not automatically the prepared petalled trajectory. Every actual nonzero source harmonic and radiation channel must pass the corresponding test; petal count alone does not tell us which electromagnetic harmonics are present. For constant κ and a single lossless Lorentz nuclear response, the driven cancellation equation 1+κ α_N(ω) = 0 has at most one positive squared frequency. Arbitrary multi-harmonic cancellation is not automatic. How far the ordinary proton benchmark is from cancellation For the previously derived fixed-radius electrostatic geometry, κ = −1/(4πε₀R³), and α_N(0) = 4πε₀α_V. Cancellation requires an induced dipole comparable to the electron dipole, hence |κ α_N(ω)| approximately 1 with the correct phase. The versioned benchmark has η = α_V/a₀³ = 7.56×10⁻¹⁸. Relative to its static response, this requires an enhancement of approximately 1.32×10¹⁷. The inputs are the PDG 2024 proton polarizability and CODATA 2022 Bohr radius, as documented in the companion benchmark. This is not a bound on all nuclear corrections to spectroscopy or on an unspecified V2 projection. In the one-pole nuclear model, normalized cancellation amplitude is \frac{d+p}{d}=1-\frac{\eta} {1-\omega^2/\Omega_N^2-i\gamma_N\omega/\Omega_N^2} when electron backreaction is temporarily excluded solely to test the required nuclear amplitude and phase. For zero damping it vanishes at 1−ω²/Ω_N² = η, or relative detuning (Ω_N−ω)/Ω_N ≈ 3.78×10⁻¹⁸. For small residual amplitude, γ_Nω/Ω_N² must be much smaller than η as well. At the same real detuning with imaginary part equal to η, the residual amplitude is 1/√2, not near zero. The exact source-free mode must additionally satisfy the coupled matching condition above; a zero of the driven amplitude alone is insufficient. These numbers do not propose an actual ultra-narrow nuclear resonance. They quantify what would be required to rescue this particular benchmark using the assumed one-pole response. Ordinary proton Compton measurements constrain its electric and magnetic polarizabilities; an independently measured example is the MAMI result. No matching atomic-frequency nuclear response has been derived here. Replacing the ordinary response with a resonant or multidimensional one without deriving its spectrum would merely introduce the desired answer as a parameter. What is now determined, and what is not Determined: mere induction does not establish stability; coherent radiation and internal absorption give explicit loss conditions; the two-dipole model has a sharply specified exceptional dark mode; the ordinary static proton benchmark misses the required cancellation amplitude by about 17 orders of magnitude. The prior conservative feedback simulations cannot be cited as evidence for radiative stabilization. Not determined: whether V2's actual projected source, nuclear spectrum, magnetic response, and full coupled field dynamics produce a nonradiating or sufficiently long-lived bound orbit. The current project leaves those physical quantities unspecified. This cannot be decided uniquely by further tuning the illustrative oscillator. The next substantive task is to derive the local-field/current map and nuclear response from the proposed action, or identify a measured response with the same physical coupling. Reproduction and related nuclear_stability_checks.py verifies the coherent loss identity on complex amplitudes, the tuned dark mode and its failure under absorption/mismatch, and the single-frequency cancellation condition. High-precision arithmetic resolves the small benchmark detuning. It does not claim a complete radiative time evolution or a V2 stability proof. The diagnostic uses explicit runtime checks that remain active under Python optimization. It reports 88 executed numerical evaluations across ten named conditions, plus the measured loss-identity residual, not a bare PASS label. An in-memory mutation reversing the response matrix's dissipative sign failed at the loss-identity check with exit status 1 under both normal and optimized Python. The correct script also runs its checks under optimization. This verifies that the checks can reject that error, not that they exhaust all possible errors. Constructed matching examples and algebraic identities remain internal model-consistency tests, not independent physical evidence. Nuclear response feedback — reciprocal dynamics whose earlier simulations excluded radiative feedback. Nuclear radiation benchmark — source geometry, recoil, and versioned numerical inputs. Research status — current proof boundaries and correction routes.

title: Orbit current projection
summary: A conserved electromagnetic source requires a specified current projection, not identification with the detector-averaged orbit image.
text: Physical premise (IDWT): There is one infinite-dimensional physical manifold. All sectors form one nested chain of submanifolds within it. Particle depth counts ordinary, literal macroscopic spatial dimensions. “Observed” and “unobserved” describe an observer's access to those dimensions, not different kinds of physical dimension. See spatial meaning and mathematical scope. Summary: A conserved electromagnetic source requires a specified current projection, not identification with the detector-averaged orbit image. Scope This starts the electromagnetic test of the actual multidimensional orbits in the demo, including the circle and two-, four-, and six-petal cases. It does not replace them with stationary orbitals. The coefficient ray [c], the sector point [Z], and the Dirac field on physical space remain distinct until a physical bridge is specified. Bound within, free without, section 8, already proposes a fibre-integrated electron current coupled to the photon. Higher-dimensional polarization, sections 3 and 6, adds the invariant representation filter. These specify a route to a vertex, not the numerical source produced by a particular c(t). The depth-two photon sector must also be related to the electromagnetic field seen by an ordinary spatial observer; its spatial depth is not a license to replace ordinary Maxwell propagation by a two-space-dimensional wave equation. Conserved pushforward Let a density n and tangent current J on a fixed sector manifold Q obey ∂t n + div_Q J = 0. Assume no boundary flux, or sufficient decay, and a smooth physical charge readout X_t: Q → R³. This is a conditional source construction, not an identification of X_t with the demo's apparatus map. For charge e* (negative for an electron), define distributions \rho(t,x)=e_*\int_Q n(t,u)\delta^{(3)}(x-X_t(u))\,d\mu(u), j(t,x)=e_*\int_Q \left[dX_t(J)(t,u)+n(t,u)\partial_tX_t(u)\right] \delta^{(3)}(x-X_t(u))\,d\mu(u). For every compactly supported smooth test function f, integration by parts gives \frac{d}{dt}\int\rho f\,d^3x =e_*\int_Q\left[J\cdot d(f\circ X_t) +n\nabla f(X_t)\cdot\partial_tX_t\right]d\mu =\int j\cdot\nabla f\,d^3x. Thus ∂tρ + ∇·j = 0, with total charge e*∫n. The term involving ∂_tX_t is required for a moving readout/frame. This proof allows many-to-one maps; it needs neither an inverse map nor a choice of one point on each fibre. Gauge invariance of ∫(j·A − ρφ) dt d³x follows, up to boundary terms, from this continuity equation. Gauge invariance alone does not select X_t. For a point trajectory U(t) with n = δ_U and J = U̇δ_U, these equations reduce to ρ = e_*δ(x−Γ(t)), j = e_*Γ̇δ(x−Γ(t)), where Γ = X_t(U(t)). This is precisely the extra assumption needed before a displayed curve can be treated as a moving electromagnetic point charge. An invariant polarization filter acting on a spinor current needs its own covariant conservation check. Arbitrarily deleting current components does not inherit this proof. A concrete projected action must provide the conserved source, its normalization, and its observer-space interpretation. Why the exposure image is insufficient The demo's registration density is a full-period average of G_σ(x−Γ(t)). Its being stationary does not make the instantaneous source stationary. For a fixed normalized centered spatial kernel, the conditional source ρ = e_*G_σ(x−Γ), j = e_*Γ̇G_σ(x−Γ) conserves charge, but still has electric dipole d(t) = e_*Γ(t). Spatial broadening alone does not smooth that dipole's time dependence. A physical frequency-dependent form factor can affect high-frequency radiation; that is additional source physics, not a consequence of plotting a blurred exposure. A complete-period average of a periodic conserved source has divergence-free mean current. It discards nonzero time harmonics. Computing radiated power from that mean is not computing the mean power of the original source. Calculation to close Derive the charged projected action and its current; evaluate it on the actual bound orbit; push it to the physical electromagnetic observer with its polarization filter; then compute its multipoles and response to a probe. The source must include the nucleus and any compensating field contribution, not only the electron, when testing a complete bound system. The follow-up spectrum test gives explicit constraints for several orbit shapes and separates a literal point-source assignment from a fixed bilinear current assignment. Neither assignment is selected by the current V2 text. Related Orbit electromagnetic spectrum — applies this distinction to the circle, petalled orbits, and detuned cases. title: Orbit electromagnetic spectrum
summary: Circle, petalled, and detuned actual orbits give distinct conditional radiation diagnostics and finite-generator constraints on electromagnetic probes.
text: Physical premise (IDWT): There is one infinite-dimensional physical manifold. All sectors form one nested chain of submanifolds within it. Summary: Circle, petalled, and detuned actual orbits give distinct conditional radiation diagnostics and finite-generator constraints on electromagnetic probes. Two explicit source hypotheses The current projection audit identifies a missing physical map, not a reason to stop calculating. Here we test two conditional assignments, without claiming either follows from V2: The displayed trajectory is the electromagnetic point-charge position. The current is bilinear in a fixed linear field lift of the coefficient vector c, so its dipole is c†D_i c for fixed Hermitian matrices D_i. These hypotheses generally disagree. Their predictions are diagnostics for the missing coupling, not two interchangeable descriptions of the same source. The actual orbit family is retained throughout; no stationary orbital model is substituted. Literal point-source assignment: ideal petals Use aligned planar readout, θ = νt, fixed nucleus at the origin, fixed R, and the same ν across cases. For L ≥ 1, z(\theta)=\Gamma_x+i\Gamma_y=R|\cos L\theta|e^{i\theta}. The circle is the separate ring sector z = Re^{iθ}. This comparison is not a claim that different physical atomic states have equal radii or clocks. For ordinary nonrelativistic electromagnetic point sources, or the long-wavelength electric-dipole approximation to an extended source, \langle P\rangle=\frac{\langle|\ddot d|^2\rangle}{6\pi\epsilon_0c^3}, \qquad P_{\rm circle}=\frac{e_*^2R^2\nu^4}{6\pi\epsilon_0c^3}. The external electromagnetic formula and its assumptions are derived in UT Austin's dipole-radiation notes, equation 15. All orbit substitutions and spectral results below are calculations here. This is a classical source test, not a quantum spontaneous-emission formula or a derivation of V2's electromagnetic field equations. The exact Fourier expansion is \frac zR=\frac2\pi e^{i\theta} +\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}a_n \left[e^{i(1+2nL)\theta}+e^{i(1-2nL)\theta}\right], \qquad a_n=\frac{2(-1)^{n+1}}{\pi(4n^2-1)}. Both senses of rotation contribute to the planar acceleration norm. With the first N sideband pairs retained, Parseval gives \frac{P_N}{P_{\rm circle}}=\frac4{\pi^2} +\sum_{n=1}^{N}a_n^2 \left[(1+2nL)^4+(1-2nL)^4\right]. Each summand tends to 8L⁴/π², not zero. The formal sum diverges. Equivalently, at each center crossing the one-sided velocity jump has magnitude 2RLν; the raw displayed curve has no square-integrable acceleration. Therefore it cannot be inserted unregularized into a finite-power point-charge calculation. This excludes that unregularized source prescription, not the smooth 6D coefficient orbit. The absolute-value observer readout creates the cusp. For an extended source the dipole approximation cannot be extended to arbitrarily high frequencies; the divergence is not a calculated infinite physical power for V2. The source's form factor and temporal regularity must be specified before taking that limit. Detuned multi-maximum cases For the exchange perturbation, put a = Ω/ν and m = (g/Ω)². Then z/R=r(\theta)e^{i\theta},\qquad r=\sqrt{1-m\sin^2(a\theta)}, r'=-\frac{ma\sin2a\theta}{2r},\qquad r''=-\frac{ma^2\cos2a\theta}{r} -\frac{m^2a^2\sin^22a\theta}{4r^3}, \frac{\langle P\rangle}{P_{\rm circle}} =\left\langle(r''-r)^2+4(r')^2\right\rangle. Nonzero detuning gives m < 1 and smooth bounded acceleration. Choose the demo's +1-maximum alignments g/ν = L, a = L + 1/2, δ/ν = √(L+1/4): starting ideal case detuned maxima per clock turn δ/ν conditional planar P/P_circle circle, separate sector no radial modulation — 1 two petals, L = 1 3 1.11803399 1.88272246 four petals, L = 2 5 1.50000000 16.80500000 six petals, L = 3 7 1.80277564 85.88942381 The detuned images close in one clock turn; their full coefficient rays need two turns when ε = 0. The numbers use quadrature independently checked against Fourier acceleration and a coarser grid. They are not measured atomic emission rates. With a nonzero depth readout Γ_z, its squared acceleration adds to the planar result if it is also identified as physical charge position. No nuclear recoil or radiation reaction is included. Detuning removes the cusp but does not supply a nonradiating bound state. Fixed bilinear source: an exact frequency constraint Suppose a time-independent linear lift ψ(u,t) = Σ_a c_a(t)s_a(u) into an admissible Dirac field on physical space bundle has actually been supplied. Fibre integration, a fixed linear polarization filter, and the dipole integral then turn a bilinear current into d_i(t) = c(t)†D_i c(t). This does not identify s_a with homogeneous coordinates or bypass the spatial spinor-bundle obstruction. If i ċ = Hc and H has frequency eigenvalues λ_a, direct expansion gives d_i(t)=\sum_{a,b}c_a(0)^*c_b(0)(D_i)_{ab} e^{i(\lambda_a-\lambda_b)t} in its eigenbasis. Only occupied eigenvalue differences can occur. For the ideal four-state orbit the eigenvalues, modulo a common shift, are ν{L,−L,−1,0}. In particular, the six-petal four-state truncation permits 6ν but not 5ν in such a dipole. These are unforced signal bounds within the stated truncation, not general absorption bounds. A subsequent geometric probe calculation shows that an exactly retained unforced orbit can respond through omitted section modes. The infinite harmonic tail of the displayed petalled position cannot equal any fixed bilinear dipole within this finite model. This remains true for the noncircular detuned square-root readout, which also has infinitely many harmonics (or sidebands for incommensurate Ω/ν). For general detuning and relative phase, replace the eigenvalues by {ε+Ω, ε−Ω, −ν, 0}. Thus ε, though invisible to every displayed coordinate, shifts cross-block probe frequencies whenever the appropriate D_i elements are nonzero. A photon probe could distinguish identical-looking orbits; whether it does depends on the derived vertex. This is a concrete target for the next physical calculation, not evidence of an observed splitting. The constraint assumes a fixed finite linear lift and fixed bilinear source. A nonlinear field bridge, time-dependent projector, additional occupied modes, or self-consistent field dynamics needs a new calculation. Arbitrary smooth replacement of the detector map is not a derivation of D_i. Weak-field response along an actual orbit Take the preparation time as t₀ = 0. For energy Hamiltonian ℏH and perturbation −Σ_j E_j(t)D_j, define D_i(t) = e^{iHt}D_i e^{-iHt}. Linearizing the evolution gives \delta d_i(t)=\sum_j\int_{t_0}^{t}\chi_{ij}(t,s)E_j(s)\,ds, \qquad \chi_{ij}(t,s)=\frac{i}{\hbar} c_0^\dagger[D_i(t),D_j(s)]c_0. The diagnostic checks this sign and normalization in units ℏ = 1 against an exact small impulse, including detuning and an invisible relative phase. An orbit preparation is generally not stationary, so this is a two-time response, not automatically a function of t−s. Averaging over unknown initial orbit phase must be justified by the preparation. Net absorption, linewidths, and radiative stability need the physical D_i, coupling to field modes, and backreaction; an arbitrary random test matrix supplies none of these. Outcome and reproduction The circle alone misses both the readout cusp and the finite-spectrum incompatibility.
