The continuation acceptance gate now requires a complete finite integration, fixed Casimirs, and independently refined closure before saving a checkpoint. Reduced recurrence problem The exact completed-Coulomb L=3 orbit occupies only coordinates (q_0,q_1,q_3,q_4) and the corresponding 4\times4 skew-source block. This sector remains invariant under both the full-4D Coulomb potential and the finite cylindrical potential supported on (q_0,q_1). Reducing to it leaves four positions, four momenta, six skew components, and the period. The shooting residual contains full-state recurrence, the phase condition q_1(0)=0, and the family condition q_0(0)=1. Fixed energy is another legitimate family constraint; it was not mathematically inappropriate. Neither constraint guarantees that the desired family exists. The section q_1(0)=0 is not by itself a radial turning-point condition. At homotopy h=0, the exact orbit has T=20.99780573,\qquad \|X(T)-X(0)\|=1.86\times10^{-12}. Thus the reduced dynamics and recurrence equations reproduce the analytic start. Why ordinary continuation stalled For V_h=(1-h)(-1/|q|)+hV_{r_N}(|q_{\rm vis}|),\qquad r_N=0.3, ordinary least-squares steps of h=0.05 and 0.005 stagnated with recurrence residuals 0.459 and 0.151 respectively. These are rejected numerical shoots, not evidence that a cylindrical periodic orbit does not exist. The Jacobian at the exact start is rank deficient, with symmetry and source-invariant structure. Not every unresolved direction has been proved to be a removable gauge direction. Ordinary whole-orbit finite differences misleadingly reported ranks from 8 to 12. This has now been replaced by local complex-step differentiation and simultaneous integration of the 14\times14 fundamental matrix. The local Jacobian agrees with an independent centered derivative to 5.53\times10^{-11}. The analytic shooting Jacobian has exactly eight resolved singular values, (94.7368,14.6897,5.94203,5.87715,1.37876,0.928496,0.838421,0.197030), with the other seven at 1.5\times10^{-12} or below. A separately integrated parameter-sensitivity equation gives kernel forcing norm 52.5150. Its component outside the resolved Jacobian range is only 2.70\times10^{-8}, and the minimum-norm tangent has norm 6.20934. Therefore there is no resolved first-order obstruction to continuing the petal orbit toward the cylindrical kernel. The h=10^{-4} tangent predictor has recurrence residual 8.59\times10^{-6}. Truncating newly split soft singular values rather than inverting them gives rank-aware correction residuals 4.87\times10^{-7} and 2.23\times10^{-7}. The corrected period is 20.99091657. These are the original, unrefined shooting diagnostics. They do not establish a periodic micro-branch or continuation to the fully cylindrical endpoint h=1. The unconstrained correction changes the source's quadratic and Pfaffian Casimirs by 2.19\times10^{-3} and 1.08\times10^{-3}. Continuing those values freely is mathematically allowed across a family of source orbits, but is not appropriate if V2 fixes the electron's source coadjoint orbit. Adding both Casimirs raises the resolved shooting rank from 8 to 10. Its analytic first-order equation is still solvable to 2.70\times10^{-8}, with tangent norm 7.32359, so fixed source invariants present no first-order obstruction. The first attempt to impose the Casimirs as extra residuals stalled at 4.49\times10^{-6}. The corrected formulation instead uses \mathfrak{so}(4)\cong\mathfrak{so}(3)_+\oplus\mathfrak{so}(3)_- and parameterizes the fixed coadjoint orbit as the product of the two spheres with the original self-dual and anti-self-dual radii. This removes both Casimir-normal directions identically. The chart reconstructs the initial source to 2.78\times10^{-17} and gives a rank-8-of-13 shooting Jacobian. At h=10^{-4}, rank-aware correction reduces the recurrence residual from 1.37\times10^{-5} to 2.44\times10^{-7}, with T=20.99128584 and maximum Casimir error 1.78\times10^{-15}. The Casimir parameterization is valid, but this unrefined closure estimate does not certify continuation. Continuation with the previous residual included in each predictor originally reported the following unrefined values, retained as a diagnostic record: h period T recurrence residual maximum Casimir error 1\times10^{-4} 20.99128584 2.44\times10^{-7} 1.78\times10^{-15} 2\times10^{-4} 20.98482005 1.75\times10^{-7} 0 4\times10^{-4} 20.97204284 2.01\times10^{-7} 4.44\times10^{-16} 8\times10^{-4} 20.94710312 3.94\times10^{-7} 0 1.6\times10^{-3} 20.89958488 6.03\times10^{-7} 0 3.2\times10^{-3} 20.81331458 6.31\times10^{-7} 8.88\times10^{-16} 6.4\times10^{-3} 20.67292125 4.25\times10^{-7} 8.88\times10^{-16} 9.6\times10^{-3} 20.56750468 2.49\times10^{-7} 4.44\times10^{-16} 1.28\times10^{-2} 20.48965107 5.24\times10^{-7} 4.44\times10^{-16} The optimizer reached h=0.0128 using an intermediate h=0.0096 candidate, but the independent check above rejects its accuracy. Neither an accepted 1.28% continuation branch nor a branch termination follows. First-order solvability at a rank-deficient start also does not, alone, imply nonlinear continuation. Required continuation method First correct candidates using integration accuracy independently adequate for the desired closure tolerance. Pseudo-arclength continuation is a candidate improvement, not a guaranteed remedy. Multiple-shooting nodes can be placed at the six cylindrical-support encounters, where the profile changes curvature most rapidly. The existing fixed SO(4) source chart already uses self-dual and anti-self-dual two-spheres and removes the two Casimir-normal directions. Time phase, amplitude/arclength, and the remaining visible/unobserved rotation gauges must also be fixed explicitly. title: Dimensional magnetic kernel comparison
summary: The constrained magnetic kernel distinguishes five-dimensional null-axis polarization from six-dimensional complex-structure polarization, while the scalar-exchange bridge explicitly supplies a five-dimensional vector-channel escape route.
text: Physical premise (IDWT): There is one infinite-dimensional physical manifold. All sectors form one nested chain of submanifolds within it. Particle depth counts ordinary, literal macroscopic spatial dimensions. “Observed” and “unobserved” describe an observer's access to those dimensions, not different kinds of physical dimension. See spatial meaning and mathematical scope. Summary: The constrained magnetic kernel distinguishes five-dimensional null-axis polarization from six-dimensional complex-structure polarization, while the scalar-exchange bridge explicitly supplies a five-dimensional vector-channel escape route. Same kernel, different spinor moments Use the existing magnetic bridge: a fixed square-integrable density envelope, one uniform pure polarization, positive magnetic cost, and the leading Pauli coupling. At nonzero Fourier wavevector k, the closed-field projector on skew matrices is \mathcal P_kJ=P_kJ+JP_k,\qquad P_k=\frac{kk^T}{|k|^2}. This formula is valid in either ambient dimension. Its amplitude-space rank is d-1 and its isotropic angular average is (2/d)I on bivectors. In particular the average factor is 2/5 in five dimensions and 1/3 in six. An average projector factor is not itself a particle-depth measurement. With \|J\|^2=-\operatorname{tr}(J^2)/2, \|\mathcal P_kJ\|^2=\frac{|Jk|^2}{|k|^2}. The selected moments derived from the explicit spinors obey J_5^2=-I_5+nn^T,\quad |n|=1, \qquad J_6^2=-I_6. Therefore their directional response strengths are \|\mathcal P_kJ_5\|^2=1-(n\cdot\widehat k)^2, \qquad \|\mathcal P_kJ_6\|^2=1. There is a genuine zero-response direction in five dimensions. No rescaling of the coupling removes it. More generally every skew matrix in an odd-dimensional real space is singular, since \det J=\det(-J)=(-1)^d\det J. Thus a nonzero isotropic response for every wavevector at one fixed polarization is impossible for any odd-dimensional bivector in this kernel. Four-dimensional invertible skew matrices exist, so this parity result alone does not establish exactly six. Envelope anisotropy changes the minimum family differently Write f(k)=|\widetilde n(k)|^2\geq0 for the prescribed envelope weight, using a consistent Fourier convention, and define W=\int f(k)\,dk,\qquad T=\int f(k)\widehat k\widehat k^T\,dk,\qquad\operatorname{tr}T=W. After constrained field minimization, the polarization energies are E_5(z)=-\frac{g^2}{2Z_B}\left(W-n(z)^TTn(z)\right), \qquad E_6(z)=-\frac{g^2}{2Z_B}W. For an isotropic five-dimensional envelope, T=(W/5)I_5, the whole CP3 polarization family still minimizes and the magnitude is (4/5)g^2W/(2Z_B). For a generic anisotropic envelope with a simple lowest eigenvalue, n instead aligns with either sign of its lowest-eigenvalue axis. For any unit n, the condition \gamma(n)z=z defines a complex two-dimensional eigenspace, and its normalized rays form CP1. The explicit spinor identity gives precisely these rays the prescribed n. Hence a simple lowest envelope eigenvalue leaves two CP1 minimum families, one over each sign of the selected axis, not the full CP3. At either family, four ray directions acquire positive curvature and two remain flat. In six dimensions all six ray directions remain flat under this spin-magnetic energy for any such fixed envelope. If the lowest eigenvalue of T has multiplicity m, its allowed unit vectors form S^{m-1} and each has a CP1 ray fibre. The minimum family therefore has real dimension m+1; this dimension count does not assert that the bundle is globally a product. The m=1 case is the two CP1 components above, and m=5 restores all of CP3. In particular, an envelope respecting a three-visible-plus-two-unobserved split has T=\operatorname{diag}(t_V I_3,t_H I_2), with 3t_V+2t_H=W. If t_H<t_V, the minimum family has dimension three; if t_V<t_H, dimension four; if they are equal, dimension six. This symmetry-respecting comparison is more relevant to a fixed nuclear three-plane than assuming an arbitrary five-distinct-eigenvalue envelope. The corresponding six-dimensional pure-spinor magnetic energy remains ray-independent within the stated uniform-polarization approximation. For T=\operatorname{diag}(2,2,2,1,1)/8, a separate finite-difference check gives ray Hessian (0,0,0,1,1,1) to 4\times10^{-8}, as the dimension count predicts. The fibre argument is explicit: \gamma(n)^2=I and \operatorname{tr}\gamma(n)=0 give a two-complex-dimensional positive eigenspace. A ray in it has n(z)\cdot n=1; the already proved unit norm of n(z) forces n(z)=n. Rotational covariance gives the same smooth two-real-dimensional fibre over every axis. An exact axis-weight quadrature with five-dimensional weights (5,4,3,2,1)/15 yields the ray Hessian eigenvalues \left(0,0,\frac8{15},\frac{16}{15},\frac{24}{15},\frac{32}{15}\right), for energy normalized by g^2/(2Z_B)=1. Numerical derivatives reproduce these values. With six-dimensional weights (6,5,4,3,2,1)/21 every ray Hessian eigenvalue is zero analytically and below 1.2\times10^{-8} in the finite-difference calculation. This is a structural prediction of two competing kernels, not a fit of their coupling constants. The five-dimensional null axis and the envelope are explicit variables; no V1 choice of S5 or CP2 spatial base was used. Relation to the spectral discriminator The spectral comparison assumed an isotropic unrestricted bivector cost. For an isotropic envelope, the integrated magnetic projector merely rescales that coupling, preserving the corresponding gap multiplicities. For an anisotropic envelope the selected field is generally not proportional to J. Consequently the six-dimensional frozen-field excited gaps need not remain triply equal for an anisotropic envelope, even though its joint field-plus-ray minimum family remains CP3. These are different statements. Do not demand the isotropic-source singlet-triplet spectrum of every anisotropic magnetic preparation. The existing scalar-exchange bridge supplies the escape channel The operator-class restriction is substantive in the project's other source proposal. In five dimensions the sixteen Hermitian matrix directions are the identity, five \gamma_a, and ten bivectors H_{ab}, orthogonal with trace norm four. For any Hermitian density matrix \varrho, write N=\operatorname{tr}\varrho,\quad v_a=\operatorname{tr}(\varrho\gamma_a), \quad b_{ab}=\operatorname{tr}(\varrho H_{ab}). Completeness gives 4\operatorname{tr}(\varrho^2)=N^2+|v|^2+|b|^2. The same explicitly assumed Gaussian scalar-exchange reduction used in the scalar bridge therefore becomes E_G=\frac\kappa2\left(N^2-\operatorname{tr}\varrho^2\right) =\frac{3\kappa}{8}N^2-\frac\kappa8\left(|v|^2+|b|^2\right). It supplies both a vector and a bivector channel. Dropping the vector channel would not preserve that exchange identity. For a pure ray, S(b)+v\cdot\gamma=4zz^\dagger-I, exactly the operator that evades the five-dimensional bivector-only spectral no-go. Thus the leading Pauli/magnetic proposal and the full scalar-exchange proposal do not have the same dimension-discrimination power. No spectral exclusion of the full five-dimensional exchange competitor has been proved. The existing exchange caveats—Gaussian closure, statistics, normal ordering, and absence of exact one-particle two-body self-interaction—remain unchanged. Physical scope and next test This calculation tests a concrete part of the response kernel already in the archive. It omits orbital magnetic energy, electric response, radiation, spatial profile relaxation, nonuniform polarization, and the nucleus. Anisotropy should next be generated by the coupled envelope/nucleus solution, rather than chosen only as a diagnostic Fourier weight. The useful discriminant is polarization response to controlled envelope anisotropy, or a preparation-resolved directional magnetic response. Whether the electron exhibits either specified response still needs a derived observable map. The mathematics does not identify an electron from CP3 geometry or an averaged cloud alone. Verification dimensional_magnetic_kernel_checks.py performs 500 runtime checks, including kernel projection, directional responses, envelope minimization, the CP1 family, numerical Hessians, and the mixed-density exchange identity. Evidence: dimensional-magnetic-kernel.json. Related Frozen magnetic texture test — subsequent predeclared test that relaxes uniform polarization while leaving this kernel unchanged. Magnetic bivector master bridge — the same constrained field projector and fixed-envelope approximation. Master scalar exchange bridge — the same Gaussian closure, whose five-dimensional decomposition has an extra channel. Five-dimensional CP3 selection and spectral discrimination — explicit spinor moments and operator-class spectral theorem. Dimensional necessity from response — separates kernel-specific discrimination from general dimensional lower bounds.

title: Dimensional precession test
summary: Six dimensions are minimal for the stated static plane-induced precession mechanism, but a reciprocal 4D model also precesses and an unconstrained nonlinear readout cannot identify particle depth.
text: Physical premise (IDWT): There is one infinite-dimensional physical manifold. All sectors form one nested chain of submanifolds within it. Summary: Six dimensions are minimal for the stated static plane-induced precession mechanism, but a reciprocal 4D model also precesses and an unconstrained nonlinear readout cannot identify particle depth. Question and fair comparison Particle-depth correction: the D=4 carrier used below has sector CP1, not V2's Q4=CP2. V2 also has Q5=S5, which is not excluded by the absence of an odd-dimensional orthogonal complex matrix J. The result below is only about a restricted vector-carrier family. It must not be promoted to a minimum-six V2 particle-depth theorem. The subsequent five-depth comparison tests the actual CP2 and S5 sectors and reproduces the prepared demo trajectory exactly. A lower-dimensional reproduction tests whether a proposed orbit mechanism requires six dimensions. A failed numerical search alone cannot establish that necessity. This note gives an analytic obstruction within a stated model family, then an explicit lower-dimensional counterexample to the broader claim. These are actual geometric trajectories, not stationary orbital densities. No experimental electron trajectory is fitted here. Retain the same nuclear three-plane O, orthogonal complex structure J on the electron's real vector carrier, invariant Hamiltonian rule, isotropic cross-plane response cost, and no additional fixed direction inside O. The response channel is still an effective-model premise in every dimension. Here D is the real dimension of the vector carrier on which J acts. The sector manifold SO(D)/U(D/2) has its own dimension: it is a two-real-dimensional sphere for D=4 and six-real-dimensional CP3 for D=6. Neither the number of complex coefficients nor the response mode count is automatically D. Only the even-D orthogonal-complex family is being compared. A real J with J squared equal to minus the identity cannot exist in odd D, since det(J) squared would equal minus one. A three-plane cannot fit in D=2. This does not rule out alternative 3D or 5D dynamical theories using different state variables. Exact obstruction in four dimensions With a three-plus-one split, write J=\begin{pmatrix}A&u\\-u^T&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad A=[a]_\times. The constraint gives u dot u=1, Au=0, and A squared minus uu^T=-I3. Since A squared=aa^T−|a|² I3, taking traces gives |a|²=1, and substitution gives aa^T=uu^T. Thus a=plus or minus u. The two signs label the two components; select u=a in the explicit checks. The same conclusions hold in the other component. Consequently s=−tr(A squared)/2=1 and ||Q||²=||u||²=1 everywhere. SO(3) rotations inside O act transitively on this sphere. Every smooth scalar energy depending only on J and the unoriented three-plane, invariant under those rotations, is constant on each component. This is stronger than testing a few candidate potentials. In particular, eliminating the same positive-cost response gives E_{\rm eff}^{(4)}=-\frac{\chi g^2}{2},\qquad E_{\rm eff}^{(6)}=-\frac{\chi g^2}{2}(3-2s). The finite singlet-plus-excitation source gives the same contrast: E_-^{(4)}=\frac{\Delta-\sqrt{\Delta^2+4g^2}}2,\qquad E_-^{(6)}=\frac{\Delta-\sqrt{\Delta^2+4g^2(3-2s)}}2. The 4D source has three excited components rather than nine. Its induced response is not zero, but its equilibrium energy cannot distinguish the electron orientations. The static precession flow is zero. In 6D the interior 0<s<1 supports a nonzero flow when the kernel slope is nonzero. The endpoints remain stationary as established in the earlier note. Therefore six is the minimum vector-carrier dimension for this particular static, isotropic, three-plane-induced precession mechanism. It is not a theorem that only six-dimensional particles can precess, nor that D>6 is excluded. Reciprocal four-dimensional precession nevertheless exists Keep the response dynamical instead of eliminating it. Let x and y be three-component canonical response variables, with chi,M,I_e positive: E=\frac{|y|^2}{2M}+\frac{|x|^2}{2\chi}-g x\cdot a,\qquad |a|=1, \dot a=\frac{g}{\mathcal I_e}a\times x,\qquad \dot x=y/M,\qquad \dot y=-x/\chi+ga. The first equation is precisely the same commutator convention restricted to the four-dimensional J, not an independently assigned orbit drive. The equations conserve E, |a|, and the vector charge I_e a+x cross y. The axis below is selected by preparation/conserved charge, not inserted into the Hamiltonian. For q=sqrt(1−c²), 0<|c|<1, write a(t)=(q\cos\omega t,q\sin\omega t,c),\quad x(t)=(b\cos\omega t,b\sin\omega t,z),\quad y=M\dot x. With Omega²=1/(M chi) and kappa=chi g², the oscillator equations require b=\frac{\chi gq}{1-\omega^2/\Omega^2},\qquad z=\chi gc. The electron equation is omega q=(g/I_e)(cb−qz). In addition to the static omega=0 branch, nonzero solutions satisfy \omega^2+\frac{\kappa c}{\mathcal I_e}\omega-\Omega^2=0. For c=.6, chi=1.2, g=.7, I_e=1.3, Omega=2, the computed rates are 1.86890551 and −2.14029012. Direct integration of all three vectors agrees with the exact rotations to about 2.5e-11 through t=8. Norm, energy, and rotation charge are conserved to the stated numerical tolerances. These are nontrivial, autonomous, reciprocal lower-dimensional solutions. Their stability, physical source, and atomic relevance have not been established. This harmonic-source result must not be transferred without checking to the finite, bounded contact-state model. A sharper conditional discriminator: the slow-response-ratio branch For fixed chi,g,I_e and nonzero c, the nonzero 4D rates approach plus or minus Omega as Omega increases, not a finite nonzero static rate. Their transverse response amplitude grows with Omega; they do not have a regular bounded-response adiabatic limit. The 4D static family remains stationary. By contrast, the 6D low-rate branch satisfies \omega(1-\omega^2/\Omega^2)=\frac{2\kappa\sqrt{s}}{\mathcal I_e} and approaches the finite nonzero right-hand side at an interior s. This suggests testing precession well below an independently established source-response resonance, not merely testing whether precession occurs. It distinguishes these two specified effective models. Extra anisotropy, position-dependent interactions, or other source channels could change the 4D result and would need separate tests. A physical clock, source resonance, and readout still have to be derived before this becomes an experimental prediction for electrons. A second conditional discriminator is mixed-block rank. Q maps D−3 unobserved directions into O, so rank(Q)<=D−3. The 6D interior has singular values (1,sqrt(1−s),sqrt(1−s)), hence rank three. A physically justified measurement of three independent geometric mixed directions would imply D>=6 within this interpretation. Nine fitted response coefficients alone would not: source-field mode coefficients could supply response channels without counting further spatial directions. Such representations introduce no physical dimensions outside the one infinite manifold. Neither this rank criterion nor the static argument isolates exactly D=6. Why the displayed petal family is not itself a dimension witness The existing CP3-to-demo bridge permits a chosen nonlinear readout. Allowing the same freedom in a smaller state space makes the displayed trace non-identifying. On the equatorial circle a=(cos theta,sin theta,0) of the 4D sector sphere, the autonomous Hamiltonian H=I_e omega a_z generates theta=omega t. This Hamiltonian does introduce an axis; it is a separate readout counterexample, not the isotropic static-source model above. Let T_L be the Chebyshev polynomial, so T_L(cos theta)=cos(L theta). Choose w(a)=R|T_L(a_x)|(a_x+i a_y),\qquad h(a)=\eta R\sqrt{1-T_L(a_x)^2}(4a_x^3-3a_x). This gives exactly w=R|cos(L theta)| exp(i theta) and h=eta R|sin(L theta)|cos(3 theta), including the demo's 2L planar petals. Checks include L=1,2,3,4,7,10. The absolute-value readout has the same non-smooth zeros as the target formula. This is deliberately a detector/readout counterexample: the underlying geometric trajectory is a circle, not a petalled position trajectory. It is not a linear spatial projection or a derived physical apparatus law. It shows why the freely chosen nonlinear readout in the previous CP3 bridge cannot, by itself, certify depth. A physical restriction on that readout could restore discriminatory power and must be applied equally to both dimensional hypotheses. Verification lower_dimension_response_checks.py checks the exact polynomial complex-structure identity, random-frame static obstruction, harmonic and finite-source energies, 6D rank and static flow, vector-to-matrix dynamics, differential conservation, both integrated 4D rotations, the contrasting fast-response limits, and the readout identity. All verdicts use explicit runtime conditions, including under Python -O. Normal and optimized runs each complete 577 evaluations across 23 runtime conditions. An in-memory mutation audit reverses the electron velocity and, separately, rescales the readout by 1.1. Both errors are rejected in normal and optimized execution by the independent matrix-dynamics and readout conditions respectively; no mutated source is saved. Writing a displacement as x, its uncoupled local equation is \ddot x=\sigma^2x with \sigma=\sqrt{F'(R_*)}=0.2202671528. The quadratic potential is V(x,y)=-\frac{\sigma^2}{2}x^2+bxy+\frac\kappa2y^2. Static elimination gives y=-bx/\kappa and V_{\rm eff}''=-\sigma^2-\frac{b^2}{\kappa}<0. Thus a passive positive-energy orientation mode makes the relaxed curvature more negative and the autonomous coupled system retains a real exponential eigenvalue. Runtime checks cover twelve (\kappa,b) pairs and positive orientation inertias. The driven susceptibility \chi_N(\omega)=\frac1{\kappa-I\omega^2} does reverse sign above resonance. A plane coordinate alone is not a phase space The configuration space of rank-three planes in six dimensions is \operatorname{Gr}(3,6),\qquad \dim\operatorname{Gr}(3,6)=3(6-3)=9. Its conjugate momentum is not optional bookkeeping: it is where the plane stores angular momentum between electron encounters. Gyroscopic stabilization is possible A rotating nuclear three-plane has at least a two-component transverse normal mode. The minimal conservative gyroscopic normal form is \ddot{\mathbf x}+2\Omega J\dot{\mathbf x}-\sigma^2\mathbf x=0, \qquad J=\begin{pmatrix}0&-1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}. The antisymmetric term does no work, so E=\frac12|\dot{\mathbf x}|^2-\frac{\sigma^2}{2}|\mathbf x|^2 is conserved. The characteristic equation is (\lambda^2-\sigma^2)^2+4\Omega^2\lambda^2=0. All four roots are imaginary exactly when \boxed{|\Omega|\ge\sigma}. Below threshold there is a real part. Above threshold the two positive oscillation frequencies are \omega_\pm=|\Omega|\pm\sqrt{\Omega^2-\sigma^2}. Consequently the stabilizing normal form of the preceding section requires a physical antisymmetric term without the compensating coordinate artifact. Candidates include a Berry-curvature term on the dynamical orientation space, a magnetic bivector coupling, or a spinning-rotor relative equilibrium whose energy--momentum Hessian supplies the needed block. title: Flat nucleus precession
summary: The fixed nuclear three-plane and an invariant CP3 binding energy yield an exact conditional precession flow, with conserved misalignment and no automatically selected petal lock.
text: Physical premise (IDWT): There is one infinite-dimensional physical manifold. All sectors form one nested chain of submanifolds within it. Summary: The fixed nuclear three-plane and an invariant CP3 binding energy yield an exact conditional precession flow, with conserved misalignment and no automatically selected petal lock. Premises: follow the lower-dimensional nucleus A depth-three nucleus is lower-dimensional relative to a six-dimensional electron. The existing binding module represents its depth-three structure by a fixed projector P onto O in V6 = O direct-sum H. This is not a literal two-dimensional disk, nor an assumption that the nucleus is isotropic in all six directions. The bound/free module extends lower-depth modes cylindrically across their unstructured directions. It does not replace that extension with delta-function sheet support. This calculation uses the electron's physical spatial position, represented by the orthogonal complex structure J in SO(6)/U(3) = CP3. It does not substitute a stationary orbital or a coefficient ray for that point. Three premises are retained explicitly: a fixed nuclear frame, its SO(3) times SO(3) symmetry, and Hamiltonian evolution on the invariant symplectic CP3 orbit. Additional electron kinetic/field variables and nuclear motion are not included in this reduced flow. Flatness alone does not prove this reduction. From the existing energy to motion Write J=\begin{pmatrix}A&Q\\-Q^T&C\end{pmatrix},\qquad J^T=-J,\quad J^2=-I,\quad P=\operatorname{diag}(I_3,0). The binding module gives AQ + QC = 0 and s=-\frac12\operatorname{tr}A^2\in[0,1],\qquad V_N=V(s). Use the invariant matrix pairing ⟨X,Y⟩ = −tr(XY)/2. Fix the Hamiltonian sign and normalization by \dot J=\frac1{\mathcal I}[\nabla_J V,J],\qquad \mathcal I>0. Here the action scale I (written as mathcal I in equations) is a symplectic normalization, not a nuclear mechanical moment of inertia. It is not fitted or identified with a physical constant in this diagnostic. The natural coadjoint-orbit symplectic construction supplies this commutator form; see Karshon's Hamiltonian group-action notes. The following specialization and solution are derived here. Reversing the symplectic sign reverses precession, not the conservation or closure results. Direct variation gives \delta V=-V'(s)\operatorname{tr}(A\delta A),\qquad \nabla_J V=2V'(s)PJP. Consequently \dot J=\frac{2V'(s)}{\mathcal I}[PJP,J],\qquad \dot A=0,\quad\dot C=0,\quad \dot Q=\frac{2V'(s)}{\mathcal I}AQ. Both s and V(s) are conserved. V'(s) is therefore constant along each trajectory even when V is nonlinear. The exact solution is Q(t)=\exp\!\left(\frac{2V'(s_0)}{\mathcal I}A_0t\right)Q_0. Equivalently the full J is conjugated by diag(exp(2V'(s0)A0 t/I),I3). Antisymmetry, J² = −I, and the chosen CP3 component are preserved. This is actual motion on the proposed electron-sector manifold, not motion created by changing the observer coordinates. Exact precession, with an explicit rate For the binding module's canonical family, A0 = √s0 K and Q0 = diag(√(1−s0),√(1−s0),1), where K generates rotations in the first two axes. For 0 < s0 < 1 and V'(s0) nonzero, Q rotates with signed rate \omega_{\rm p}=\frac{2V'(s_0)\sqrt{s_0}}{\mathcal I},\qquad T_J=\frac{2\pi}{|\omega_{\rm p}|}. The nucleus-relative structure can therefore support precession through an orientation-dependent scalar binding energy. No separately inserted magnetic field or comparison to conventional atomic dynamics is used to obtain this conditional result. But the nuclear kernel must still give a nonzero slope: V'(s)=\int_{Q_N}\rho_N(u)\,\partial_s K_{N6}(u,J(s))\,d\mu_N(u), assuming differentiation under the integral is valid. The lower-dimensional structure permits this dependence; it does not determine its strength. Endpoint qualifications matter. At s0 = 0, A = C = 0 and this contribution to the flow vanishes. At s0 = 1, Q has rank one and AQ = 0, so J is also stationary even if the matrix exponential rotates its unused plane. If V'(s0) = 0, the motion is stationary at any s0. What this resolves, and what it does not There is now an explicit precession equation for the fixed, lower-depth nuclear geometry already written in V2. This is not a new force invented to fit a petal shape. Positive V'(0) makes the exchanging configuration an energy minimum, but the isolated Hamiltonian flow does not relax toward it: s is conserved. An energy minimum is not an attracting trajectory. This corrects any reading of “selects the lock” as automatic dynamical capture. A nonzero precession rate depends on the interaction slope and the prepared s0. This reduced model has no separate orbital-angle variable, so it does not yet derive a ratio to the Coulomb orbit clock. Integer L-dependent frequency locking cannot be inferred from its periodicity. No physical three-coordinate readout has been assigned to J(t) here. Its periodicity alone is not a derivation of the visualization's petals or of its specific 1:1:3 vector-plane generator. The earlier conditional petal construction remains the target to connect to, not a result erased by this calculation. The next calculation should retain the electron–nucleus relative position and the dependence of K_N6 on it, together with the sector variable J. It must determine whether that same interaction synchronizes the relative orbit and this precession. The choice of a product position–CP3 phase space would itself need justification; J must not silently become a duplicate “internal orientation”: CP3 is the particle's actual spatial submanifold. Any relative-position variables must be derived from that same spatial geometry, without counting the electron position twice. Nuclear response can subsequently be included reciprocally, without confusing an electric-polarization calculation with magnetic feedback. A spatial revolution within O does not itself rotate the projector onto O. Making P(t) rotate at an assigned orbital rate would therefore insert a drive, not derive synchronization from “flatness.” The nucleus-to-electron direction inside O may supply additional position-dependent invariants, but those must come from the source map and kernel. The fixed-P calculation deliberately does not prescribe that missing clock through a rotating frame. Verification flat_nucleus_precession_checks.py tests the energy gradient by finite differences, the closed-form derivative, independent O/H frame rotations, numerical integration against the exact solution, constraint and energy conservation, both stationary endpoints, and the predicted full-period versus half-period recurrence. Linear, nonlinear, positive-slope, and negative-slope potentials are tested. All conditions use explicit runtime failures, not assert or a literal PASS. The output reports computed counts and residuals. These tests establish consistency of this reduced model, not its physical premises. The normal and optimized runs each complete 1,991 evaluations across 16 conditions; the largest integration-versus-exact residual is approximately 1.4e-11. An in-memory reversal of the velocity sign is rejected at the independent exact-solution derivative check in both modes. No mutated source is saved; this is a test-sensitivity check, not physical validation. Related Research status — current proof boundaries and next calculations. Actual orbit research correction — preserves the Coulomb-plus-precession target and distinguishes successive constructions.

Define the observed-unobserved exchange involution S_{OH} =\begin{pmatrix} 0&I\\ I&0 \end{pmatrix}. For this special equal-diagonal lock, [K_{\rm lock},S_{OH}]=0. So the particular Procrustes Hessian used in sections 56--57 is exchange symmetric after alignment. However, the most general reciprocal Hermitian block with the same off-diagonal link is K_{\rm gen} =\begin{pmatrix} aI&-\kappa I\\ -\kappa I&cI \end{pmatrix}. It is Hermitian for arbitrary real a,\ c,\ \kappa, but [S_{OH},K_{\rm gen}]=0 if and only if \boxed{a=c.} Therefore \boxed{\text{Hermiticity / reciprocal response does not imply }O\leftrightarrow H\text{ exchange symmetry}.} The exchange symmetry of the special lock Hessian comes from the additional choice of equal observed and unobserved self-stiffnesses, not from self-adjointness alone. 83.2 The orbit generator makes the distinction especially clear The spinor orbit family is \widetilde G_q =\operatorname{diag} \left( q+\frac14, -q+\frac14, -\frac34, \frac14 \right). It is Hermitian for every real q. The spin-factor swap acts by |+-\rangle\leftrightarrow|-+\rangle. Direct calculation gives [S_{OH},\widetilde G_q]=0 if and only if \boxed{q=1.} Hence the desired q=1 value is selected by exchange invariance, not by Hermiticity. 83.3 The locked complex structure is not itself exchange-even In the aligned real 3+3 frame, the locked complex structure is J_{\rm lock} =\begin{pmatrix} 0&I\\ -I&0 \end{pmatrix}. With the same exchange involution S_{OH} =\begin{pmatrix} 0&I\\ I&0 \end{pmatrix}, one finds \boxed{\{S_{OH},J_{\rm lock}\}=0,} not [S_{OH},J_{\rm lock}]=0. So exchanging the two locked three-planes reverses the sign of the complex structure: S_{OH}J_{\rm lock}S_{OH}^{-1}=-J_{\rm lock}. This is important conceptually. The frame lock identifies the two three-frames, but it does not automatically make them indistinguishable under an ordinary commuting symmetry. The complex orientation distinguishes the direction of the map H\to O from its reverse. 83.4 The nucleus also distinguishes the two halves The bound-state module defines O as the nuclear-relative three-plane and H=O^\perp as its orthogonal complement. The construction therefore gives the two subspaces different physical roles before locking. This means an O\leftrightarrow H symmetry cannot be inferred merely from their equal dimension. 83.5 Status of the exchange selection route The exact result from section 82 remains true: O\leftrightarrow H\text{ invariance of }G_q \Longrightarrow q=1. But section 83 shows that current V2 does not derive that invariance from: self-adjointness of the master Dirac operator; reciprocal cross-depth response; Hermiticity of the lock Hessian; or the existence of the locked complex structure. The exchange route is therefore conditional and cannot yet be used as a first-principles derivation of the 1{:}1{:}3 orbit spectrum. 83.6 Revised proof obligation The integer orbit parameter remains open unless one can derive an additional symmetry or selection law. The remaining possibilities are now sharply separated: derive a genuine O\leftrightarrow H invariance of the stationary Hamiltonian circle from the projected electron interaction; derive q=1 from a different representation-theoretic property of the selected circle; derive a dynamical variational rule over the allowed integral circles; or accept q as presently undetermined in the written V2 action. The next useful test is representation-theoretic rather than variational: classify the integral U(1) subgroups of SU(4) compatible with the locked subgroup and the required \mathbf1\oplus\mathbf3 decomposition, and ask whether regularity, primitiveness, or isotropy of the locked orbit reduces the family (q,-q,-1,0) to q=1 without invoking factor exchange. Locked-sector preservation theorem: invariance of the \mathbf1\oplus\mathbf3 split uniquely selects q=1 Section 83 showed that Hermiticity does not imply an observed--unobserved factor-exchange symmetry. There is, however, a cleaner representation-theoretic condition already built into the locked electron geometry. After the diagonal frame lock, (\mathbf2,\mathbf2) \downarrow_{Spin(3)_{\rm diag}} =\mathbf3\oplus\mathbf1. The bound-state module interprets these as the exact three-channel p-like sector and one-channel s-like sector. If the stationary orbit generator is to act within these locked sectors rather than continuously converting the singlet into the triplet, it must preserve this decomposition. For the full integer orbit family, that condition uniquely forces q=1. 84.1 General orbit family in the coupled-spin basis Use the product-spin basis |++\rangle, \quad |+-\rangle, \quad |-+\rangle, \quad |--\rangle, with traceless generator \widetilde G_q =\operatorname{diag} \left( q+\frac14, -q+\frac14, -\frac34, \frac14 \right). Pass to the standard diagonal-spin basis |1,1\rangle, \quad |1,0\rangle, \quad |1,-1\rangle, \quad |0,0\rangle, where |1,0\rangle =\frac{|+-\rangle+|-+\rangle}{\sqrt2}, and |0,0\rangle =\frac{|+-\rangle-|-+\rangle}{\sqrt2}. Exact transformation gives \boxed{ \widetilde G_q^{\rm CG} = \begin{pmatrix} q+\frac14&0&0&0\\ 0&-\frac q2-\frac14&0&\frac{1-q}{2}\\ 0&0&\frac14&0\\ 0&\frac{1-q}{2}&0&-\frac q2-\frac14 \end{pmatrix}. } The crucial matrix element is therefore \boxed{ \langle1,0|\widetilde G_q|0,0\rangle =\frac{1-q}{2}. } Thus every q\ne1 mixes the locked singlet with the m=0 member of the triplet. 84.2 Preserving the locked irreducible sectors Let P_3 =\operatorname{diag}(1,1,1,0) project onto the locked triplet and P_1 =\operatorname{diag}(0,0,0,1) onto the locked singlet. The orbit generator preserves the decomposition if and only if [P_3,\widetilde G_q]=0. Direct calculation gives off-diagonal entries proportional only to 1-q, so \boxed{ [P_3,\widetilde G_q]=0 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad q=1. } Equivalently, using the total locked-spin Casimir J^2 =\operatorname{diag}(2,2,2,0), one finds \boxed{ [J^2,\widetilde G_q]=0 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad q=1. } This does not require the orbit generator to commute with the whole diagonal Spin(3). It only requires that it not mix inequivalent irreducible sectors. The beam axis may still split the triplet internally. 84.3 Why beam SO(2) alone was too weak The axial generator in this coupled basis is J_z =\operatorname{diag}(1,0,-1,0). For every q, \boxed{[J_z,\widetilde G_q]=0.} Both the triplet m=0 state and the singlet have axial quantum number zero, so beam-axis symmetry cannot distinguish or prevent their mixing. This explains exactly why the Section-81 beam-centralizer argument failed in the physically correct basis. The stronger invariant is the locked representation label carried by J^2. 84.4 Unique surviving generator At q=1, the mixing vanishes and \boxed{ \widetilde G_1^{\rm CG} =\operatorname{diag} \left( \frac54, -\frac34, \frac14, -\frac34 \right). } This is exactly the existing V2 orbit generator, and Section 74 already showed that it can be written without any singlet--triplet discriminator as \boxed{ \widetilde G_1 =-\frac34I +\frac12J_z +\frac32J_z^2. } The absence of a J^2 term now has a sharper meaning: the selected generator acts identically on the two m=0 states and therefore preserves the \mathbf3\oplus\mathbf1 decomposition without using the representation label to shift one sector relative to the other. Passing to \Lambda^2\mathbf4 then gives the already verified positive rotation rates \boxed{ \frac12, \frac12, \frac32 } and hence \boxed{1:1:3.} 84.5 Status of the result The algebraic theorem is exact: \boxed{ \text{within the family }(q,-q,-1,0), \quad \text{preservation of }\mathbf3\oplus\mathbf1 \Longrightarrow q=1. } This is stronger than the factor-exchange route because it does not require O and H to be physically interchangeable. It only asks the stationary orbit dynamics to respect the irreducible sectors produced by the already-selected diagonal frame lock. The remaining physical question is whether that preservation law is mandatory in V2. The current electron module calls \mathbf1\oplus\mathbf3 the exact s\oplus p branching used by the chemistry construction, which strongly motivates treating the two summands as distinct locked channels. But the projected master action has not yet explicitly proved [P_3,H_{\rm orb}]=0. So the result should presently be stated as a representation-theoretic closure theorem conditional on channel preservation, not yet as an unconditional action theorem. 84.6 Next falsification test The next step is to inspect every place the \mathbf1\oplus\mathbf3 branching is used in the bound-state, magnetic, and observer modules and ask whether any existing observable or transition law actually requires singlet/triplet preservation. If V2 already assumes or derives that the s-like channel cannot be coherently mixed with the p-like triplet by the stationary orbit Hamiltonian, then q=1 is no longer free and the dimensionless 1{:}1{:}3 spectrum is closed. If such mixing is allowed, then this theorem remains only conditional and q is still an open dynamical datum. Related Research status — current proof boundaries and correction guidance. The result is exact: within the integral family (q,-q,-1,0), q=1 is the unique branch whose stationary Hamiltonian produces no drift of the selected frame link. 87.1 Use the singlet adapted to the selected diagonal lock For the aligned frame link Q_{m scat}=I, choose the coupled basis |1,1angle,\quad |1,0angle,\quad |1,-1angle,\quad |0,0angle. The last state is the one-dimensional invariant line of the selected diagonal Spin(3): |Sangle=|0,0angle. In the two-dimensional subspace \operatorname{span}\{|1,0angle,|Sangle\}, the general orbit generator is exactly  oxed{ \widetilde G_q =\left(- rac q2- rac14ight)I - rac{q-1}{2}K_z. } Thus the entire nontrivial action on the selected singlet line is the relative-frame term. 87.2 Exact time evolution Up to the common phase generated by the scalar term,  oxed{ |S(t)angle =\cos\!\left( rac{(q-1)t}{2}ight)|Sangle +i\sin\!\left( rac{(q-1)t}{2}ight)|1,0angle. } Consequently  oxed{ |\langle S|S(t)angle|^2 =\cos^2\!\left( rac{(q-1)t}{2}ight). } The instantaneous Fubini--Study velocity away from the selected singlet ray has squared norm  oxed{ \left\|(I-|Sangle\langle S|)\widetilde G_q|Sangleight\|^2 = rac{(q-1)^2}{4}. } Therefore  oxed{ q=1 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad 	ext{zero projective drift away from the selected locked ray}. } This is stronger than preservation of the whole maximally entangled orbit. eq1 flow remains within the maximally entangled s=0 family; what it changes is the orientation of the frame link inside that family. On the associated real three-frames, the selected link therefore evolves as a relative SO(3) rotation with angle magnitude  oxed{	heta_{m rel}(t)=(q-1)t.} In the aligned frame, Q(t)=R_z((q-1)t) up to the overall orientation convention. For the scattering-frame functional already tested in sections 56--57, V_{m frame}(Q) = rac\kappa2\|I-Q\|_F^2, this gives the exact mismatch energy  oxed{ V_q(t) =2\kappa\left[1-\cos((q-1)t)ight] =4\kappa\sin^2\!\left( rac{(q-1)t}{2}ight). } Hence  oxed{ V_q''(0)=2\kappa(q-1)^2. } For positive lock stiffness, q=1 is the unique integral branch with identically zero frame-mismatch cost. 87.4 What this does and does not prove This closes a loophole left by section 86. Thus the integer family has the kinematic interpretation: q-1 measures the winding rate of the relative-frame drift with respect to the primitive orbit parameter. It is not yet proven to be a quantized harmonic-oscillator occupation number, so that stronger interpretation should not be asserted. 87.5 Relation to the earlier minimum-norm result Section 78 found independently that \|\widetilde G_q\|^2=2q^2+ rac34 is uniquely minimized at q=1 over positive integral q. The second is preferable because it refers to an interaction structure already developed in V2 rather than postulating a new variational functional over Hamiltonian circles. 87.6 Remaining dependency The conclusion is as strong as the scattering-frame lock itself. The geometry and the exact evolution above are established, but current V2 has not yet derived the coefficient and precise Q_{m scat} coupling from the master operator. Therefore the present status is  oxed{ 	ext{if the scattering-selected frame potential is the physical gross-lock term, then }q=1	ext{ is dynamically forced for the stationary locked branch}. } This substantially narrows the remaining proof obligation. One no longer needs an independent principle saying ``choose the smallest q.'' One needs to derive the already-motivated full-rank scattering-frame coupling from the projected master dynamics. The base part of the argument can now be stated invariantly, without relying on the notation used for the magnetic trajectory. The electron sector is Q_6=\mathbb{CP}^3\cong SU(4)/U(3). For any selected ray [Z_*]\in Q_6, its isotropy algebra is \mathfrak h_{Z_*} =\{X\in\mathfrak{su}(4):(I-P_*)XZ_*=0\}, \qquad P_*=Z_*Z_*^\dagger. Projecting its action orthogonally away from the selected ray gives \boxed{ (I-P_*)\widetilde G_q|S\rangle =\frac{1-q}{2}|1,0\rangle. } Therefore \boxed{ \widetilde G_q\in\mathfrak h_{Z_*} \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad q=1. } This is the cleanest form yet of the selection theorem. Summary: An explicit quadratic nuclear-plane kernel reproduces the precession flow, while inverse-rate reconstruction exposes nonuniqueness and the oriented source required for the full petal generator. What is being reverse engineered The target is first the fixed-nucleus sector precession just derived, and then the stronger target of the visualization's selected rotation generator. These are distinct inverse problems. Constructing a kernel that yields a specified motion proves compatibility, not independent physical selection. No measured masses, fields, or conventional atomic-orbital densities are used in the construction below. Retain J in SO(6)/U(3), the nuclear three-plane projector P, and the symplectic convention dot J = [grad V,J]/I of the precession note. The scale I is an action normalization. The common 6-vector frame and projectors are the binding module's geometric premises, not new coordinates added to the particle. 1. An explicit nuclear-plane interaction kernel Let u denote a nuclear configuration, P(u) its rank-three projector in the shared frame, and gamma(u) a scalar coefficient. Define \boxed{ K_{N6}^{\rm orient}(u,J) =\frac{\gamma(u)}2\|P(u)JP(u)\|_F^2 =-\frac{\gamma(u)}2\operatorname{tr}(P(u)JP(u)J). } This is a smooth, quadratic orientation interaction. Under a simultaneous SO(6) rotation of both arguments it is invariant. It measures how much the electron complex structure rotates nuclear-plane directions within that plane instead of into its complement. It does not model the nucleus as a point or a thin charged sheet. For a normalized nuclear density with a common projector P(u)=P0, V_N(J)=\int\rho_N(u)K_{N6}^{\rm orient}(u,J)d\mu_N(u) =\bar\gamma s(J;P_0),\qquad \bar\gamma=\int\rho_N(u)\gamma(u)d\mu_N(u). It gives precisely the previous V(s)=kappa s with kappa=mean gamma. Thus the previously unspecified orientation kernel now has an explicit candidate. For varying P(u), the integral remains well defined but generally does not collapse to one scalar times s; its anisotropy must be retained. The coefficients, density, and identification of the shared frames are still physical inputs. This kernel is the orientation channel only. It does not supply radial Coulomb binding, spatial falloff, retardation, a field propagator, or a definition of physical separation on the sector. Adding a J-independent term leaves the reduced J flow unchanged, but cannot be advertised as solving the separate relative-position dynamics. 2. Reciprocity is available from the same energy For fixed u and the skew pairing −tr(XY)/2, \nabla_J K=2\gamma PJP. For projector variations, with the ordinary symmetric trace pairing, \delta_P K=\operatorname{tr}(G_P\delta P),\qquad G_P=-\gamma JPJ. The latter expression is an ambient gradient restricted to allowed tangent variations delta P = [B,P], B skew; it is not by itself a nuclear velocity. Simultaneous rotation of both arguments gives \delta_J K\big|_{\delta J=[B,J]} +\delta_P K\big|_{\delta P=[B,P]}=0. Hence a joint dynamical model can use this single interaction to obtain reciprocal orientational forces. A nuclear kinetic or symplectic action is still needed for the response equation; no mechanical inertia or magnetic susceptibility is silently supplied by this identity. 3. Invert an entire precession-rate function For 0<s<1 the previous flow gives the signed rate \omega_{\rm p}(s)=\frac{2V'(s)\sqrt{s}}{\mathcal I}. Therefore a prescribed rate function determines the reduced potential up to a constant on an interval: \boxed{ V(s)=C+\frac{\mathcal I}{2} \int^s\frac{\omega_{\rm p}(v)}{\sqrt v}\,dv. } For example, omega_p(s)=a sqrt(s)+b s^(3/2) gives V(s)=C+I a s/2+I b s²/4. Substituting s(J;P(u)) into this expression gives a higher-order orientation-kernel candidate, for a fixed common plane. A single trajectory at conserved s0 gives much less information: it fixes only V'(s0)=I omega_p(s0)/(2 sqrt(s0)). Adding lambda(s−s0)² changes the kernel away from that trajectory without changing its motion. Likewise, any delta K with zero nuclear marginal leaves V unchanged. Thus neither one precessing orbit nor an entire reduced V identifies a unique microscopic kernel. 4. A nonzero universal rate has a regularity cost Demanding omega_p(s)=omega0 at every 0<s<1 gives V(s)=C+\mathcal I\omega_0\sqrt{s}. This is not smooth at the aligned configuration. Along the smooth signed-coordinate curve A=epsilon K, Q=diag(sqrt(1−epsilon²), sqrt(1−epsilon²),1), C=−epsilon K, it becomes proportional to |epsilon|. The two directional derivatives disagree at zero. This is a property of the inverse construction, not a prohibition on precession. A smooth alternative is V_\eta(s)=\mathcal I\omega_0(\sqrt{s+\eta^2}-\eta),\qquad \omega_{{\rm p},\eta}(s)=\omega_0\sqrt{\frac{s}{s+\eta^2}},\quad\eta>0. It approaches the desired rate away from alignment and tends to zero near alignment. Eta is an additional model parameter, not a derived nuclear width and not the visualization's imbalance parameter. Matching one selected s0 to an orbital clock instead only calibrates a coefficient; it does not establish a dynamically attracting frequency lock. 5. Reverse engineering the full chosen rotation For a prescribed skew generator B_star with units of inverse time, the linear potential V_{\rm target}(J)=\mathcal I\langle B_\star,J\rangle =-\frac{\mathcal I}{2}\operatorname{tr}(B_\star J) gives exactly dot J=[B_star,J] and J(t)=exp(t B_star)J0 exp(−t B_star). Choose the 1:1:3 vector-plane generator corresponding to the existing magnetic construction and this supplies its base rotation. Its specified spin/section lift can then be tested against the existing coefficient flow; the physical observer map and preparation are still required for petals. An inverse source kernel is consequently K_{\rm drive}(u,J)=\mathcal I\langle B(u),J\rangle,\qquad \int\rho_N(u)B(u)d\mu_N(u)=B_\star. This identifies the source tensor that would be needed, rather than deriving that tensor from a scalar nuclear density. It is a separate candidate from the quadratic plane kernel; summing them generally changes the target flow. No claim is made that the sum preserves the desired petals automatically. 6. What a bare nuclear plane can and cannot select A kernel depending only on the unoriented plane P and J must respect the stabilizer SO(3)_O times SO(3)_H. No nonzero fixed skew matrix B_star commutes with this whole group: each diagonal skew 3x3 block must commute with all SO(3) rotations and is therefore zero; the off-diagonal block cannot be invariant under independent rotations of O and H either. Thus a bare plane cannot select that particular linear drive. This does not contradict the quadratic kernel's precession: its effective generator 2 mean(gamma) PJP/I also depends on the electron's prepared J. The result does not exclude a joint symmetry-breaking electron–nucleus solution. It says that an oriented nuclear current, a relational electron–nucleus tensor, or another dynamically selected structure must supply the missing orientation if the full fixed generator is to follow from the source. Flatness already provides the split; it does not provide every axis and relative rotation rate inside that split. Status and next test We have constructed a smooth quadratic inverse kernel, derived both orientation variations, and inverted general precession-rate functions. We have also identified an exact linear source kernel for the stronger target and the extra source information it requires. None is a unique first-principles interaction or a completed electron–nucleus binding model. Next, use the actual projected nuclear/electron currents to calculate the allowed source tensors and their energy cost. Test whether the quadratic orientation channel and a selected linear drive emerge together with the same orbital clock, rather than fitting their sum to the displayed curve. Explicit runtime conditions remain active under Python -O; synthetic targets are not experimental data and no literal PASS is used as a physical verdict. title: Multicentre orbit axes
summary: Three-petal motion gives exact trigonal axes and a distinct 6D rotation gives tetrahedral axes; under bound-within/free-without, projected nuclear crossing is an encounter rather than an unobserved-depth miss.

Summary: Three-petal motion gives exact trigonal axes and a distinct 6D rotation gives tetrahedral axes; under bound-within/free-without, projected nuclear crossing is an encounter rather than an unobserved-depth miss. The corrected molecular question Molecular nuclei should not be inserted as generic fixed perturbations. The stronger proposal is that they settle along directions selected by a shared electron trajectory. The electron follows Hamiltonian motion in six coordinates; in a weak-force interval this approaches a straight line, while nuclear encounters bend it. Molecular shape may then be a closure and force-balance condition constrained by conservation of total momentum, energy, and the six-dimensional angular-momentum bivector. There are two different apparent encounters: the orbit can project through a central nucleus while carrying nonzero coordinates unsupported by that nucleus; an outer nucleus can lie along a petal axis without lying at the electron's instantaneous radius. Three trigonal directions are exact For the checked signed relative equilibrium (x,y)=\cos(3\theta)(\cos\theta,\sin\theta), the three distinct outward maxima occur at 0,2\pi/3,4\pi/3. Their unit vectors have off-diagonal Gram entries -1/2, so their mutual angle is exactly 120^\circ. The actual signed three-petal branch, rather than a modulus-folded six-lobe image, therefore supplies the trigonal axes directly. Four directions require a three-dimensional projection The planar signed L=4 rose has eight directions and is not tetrahedral merely because its integer is four. A different one-parameter rotation in six coordinates does produce four tetrahedral directions. Set a=\sqrt{\frac23},\qquad b=\frac1{\sqrt3}, and q(\theta)=(a\cos\theta,a\sin\theta,b\cos2\theta, b\sin2\theta,0,0). This is a genuine constant-radius group orbit, |q|=1. At the four quarter turns its visible positions are (a,0,b),\quad(0,a,-b),\quad(-a,0,b),\quad(0,-a,-b). Every distinct pair has inner product -1/3, giving \arccos(-1/3)=109.4712206\ldots^\circ. Equiangularity forces the amplitude ratio: -b^2=-a^2+b^2 gives a^2=2b^2, and unit radius fixes both amplitudes. This is an orbit-level counterpart of the s+3p simplex geometry, but the completed interaction has not yet been shown to sustain this (1,2) rotation. Conservation closes the angle calculation Suppose the electron follows near-straight segments between n equivalent interactions and each passage exchanges the same impulse magnitude along a unit nuclear direction \mathbf n_a. Periodic momentum closure requires \sum_{a=1}^n\mathbf n_a=0. If equivalence also makes every distinct pairwise product equal to c, dotting the closure equation with any \mathbf n_b gives 1+(n-1)c=0, \qquad c=-\frac1{n-1}. Consequently n=3 forces c=-1/2 and the trigonal angle 120^\circ, while n=4 forces c=-1/3 and the tetrahedral angle 109.471\ldots^\circ. Conversely, both direction sets checked above sum to zero, so equal impulses close exactly. This supplies a candidate dynamical link that the earlier hybrid-state proof did not: straightest-path tendency supplies the segments, conservation closes their impulse polygon, and equivalent nuclear interactions make it a regular simplex. The conclusion is conditional on equal impulse magnitudes and equivalent passages. It is not by itself evidence that the presently proposed interaction kernel produces those impulses, and the visible simplex theorem is not uniquely six-dimensional; the six-dimensional content is the continuous six-dimensional orbit that realizes the passages. Exact passage through the cylindrically extended nucleus For every checked signed-rose branch L=2,3,4, the visible coordinates vanish at \theta_k=\frac{(k+1/2)\pi}{L}. Direct evaluation gives |q_{\rm vis}(\theta_k)|=0, \qquad |q_{\rm hid}(\theta_k)|=1. Under "bound within, free without," the first equation is the physically relevant one. A depth-three nucleus extends cylindrically through the three directions it does not support, so nonzero q_{\rm hid} does not provide separation. The trajectory encounters the nuclear support whenever its three supported coordinates coincide. The earlier "full-depth miss" interpretation is withdrawn as inconsistent with that premise. What the first fixed-ligand test says A provisional embedded-point kernel V(q)=-\sum_a\frac{Z_a}{|q-(R_a,0)|} was used only to perturb the completed one-centre solutions. With ligands at radius 2.5 and charge 0.01, the nearest visible central approaches were about 0.00215 for three trigonal ligands and 0.00120 for four tetrahedral ligands; unsupported-coordinate norms were about 0.9972 and 0.9978. Energy was conserved, but the old orbit did not recur exactly. This embedded-point calculation belongs to the alternative unobserved-localized model; it is retained only as a rejected-control comparison. Cycle-averaged force-balance verdict The provisional kernel was next tested against the reciprocal condition \frac1T\int_0^T F_a(t)\,dt=0 for every symmetry-related ligand. A root at R=1 is inadmissible: the ideal axis-aligned trajectory reaches the outer nucleus with zero unobserved separation, so the point kernel is singular there. For a unit central source, three trigonal ligands of effective charge 0.1, and the signed L=3 candidate, one noncollision root occurs at R=1.89676096. Its radial force derivative is +0.0485176, so it is unstable rather than restoring. For the orbit-aligned tetrahedral curve with central and ligand effective charges 0.1, no noncollision root occurs on the tested ranges R\in[0.2,0.95] and R\in[1.05,4]. Thus the alternative embedded-point 1/r kernel does not turn the available conservation geometry into a stable molecule. Conservation and equivalence derive the angles, but a derived lower-depth interaction/response kernel—or a materially retuned electron trajectory—is still required for stable reciprocal closure. Flexible nuclear three-planes Let a nucleus carry a rank-three orthoprojector P_a in the electron's six-coordinate space. A minimal anisotropic distance family is d_{\eta,P}^2=\Delta q^T\bigl(P+\eta(I-P)\bigr)\Delta q. The unobserved-localized point-kernel control is \eta=1, while bound-within/free-without is the cylindrical limit \eta=0. Allowing P to relax instantaneously with no orientation cost does not retain an anisotropic force. A rank-three plane in six dimensions can always be chosen either to contain the one separation vector \Delta q or to lie wholly perpendicular to it. Therefore \min_{\operatorname{rank}P=3}d_{\eta,P}^2 =\min(1,\eta)|\Delta q|^2. For \eta>0 the relaxed interaction is only a constant rescaling of 1/|\Delta q|. In the selected cylindrical limit \eta=0, the minimum is zero and the ideal Coulomb kernel becomes singular: a freely reorienting plane can turn until it intersects the electron. Complete cost-free flexibility is therefore unusable in either case. Finite inertia or stiffness is essential. The physically useful interpretation of flexibility must be finite response. The nuclear plane needs rotational inertia, an orientation stiffness relative to its lower-depth structure, or a nonzero response time. It can then lag the electron, store angular momentum, and return it through backreaction. This is the same kind of dynamical susceptibility already isolated by the response modules, now applied to molecular closure. A fixed projector and an instantaneously minimized projector are the two controls on either side of that finite-response problem. Correct next solve: reciprocal closure The nuclei must now be dynamical variables rather than fixed scenery. For a candidate period T, solve simultaneously for electron and nuclear initial data, the response source, and the nuclear scale, subject to X(T)=gX(0),\qquad P(T)=gP(0), where g is the appropriate trigonal or tetrahedral permutation-rotation, together with energy and total bivector conservation. Equivalently, in a Born--Oppenheimer reduction require zero cycle-averaged force on every nucleus, \frac1T\int_0^T F_a(t)\,dt=0. This formulation tests the proposed spatial mechanism: near-straight electron motion, deflection at the lower-depth nuclear structures, and a molecular shape selected partly by closure and conservation in six dimensions. It also makes the proposal falsifiable: if no stable reciprocal periodic branch exists for the derived kernel, geometrical availability alone is insufficient. Finite nuclear-plane response — continuation: proves passive flexibility cannot stabilize the measured saddle and isolates the gyroscopic threshold. Finite cylindrical nuclear profile — correction: replaces the rejected unobserved-localized force kernel and finds restoring trigonal and tetrahedral radial branches.

A full projective recurrence therefore requires both ΩT and νT to be integer multiples of 2π. If Ω/ν = p/q in lowest positive integer terms, its period is 2πq/ν. An irrational ratio gives no exact recurrence. The plane readout forgets the sign of the amplitude pair. It closes after one clock turn whenever 2Ω/ν is an integer, even if Ω/ν is a half-integer. u T \ \in\ 2\pi\mathbb Z. Taking Ω/ν = L but ε/ν irrational preserves the entire displayed orbit while eliminating exact recurrence of the coefficient ray. Unlike adding a multiple of I₄, this is a physical relative phase in the four-state model, not a removable global phase. Its selected representation gives the correct weights exactly; the problem is not to replace those weights with fitted frequencies. title: Reciprocal cylindrical molecule
summary: A 6D electron, relative angular source, moving finite cylindrical nuclei, and flexible nuclear-plane rotors form one translation-invariant reciprocal Hamiltonian with verified energy and Noether-charge conservation.
text: Physical premise (IDWT): There is one infinite-dimensional physical manifold. All sectors form one nested chain of submanifolds within it. Particle depth counts ordinary, literal macroscopic spatial dimensions. “Observed” and “unobserved” describe an observer's access to those dimensions, not different kinds of physical dimension. See spatial meaning and mathematical scope. Summary: A 6D electron, relative angular source, moving finite cylindrical nuclei, and flexible nuclear-plane rotors form one translation-invariant reciprocal Hamiltonian with verified energy and Noether-charge conservation. Why the first combination failed The completed petal Hamiltonian was originally written about a fixed nuclear origin. Adding moving nuclei without changing that source makes its magnetic completion depend on the absolute electron coordinate and destroys visible translation invariance. A failed momentum-derivative check exposed this before the model was used for shooting. The correction is to define the source coupling using the electron--central- nucleus relative coordinate s=q-(R_0,0). The completed kinetic term is then H_e=\frac1{2m_e}|p-m_e\lambda Cs|^2 +\frac{\langle C,C\rangle}{2I_C}. The central nucleus receives the opposite visible component of the source force. It receives no unobserved translational momentum because it remains a depth-three object. Full diagnostic Hamiltonian For nuclear centres R_a\in\mathbb R^3, momenta P_a, rank-three planes \Pi_a, and skew plane velocities \Omega_a, use H=H_e+\sum_a\frac{|P_a|^2}{2M_a} +\sum_a\frac{I_a}{2}\langle\Omega_a,\Omega_a\rangle +\sum_a V_a\bigl(|\Pi_a(q-(R_a,0))|\bigr) +\sum_{a<b}\frac{Z_aZ_b}{|R_a-R_b|}. Here V_a is the finite uniform supported-space profile of the preceding note, extended cylindrically through unsupported coordinates. The source coadjoint equation uses s\wedge p and s\wedge Cs, not q\wedge p about an external origin. Each plane obeys \dot\Pi_a=[\Omega_a,\Pi_a], \qquad I_a\dot\Omega_a=2[\Pi_a,\partial_{\Pi_a}V_a]. Every force and torque is obtained from this one energy. The executable originally specialized the equations to m_e=1 while exposing a configurable mass. The September 7 audit restores the factors of m_e in the completed square, velocity, magnetic force, and source gradient; the reported unit-mass run is unchanged. Nuclear mutual repulsion is a separately assumed centre-charge interaction here. It is not the mutual interaction of overlapping finite cylindrical charge profiles, particularly when their support planes differ. The full skew rotor also permits angular momentum in the plane stabilizer; a pure Grassmannian plane rotor requires horizontal initial angular velocity or an explicit reduction. Conserved quantities The visible total momentum is \mathcal P_O=p_O+\sum_aP_a. The visible rotational charge is \mathcal J_O=q_O\wedge p_O+C_{OO} +\sum_aR_a\wedge P_a-\sum_a I_a(\Omega_a)_{OO}. Ten random states independently check the differential conservation of H, \mathcal P_O, and \mathcal J_O. A nonlinear example contains one central cylinder plus three trigonal ligand cylinders with moving centres, four flexible planes, and a nonzero electron angular source. Over eight model time units its maximum errors are: quantity maximum error energy 7.93\times10^{-8} visible momentum 3.59\times10^{-15} visible rotational charge 2.87\times10^{-10} projector idempotence 2.18\times10^{-11} The differential energy residual is below 8.9\times10^{-10}. Thus the finite profile, moving lower-depth centres, plane rotors, and completed source are mutually compatible at the Hamiltonian level. Remaining periodic-orbit problem This calculation establishes the system to shoot; it does not claim that the arbitrary nonlinear example is molecularly periodic. The next solve should start from the exact trigonal orbit and the restoring finite-profile radius, fix centre-of-mass and global-rotation gauge directions, and solve a relative-periodic boundary condition. The monodromy calculation must retain electron, source, nuclear-centre, and plane-rotor perturbations. Stable radial force balance alone is not sufficient. The uniform-ball nuclear profile and dimensionless masses, charges, and inertias remain diagnostic inputs. A successful branch would establish existence within that controlled model, not yet derive those inputs from V2. Reproduction reciprocal_cylindrical_molecule_checks.py checks the relative-source energy gradient, visible translation and rotation charges, nonlinear integration, all four plane constraints, and a nonzero source preparation. Related Finite cylindrical nuclear profile — prerequisite: supplies the finite encounter law and restoring candidate radii. Nuclear-plane rotor — prerequisite: supplies the finite-inertia projector dynamics and torque normalization. Cylindrical petal continuation — begins fixed-centre periodic continuation and diagnoses the soft shooting directions.

title: Ring section embedding
summary: The ring's three-state generator embeds in positive-degree section spaces under the same Killing action, but this does not identify a degree-zero electron sector.
text: Physical premise (IDWT): There is one infinite-dimensional physical manifold. All sectors form one nested chain of submanifolds within it. Particle depth counts ordinary, literal macroscopic spatial dimensions. “Observed” and “unobserved” describe an observer's access to those dimensions, not different kinds of physical dimension. See spatial meaning and mathematical scope. Summary: The ring's three-state generator embeds in positive-degree section spaces under the same Killing action, but this does not identify a degree-zero electron sector. What can be unified algebraically The demo uses a separate ring coefficient generator ν diag(0,−1,0), with initial state (A,B/√2,B/√2), and a constant-radius readout whose angle is the relative clock phase. Its projective orbit is not generated by the one-dimensional H⁰(O(0)) space. There is nevertheless a simple embedding in the same section spaces used for the petalled cases. Denote the section degree by k here, keeping it distinct from the demo's ring label L = 0. For every k ≥ 2 choose normalized monomials proportional to s_0=Z_1Z_2Z_4^{k-2},\qquad s_-=Z_3Z_4^{k-1},\qquad s_r=Z_4^k. They are distinct sections of O(k). Under the same generator Ĝ_k = N₁−N₂−N₃ their weights are exactly (0,−1,0). Hence \Phi(t)=A s_0+\frac B{\sqrt2}e^{i\nu t}s_- +\frac B{\sqrt2}s_r has precisely the demo's three-state coefficient evolution and returns after 2π/ν. The prescribed ring readout Γ_x+iΓ_y = R times the normalized clock coherence is Re^{iνt}. This is an actual time-dependent coefficient orbit in a selected section subspace, not a stationary field substituted for the ring. The selected spinor-line construction lifts this field into Σ⊗O(k+2), just as it lifts the degree-k petalled orbit. At k = 2, the 10-dimensional section space therefore contains both the ring's three-state generator and the four-state generator used for four petals. No new generator weights or electric charge have been fitted to obtain this fact. What this does not unify This is not a degree-zero construction. The earlier dimension obstruction for H⁰(O(0)) remains intact, and the k ≥ 2 ring cannot be declared the physical L = 0 atomic state without a separate identification. It shows that the generator algebra need not require an unrelated carrier space; it does not derive which carrier the physical circular state occupies. The ring and petalled prescriptions select different mode subspaces and readout rules. An algebraic embedding alone does not derive a single apparatus response that selects between those rules, a nuclear preparation mechanism, energies, or transition strengths. In particular, the petal-count rule 2k applies to the prepared extremal exchange construction, not to every trajectory in O(k). Degree alone does not force a petalled outline. The smooth geometric clock dipole from the probe calculation also exists here, but it already gives circular dipole signals for some petalled preparations. It cannot by itself distinguish those detector images. Research consequence A single positive-degree field sector may support multiple coefficient-orbit families under the same Killing action. This supplies a concrete candidate bridge for the ring, with no change to the displayed petals or their code. The remaining problem is physical family selection and the degree/flux interpretation, not merely finding three suitable abstract frequencies. The scalar effective-drive route also applies algebraically in this space, but inherits the omitted-mode leakage and locking corrections audited in the companion note. The embedding is not a stability proof. Reproduction orbit_drive_origin_checks.py checks the three weights, normalized evolution, clock readout, and full recurrence for k = 2, 3, 4, while retaining the one-dimensional degree-zero check.
