title: Five-dimensional CP3 selection and spectral discrimination
summary: A five-dimensional spinor-bivector model also selects a CP3 minimum family, but its exact spectral sum rule excludes the six-dimensional singlet-triplet gap within the linear-bivector operator class.
text: Physical premise (IDWT): There is one infinite-dimensional physical manifold. All sectors form one nested chain of submanifolds within it. Particle depth counts ordinary, literal macroscopic spatial dimensions. “Observed” and “unobserved” describe an observer's access to those dimensions, not different kinds of physical dimension. See spatial meaning and mathematical scope. Summary: A five-dimensional spinor-bivector model also selects a CP3 minimum family, but its exact spectral sum rule excludes the six-dimensional singlet-triplet gap within the linear-bivector operator class. Why this comparison matters The six-dimensional selection uses one pure normalized irreducible spinor, a real skew source, positive quadratic source energy, and linear spinor-bivector coupling. Here the same construction is performed for a five-dimensional Euclidean carrier. No inherited V1 spatial geometry is assigned to that carrier. An irreducible Spin(5) spinor has four complex components, as does either irreducible half-spin representation of Spin(6). The general dimensions are 2^n for Spin(2n+1) and 2^{n-1} for each half-spin of Spin(2n). See Woit's representation construction. The explicit five-dimensional representation and its quaternionic structure are also discussed in Niedzialomski's five-dimensional spinor analysis. The following energy and spectrum calculations are explicit local derivations, not claims taken from those references. Exact five-dimensional construction Using Pauli matrices, take the Hermitian Clifford generators \gamma=(\sigma_1\otimes I,\sigma_2\otimes I, \sigma_3\otimes\sigma_1,\sigma_3\otimes\sigma_2, \sigma_3\otimes\sigma_3). They obey \{\gamma_a,\gamma_b\}=2\delta_{ab}I_4. For z^\dagger z=1, define H_{ab}=-i\gamma_a\gamma_b,\quad b_{ab}=z^\dagger H_{ab}z,\quad n_a=z^\dagger\gamma_a z, \quad S(b)=\sum_{a<b}b_{ab}H_{ab}. Let J be the skew matrix with upper entries b_{ab}, with \|J\|^2=-\operatorname{tr}(J^2)/2=\sum b_{ab}^2. Direct Clifford calculation gives |n|^2=1,\qquad \|J\|^2=2,\qquad J^2=-I_5+nn^T,\qquad Jn=0. Thus the source has two unit rotation planes and one null axis. It is not an invertible complex structure on an odd-dimensional vector space. Furthermore S(b)z=2z,\qquad zz^\dagger=\frac{S(b)^2}{8}+\frac{S(b)}4. The last identity reconstructs the ray from the bivector, so no ray degree is lost. These identities are verified as polynomials in eight independent real spinor components, without assuming normalization numerically. For an initially unrestricted skew B, take E(B,z)=\mu\|B\|^2-g\langle B,J(z)\rangle, \qquad \mu,g>0. With \rho=g/(2\mu), completion gives E(B,z)=\mu\|B-\rho J(z)\|^2-\frac{g^2}{2\mu}. All normalized rays minimize at B=\rho J(z), and the injective reconstruction makes their minimum family CP3. This does not require assuming CP3 as the carrier's spatial base. It is the collective polarization/source family of this specified five-dimensional model. The Berry term i\hbar z^\dagger\dot z is the same nonzero projective symplectic structure as in the six-dimensional construction. Adding M\|\dot B\|^2/2 gives reciprocal dynamics and the exact conserved bound \mu\|B-\rho J(z)\|^2+\frac{\|\Pi\|^2}{2M} =E_{\rm total}-E_{\min}. This controls departure from the minimum family, not spatial localization or an electron-nucleus orbit. The ten-component source-space Hessian after ground-ray elimination has six flat directions and four positive normal directions 2\mu; these are matrix-space counts, not extra spatial axes. The Hessian statement also follows analytically: minimizing the completed square over rays gives E_{\rm eff}(B)-E_{\min}=\mu\,operatorname{dist} (B,\rho J(\mathrm{CP}^3))^2. In a tubular neighborhood of this smooth embedded orbit, the squared-distance Hessian is twice the normal projector. The numerical Hessian is an independent finite-difference check of that result. What differs from six dimensions At the selected source, the five-dimensional spinor Hamiltonian has \operatorname{spec}h_5(\rho J) =g\rho\,(-2,0,0,2), whereas the six-dimensional chiral model has \operatorname{spec}h_6(\rho J) =g\rho\,(-3,1,1,1). Their gaps above the selected ray are respectively (2,2,4)g\rho and (4,4,4)g\rho. Thus “CP3 minima, a gap, a Berry term, and conservative confinement” do not distinguish them, while the full gap multiplicity does. Their induced source kinetic metrics also differ. For Fubini–Study unit horizontal tangents at z=(1,0,0,0), the five-dimensional squared bivector derivative has weights (4,4,4,4,8,8); the six-dimensional construction has weight 8 in all six directions. The five-dimensional CP3 family is not being claimed to have the same induced metric or every same response. A genuine no-go theorem for the five-dimensional competitor Every real skew 5\times5 source is orthogonally reducible to two rotation blocks and a zero direction. The corresponding irreducible spinor Hamiltonian has eigenvalues \{\alpha+\beta,\alpha-\beta,-\alpha+\beta,-\alpha-\beta\}, up to an overall scalar shift and coupling scale. Order the positive block strengths \alpha\geq\beta\geq0. If its ground state is nondegenerate, the three gaps are \Delta_1=2\beta,\qquad\Delta_2=2\alpha, \qquad\Delta_3=2(\alpha+\beta)=\Delta_1+\Delta_2. Consequently three equal positive gaps are impossible for any source in this operator class, not just for the selected minimum or a sampled parameter range. Equivalently, the ordered eigenvalues always obey \lambda_1+\lambda_4=\lambda_2+\lambda_3. This is robust: a target with eigenvalues (E_0,E_0+\Delta,E_0+\Delta, E_0+\Delta), \Delta>0, has operator-norm distance at least \Delta/4 from every scalar-plus-five-dimensional-bivector Hamiltonian, even allowing arbitrary spinor bases. If the norm error is \epsilon, each ordered eigenvalue differs by at most \epsilon. The two pair sums of the target differ by \Delta, so the competitor's equality forces \Delta\leq4\epsilon. The bound is attained: for target \operatorname{diag}(-3,1,1,1), the aligned canonical bivector spectrum (-2,0,0,2) is at distance one. Conditional exact-six theorem Assume all of the following are independently justified: The relevant polarization is one fundamental complex spatial spin module, or one irreducible half-spin module in even dimensions, of a Euclidean d-dimensional carrier. It has exactly four complex components. This means the module supplied by the spatial Clifford construction, not an arbitrary higher-spin representation, multiplicity space, or four-level internal system. Its source Hamiltonian is linear in spatial bivectors, apart from a scalar shift; no extra vector or higher-degree operator is present. A selected ray has one nondegenerate energy and three exactly equal higher energies separated by a nonzero gap. The spin-representation dimension formula restricts d to five or six. The spectral sum rule excludes five. Within these premises, d=6. Unlike a theorem that assumes chirality from the start, this argument uses the spectrum to discriminate the two four-component irreducible spinors. It does not establish that an actual electron satisfies premises 1–3. In the existing archive the six-dimensional operator produces this spectrum, but deriving a physical requirement for it independently of that operator remains necessary to avoid circular identification. Frozen-source gaps versus reciprocal response frequencies The preceding spectra hold the source fixed during a spinor variation. They are not the normal frequencies of the entire coupled source-spinor system. The flat minimum family supplies six zero modes in that larger system. This distinction can be followed through exactly. For one complex tangent u, choose the corresponding normalized complex source displacement b. If the squared moment-map derivative weight is w, then \Delta=g^2w/(4\mu) and the linearized equations are M\ddot b=-2\mu b+g\sqrt w\,u, \qquad i\hbar\dot u=\Delta u-\frac{g\sqrt w}{2}b. With time dependence e^{-i\omega t} the characteristic polynomial is \omega\left(M\hbar\omega^2-M\Delta\omega-2\mu\hbar\right)=0. Apart from the zero mode, the positive frequency pair is \omega_{\rm high,low} =\frac{\sqrt{\Delta^2+8\mu\hbar^2/M}\ \mathord{\pm}\ \Delta}{2\hbar}. In particular \omega_{\rm high}-\omega_{\rm low}=\frac{\Delta}{\hbar}, \qquad\omega_{\rm high}\omega_{\rm low}=\frac{2\mu}{M}. Thus reciprocal source motion changes the frequencies but preserves the gap as a pair separation in this quadratic, isotropic-inertia model. Five dimensions have two identical pairs and one different pair; six dimensions have three identical pairs. The remaining source-normal modes have frequency \sqrt{2\mu/M}, with multiplicity four and nine respectively. These are additional source degrees of freedom, not spatial dimensions. At \mu=1.3,g=0.7,M=0.4,\hbar=2, the five-dimensional pairs are (2.45701979,2.64548133) twice and (2.36800433,2.74492741) once. Six dimensions give the latter pair three times. Direct full nonlinear projective evolution matches the analytic tangent response: reducing perturbations from 10^{-4} to 10^{-5} reduces the scaled prediction error by a factor of ten in both models. This is a calculable response target, not a demonstrated experimental access route. Other source inertias, extra couplings, damping, nuclear interaction, and detector selection require their own calculation. For the explicitly specified drive “force on the source tangent” and readout “the same source displacement,” the complex-helicity susceptibility is \chi_b(\omega)=\frac{\Delta-\hbar\omega} {\omega(M\hbar\omega^2-M\Delta\omega-2\mu\hbar)}. Its nonzero mode poles have nonvanishing numerators, so they are not dark to this input/output pair. The full linear-system resolvent reproduces this formula at fifteen off-resonant probes in each dimension to below 1.8\times10^{-15}. The frozen-source value \omega=\Delta/\hbar is an antiresonance of this helicity response, not a coupled-system pole. These are ideal model controls and observations; their laboratory access has not been derived. Operator-class escape route: why the hypotheses matter The same five-dimensional matrices obey S(b)+\sum_a n_a\gamma_a=4zz^\dagger-I_4. Allowing an additional vector source therefore reproduces the singlet-triplet operator exactly in five dimensions. The no-go theorem is a theorem about linear bivector coupling, not arbitrary five-dimensional interactions. Scalar nonlinearities in the bivector operator could also alter its spectrum. A microscopic derivation must justify the allowed operator class before this discriminator can decide spatial dimension. None of these source-polarization energy gaps have yet been identified with measured atomic excitation energies. Their multiplicities should not be relabelled p/d/f shell counts. Verification spin5_selection_checks.py checks universal Clifford polynomial identities, moment-map injectivity, the completed-square minimum, all six projective tangent directions, the selected spectrum, normal Hessian, induced metric, Berry curvature, and reciprocal conservation. The first run completed 501 checks. Later spectral-distance and vector-channel checks extend that run; saved reports retain their separate counts. spinor_response_poles_checks.py checks the reciprocal frequency calculation against the full variational matrix and nonlinear evolution. Evidence: extended selection checks and reciprocal response checks. The forced-response extension completes 93 runtime checks, including source-pole observability. Related Dimensional magnetic kernel comparison — applies the same spinors to the existing constrained magnetic kernel and checks the scalar-exchange escape channel. Chiral CP3 selection — six-dimensional construction compared under the same type of source energy. title: Linear Dirac-action variation does not fix the projector sigma-model coefficient
summary: Research record, section 65: Linear Dirac-action variation does not fix the projector sigma-model coefficient.
text: Physical premise (IDWT): There is one infinite-dimensional physical manifold. All sectors form one nested chain of submanifolds within it. This is an exploratory research record, not an independently established V2 result. Read the related later audits before using an intermediate conclusion. 65. Linear Dirac-action variation does not fix the projector sigma-model coefficient Section 64 gave, under its separate-factor Clifford-commutation assumptions, the derivative identity [D,P]=i\gamma^\mu\nabla_\mu P and therefore a canonical positive quadratic norm whose Clifford trace is the Grassmannian sigma-model kinetic density. The next question is whether the already written linear Dirac action automatically supplies that quadratic norm with fixed coefficient. It does not. 65.1 Correct moving-subspace spectral test Let P(t)=R(t)P_0R(t)^T and transport an orthonormal basis of the selected subspace with the same rotation, U(t)=R(t)U_0. The physically relevant compressed operator in the moving frame is H_{\rm eff}(t)=U(t)^TDU(t). For D=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,d_2,d_3,d_4) and simultaneous rotations 1\leftrightarrow3, 2\leftrightarrow4, direct calculation gives H_{\rm eff}''(0) = \operatorname{diag} \left( 2(d_3-d_1), 2(d_4-d_2) \right). Thus the second variation of the linear projected operator is controlled by ambient spectral gaps, not by the universal Grassmannian metric. An earlier fixed-coordinate expectation test produced extra projector-normalization terms; transporting the selected basis removes that artifact and gives the correct gap formula above. 65.2 Scalar orientation-blind limit If D=mI, then H_{\rm eff}(t)=mI for every projector orientation. Hence the linear scalar Dirac term gives exactly zero frame-lock stiffness. This is consistent with the earlier result that the scalar self-contact/rest-frequency operator does not by itself select the 3+3 orientation. 65.3 The positive commutator norm is distinct For the same motion, \operatorname{Tr}([D,\dot P]^\dagger[D,\dot P]) = 2\left[(d_3-d_1)^2+(d_4-d_2)^2\right]. This is a positive quadratic functional of the squared spectral gaps. It is not the same as the second variation of the linear compressed operator, which is linear in the gaps. Therefore \boxed{ \bar\Psi PDP\Psi \not\Rightarrow \operatorname{Tr}([D,P]^\dagger[D,P]) } with a fixed universal coefficient. 65.4 Consequence for projector dynamics The canonical candidate S_P =\frac{\alpha}{2N_s} \operatorname{Tr}([D,P]^\dagger[D,P]) gives the Grassmannian kinetic metric only under the additional assumptions in section 64, but the current V2 action does not force this term merely from the unit coefficient of the linear Dirac kinetic term. The overall coefficient \boxed{\alpha} therefore remains a genuine action-level quantity unless an additional master principle fixes it. 65.5 Status The projector route survives, but one shortcut is ruled out: \boxed{ \text{unit normalization of the linear Dirac action does not fix the projector sigma-model normalization.} } What remains viable is either: a genuine master-field quadratic commutator/projector term; a symmetry or normalization principle fixing its coefficient; or a nonperturbative relation tying the projector-gradient norm to an already derived V2 spectral ratio. Its instantaneous marginal is \int \delta(x-X(t))\delta(y-Y(t))\,d^3y=\delta(x-X(t)). Unobserved-coordinate marginalization does not spread a point. For a normalized extended joint density, its visible marginal can instead be extended. A time-averaged trajectory also gives a different object, \overline\rho(x)=\frac1T\int_0^T\delta(x-X(t))\,dt. Identifying this time measure with detection probabilities requires a sampling and interaction law. title: Frequency-domain review
summary: Corrected frequency-domain conclusions and the remaining hadronic proof target.
text: Physical premise (IDWT): There is one infinite-dimensional physical manifold. All sectors form one nested chain of submanifolds within it. This is a record of calculations, corrections, and unresolved hypotheses. It does not assert a completed hadronic-mass derivation or a validated replacement for the V2 master dynamics. 1. Where the investigation stands The most useful progress was not another numerical factor close to a nucleon residual. Several earlier exclusions depended on confusing a static matrix, an observed projection, or an operator coefficient with a frequency generator. Those exclusions were narrowed or withdrawn after exact checks. Two later results had not yet been recorded in the inspected ledger. First, the point-contact construction and a smooth coherent-density construction have different spectra; the latter does not automatically replace or disprove the graph-supported prescription explicitly chosen in V2. Second, a rank-one source-to-scalar-self-energy response supplies a concrete sufficient mechanism for the common-anchor ratios without measuring or solving for the sources. The unresolved issue is whether that response applies to complete occupied reference frequencies or to coefficients before the simplex multiplier. The companion contact-kernel note and rank-one-response note contain those previously undocumented calculations. They are live possibilities and exact comparison tests, not a numerical baryon prediction. The last inspected hadronic ledger ends at Section 76. Its Sections 67--76 contain the earlier saved corrections. The returned execution report confirmed that write and its verification. Later read-only tests did not, by themselves, save the additional findings. This notes package preserves them separately rather than extending an exploratory ledger as though it were a finished module. 2. Observable and notation discipline The target is a rest-frequency ratio, ultimately z_B=\frac{\omega_B}{\omega_e}, \qquad \omega_e=\frac{m_ec^2}{\hbar}. Use \varpi_d=\mu_d/\hbar when \mu_d denotes the sector energy unit, and distinguish it from an oscillator frequency produced by a constriction model. On the hypothesized ordinary contact branch, \omega_{n,d}=\varpi_d S(n,d), \qquad S(n,d)=\binom{n+d-1}{d}. A specified occupied reference frequency is \omega_d^\star=\varpi_d S(n_d^\star,d), not generally \varpi_d. In particular, the depth-four reference has count 15, while the electron reference has count 18564. The pre-prism source-phase proposal \Omega_{n,d}=S(n,d)-1 is yet another object; its identification with time-dependent physical dynamics remains conditional in the contact-resonance source, Section 3. No independently calibrated field amplitude is an input to these notes. Arbitrary normalization of an eigenvector cannot move the eigenvalues of a fixed linear operator. However, replacing an unknown coefficient by an unknown frequency ratio does not determine it, and a nonlinear background dependence cannot be erased by renaming its variables. Genuine coefficients, projected kernels, kinetic metrics, and boundary conditions still need a derivation or a demonstrated cancellation. 3. Corrected static and spectral matrix results For the adopted test values G=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\b&c\end{pmatrix}, \qquad a=8\sqrt7,\quad b=4\sqrt6,\quad c=12/\sqrt7, one has b^2=ac. The three quantities previously conflated are \underbrace{a-b^2/c}_{\text{actual static Schur complement}}=0, \qquad \underbrace{b^2/c}_{\text{removed relaxation contribution}}=a, \qquad \underbrace{a}_{\text{clamped principal block}}. The frequency-dependent matrix elimination instead uses f(z)=a-z-\frac{b^2}{c-z}, \qquad (c-z)f(z)=\det(G-zI)=z(z-a-c). This is exact away from the excluded complementary denominator. That excluded value must be checked in the original problem. The full matrix eigenvalues are 0 and a+c, not the removed static contribution considered in isolation. The operator square root also does not commute with projection. Here \sqrt G=\frac{G}{\sqrt{a+c}}, \qquad \frac{\langle3|\sqrt G|3\rangle}{\sqrt a}=\sqrt{14/17}, \qquad \frac{\sqrt{\langle3|G|3\rangle}}{\sqrt a}=1. The reference-band law (\omega_d^\star/\omega_e)^2=g_{dd}/g_{66} alone does not identify the full interacting frequency generator with \sqrt{G/g_{66}}. Consequently the earlier universal prohibition on a term linear in a dimensionless coupling was too strong. The particular matrix prescriptions were checked; a different operator map was not disproved. These corrections are already recorded in the hadronic ledger, Section 73. 4. Projection of a signal is not replacement of its generator For a time-independent linear map P and the same clock, P\bigl(u e^{-i\omega t}\bigr)=(Pu)e^{-i\omega t}. A nonzero projected line retains its frequency. A zero projection removes the line. This is different from physically imposing a new closed dynamics generated by PHP on a subspace that does not reduce H. The exact diagnostic used u=\begin{pmatrix}1/\sqrt6\\\sqrt{5/6}\end{pmatrix}, \qquad H=64uu^\dagger, \qquad P=\operatorname{diag}(1,0). The compressed matrix has its observed entry 32/3, but the exact projected resolvent is P(z-H)^{-1}P =\left[\frac{1}{6(z-64)}+\frac{5}{6z}\right]P. The factor 1/6 is the residue at the unchanged frequency 64. The corresponding exact reduced generator is H_{\rm eff}(z)=\frac{32z}{3z-160}. This resolves the earlier color-projection error: the ordered rank-one contact gives 64/6 under compression, but that is not a universal frequency penalty. If color and orbital factors separate as I_{\rm color}\otimes A_{\rm mode}, singlet restriction leaves the allowed orbital eigenfrequencies unchanged. Likewise, annihilation of an identical color-vector product does not exclude a shared orbital mode with a separate antisymmetric color state. These results do not establish that 64 is a physical baryon eigenvalue. See ledger Section 74. 5. A genuine color coefficient, with its sign retained With fundamental generators normalized by \operatorname{tr}(T^aT^b)=\delta^{ab}/2, the directly constructed pair operator is C_{ij}=\sum_aT_i^aT_j^a =\frac12\left(X_{ij}-\frac13I\right). On the normalized determinant singlet \epsilon\in\Lambda^3\mathbb C^3, X_{ij}\epsilon=-\epsilon. Hence C_{ij}\epsilon=-\frac23\epsilon, \qquad \sum_{i<j}C_{ij}\epsilon=-2\epsilon. All eight generators, their trace normalization, and all three pair operators were checked explicitly. For a derived interaction of the form \sum_{i<j}C_{ij}\otimes K_{ij}(z), the singlet restriction is -(2/3)\sum_{i<j}K_{ij}(z). It becomes -2K(z) only when the remaining pair operators actually coincide. This is not a frequency prediction. The radial, spin, and normalization content of K_{ij} is still required. A numerical equality with the 2/3 in 28/9=(2/3)(g_{33}/g_{44}) does not identify the two constructions. The adopted sector couplings must not silently be equated with the coefficient of a gauge-current pair interaction. The source generator convention appears in the contact-resonance module, Section 14; the diagnostic is recorded in ledger Section 76. 6. What the earlier numerical searches actually tested These searches used preselected illustrative prescriptions, not a derived composite generator. Their failures therefore do not falsify all V2 hadronic constructions. For the committed quark contact counts D_u=15, D_d=1, D_s=20, raw constituent products give 225 for uud, 15 for udd, and 300 for uds. This shows why that unqualified product prescription is unsuitable as a common nucleon bulk contribution; it does not establish how physical composite frequencies combine. A separate carrier-size scan gave: Candidate carrier Dimension W^{\otimes3}, \dim W=4 64 \operatorname{Sym}^3W 20 \Lambda^3W 4 U^{\otimes3}, \dim U=3 27 \operatorname{Sym}^3U 10 \Lambda^3U 1 W^{\otimes2} 16 \operatorname{Sym}^2W 10 \Lambda^2W 6 The number 64\varpi_3 lay about 2.77 percent below the chosen approximately 309.5 MeV per-constituent residual when the conditional sector scale was used. That proximity does not choose a baryon carrier. Its previous suppression-based exclusion was withdrawn, not replaced by a derivation. Another scan tried S(n,6)/S(13,6) for 35\le n\le47. The values bracketing the selected residual ratio near 605.676 were approximately 578.408 at n=42 and 661.038 at n=43. No operator identification justified borrowing the electron-sector scale for a composite. Scalar S^5 harmonic degeneracies were also scanned; their initial values are 1,6,20,50,105,196. Degeneracy is not automatically a frequency. These are records of unsuccessful exploratory identifications, not universal spectral exclusions or statistical null tests. The approximately 309--310 MeV quantity itself was a residual allocated per constituent after subtracting chosen quark contributions. It is not, absent an additional decomposition theorem, a separately measured pole that a correct operator must contain. The primary target is the whole baryon rest frequency. 7. The constructive spectral target Three positions in a common observed three-space give six relative Jacobi coordinates after center-of-mass removal. A fixed Euclidean hyperradius has an S^5 angular surface. This is useful effective three-body kinematics, not proof that the baryon is the depth-six electron sector or the depth-five neutrino sector. Native higher-depth coordinates, spinor bundles, and eliminated channels must be accounted for. Ledger Section 75 records the corrected distinction. For a specified stationary generator \mathsf H in electron-frequency units and an orthogonal model-space projector P_B, let Q_B=I-P_B. Exact reduction gives \mathsf H_{\rm eff}(z)=P_B\mathsf HP_B+ P_B\mathsf HQ_B(z-Q_B\mathsf HQ_B)^{-1}Q_B\mathsf HP_B, and seeks \ker\left[z_BI_{P_B}-\mathsf H_{\rm eff}(z_B)\right]\ne\{0\}. The complementary inverse has a specified domain; at its excluded values the original problem is checked. This is an exact block identity for a given generator, not a derivation of the missing blocks. A covariant Dirac operator must first be related to a stationary time generator. An off-diagonal map P_3D_\infty P_4 has no standalone ordinary frequency spectrum without further structure. The common-anchor law remains conditional on deriving the projected reference response from the action. The composite blocks and their induced spectral terms are also unresolved; amplitude fits do not supply those derivations. 8. They are not Monte Carlo significance tests, a full variational derivation, or a proof of empirical agreement. The source audit covers the cited passages and reported bounded searches. An unsuccessful search is not a proof that no suitable formula exists. The packaged checks do not include extensive statistical null tests. 9. title: Sector geometry premise audit
summary: The sphere and projective sector assignments occur in V1 and remain conditional candidates in V2; spatial depth, topology, phase rules, and interaction dynamics require separate justification.
text: Physical premise (IDWT): There is one infinite-dimensional physical manifold. All sectors form one nested chain of submanifolds within it. Particle depth counts ordinary, literal macroscopic spatial dimensions. “Observed” and “unobserved” describe an observer's access to those dimensions, not different kinds of physical dimension. See spatial meaning and mathematical scope. Summary: The sphere and projective sector assignments occur in V1 and remain conditional candidates in V2; spatial depth, topology, phase rules, and interaction dynamics require separate justification. Fixed physical meaning All sectors are nested submanifolds of the one infinite-dimensional physical manifold. This is a fixed IDWT premise. Every sector direction is macroscopic and spatial. In particular, CP3 denotes the electron's six-dimensional physical submanifold, not an internal state space. Three are shared with us, but that makes none of the six different in kind. Similarly, the electron's six dimensions are six of the tau's ten; the electron is lower-dimensional, or “flat,” relative to the tau. Neither comparison gives the containing particle an inherent physical split. The three-dimensional nuclear sector is the proposed basis of ordinary matter's three-dimensional experience. A particular observer-adapted frame calculation does not establish that general claim. The earlier attribution of three-dimensional experience to nuclear 3+3 locking is withdrawn. An incompatible coordinate construction, candidate topology, or effective model must be corrected to respect this premise. It cannot be rescued by reinterpreting a sector as an independent internal space or by abandoning nesting. The audit below distinguishes the intended physical meaning from what the written mathematics actually establishes. Nesting is a geometric requirement The named candidate list in the polarization module does not establish its required smooth inclusions. There is a concrete obstruction in that list. Suppose an embedding of CP2 into S5 existed. Both are oriented, so its real normal line would be trivial. Restricting the sphere tangent bundle would give i^*TS^5=T\mathbb{CP}^2\oplus\mathbf1. The sphere tangent bundle is stably trivial, hence its second Stiefel–Whitney class vanishes. The Whitney sum formula would then require the same for the CP2 tangent bundle. But the projective-space calculation gives w_2(T\mathbb{CP}^2)=c_1(T\mathbb{CP}^2)\bmod2=3H\bmod2\ne0. Here H is the hyperplane class. This contradiction rules out that smooth nesting of the proposed CP2 and S5 assignments. The characteristic-class tools are given in Ralph Cohen, The Topology of Fiber Bundles, chapter 3. The conclusion here is an application of those tools to the candidate list. Therefore that list needs a geometry correction; the requirement that all sectors are nested remains fixed. This audit does not choose a replacement topology or a different electron depth. The Hopf map from S5 onto CP2 is a quotient and does not supply the missing inclusion. The intermediate-depth obstruction strengthens the normal-bundle test. A standard CP1-to-CP2 inclusion admits no intervening smooth three-dimensional spatial submanifold, and a standard CP2-to-CP3 inclusion admits no intervening five-dimensional one, regardless of the proposed odd-dimensional topology. Their nonzero normal Euler class prevents the required splitting. More generally, no smooth CPa-to-CPb embedding with b>a\ge2 can be refined through every intermediate spatial depth, by its normal Pontryagin class. The same note constructs a real normal frame for CP1 inside CP3, showing that alternative partial nestings have different possibilities without selecting a physical replacement. More generally, a nested inclusion does not automatically provide a global product, retraction, or marginalization map. Contact calculations using local tangent–normal coordinates retain that conditional domain until a compatible global construction is supplied. Compact topology also supplies no metric length by itself and gives no reason to call a spatial direction microscopic. Mathematical descriptions must retain their physical meaning Existing construction What it establishes Requirement for the intended spatial theory Tangential compression of the master Dirac operator A d-direction symbol under the stated embedding and Clifford-compatibility assumptions The embedding is of a nested physical submanifold of the same infinite manifold. Homogeneous CP3 coordinate and its four-component lift A representation of points of the proposed six-dimensional spatial submanifold The coordinate lift is not automatically the Dirac field value at that point. Spinor and oscillator-mode bundles Representations of fields and modes on a spatial submanifold Their ranks do not add physical dimensions or independently postulated internal sectors. Chiral or bivector response minimum with CP3 shape A CP3 family in the chosen effective variables A family of field polarizations alone does not derive the physical spatial submanifold; its relation to spatial position and the master field must be supplied. Selected coefficient orbit and displayed petals A trajectory and readout in a chosen reduced model The dynamics must describe actual motion on physical CP3 and the response of nuclear-constrained observers. Observer-adapted 3+3 frame-lock energy A conditional energy and its extrema for a chosen grouping of equivalent spatial directions No inherent electron split follows. Any physical role of the assumed frame constraint needs a derivation; its energy minimum does not derive three-dimensional experience. Product of two particle-position spaces Records two positions on the same physical submanifold Its parameter count is not a new set of physical dimensions. The existing bundle obstructions, conditional response calculations, and stability limitations still apply. The correction is to their interpretation and claim boundaries; adding a spatial label cannot supply missing dynamics. Provenance found, physical derivation not established The listed depth geometries remain conditional candidates. The historical forces document, section 0.8b, already lists CP1, S3, CP2, S5, CP3, and CP5 at depths 2,3,4,5,6,10. This establishes their presence in V1, not a complete edit-by-edit copying history and not the correctness of the accompanying force claims. Section 12 of the V2 polarization module gives an inverse reconstruction conditional on: a smallest complex amplitude carrier; fixed normalization; a chosen physical or redundant status of common phase; transitive unitary action; and an already prescribed real spatial dimension. Within that ansatz, retaining phase gives S(2r−1), and quotienting it gives CP(r−1). The dimension arithmetic is valid. It does not show that a particle's actual configuration is this amplitude space, that its norm is constrained in this way, or that its common phase has the assumed physical status. The written reconstruction does not derive these premises from the master interaction or establish that alternative geometries are impossible. Three questions must remain separate Question What would support it What does not settle it Spatial depth d Independent kinetic derivative directions in a derived sector operator Number of display controls or complex coefficients Geometry of Q_d A derived metric, constraints, identifications, and global structure Real dimension alone or a convenient homogeneous-space construction Interaction and observed orbit Derived source, dynamics, physical projection/current and perturbation response A chosen generator with a trajectory-shaped readout The particle-depth module already identifies depth with the number of local spatial derivative directions. Even if that count were established, it would not select a unique global topology or metric. Its projected-symbol theorem itself requires a sector embedding, projector, and compatibility assumptions; writing a d-direction operator after assuming the sector is not a measurement or a derivation selecting d. The local symmetric-mode count is likewise conditional on independent quadratic directions and the specified mode construction. It is not a unique signature of CP3, S5, or another global manifold. Consequences for the current orbit investigation CP3 precession and the finite response model are valid conditional constructions on a chosen six-real-dimensional geometry. They do not establish that geometry for the electron. The earlier SO(4)/U(2) comparison varied carrier dimension, not V2's proposed particle-base dimension. Its minimum-carrier theorem cannot establish a minimum-six particle depth. The exact three-amplitude restriction on candidate CP2 and S5 reproduces the prepared ideal demo with the restricted original readout. It is a counterexample to uniqueness inside these candidate constructions, not evidence that CP2 or S5 is the correct lower-depth geometry. A response-control rank calculated in the assumed CP3 model is not yet an empirical dimension witness. Source state, readout, phase sensitivity, and memory must be accounted for before interpreting it as spatial rank. The five-depth reminder is therefore not resolved by merely substituting S5 into every calculation. Depth five stays in scope even if the S5 assignment is eventually rejected. The same applies to CP3 at depth six. Scope of the geometric construction The working mass-formula depth assignments are fixed inputs, including an electron at depth six. Its geometry, local kinetic symbol, source coupling and physical readout require derivation from the proposed master equations. Explicit geometric models provide conditional examples; their conclusions remain distinct from statements that depend only on dimension. A first target is an interaction that selects the CP3 complex-structure constraint from unconstrained six-dimensional variables, with controlled fluctuations and a justified kinetic reduction. This concerns the geometry at the assigned depth, not a new test of that depth. No new geometry is selected in this audit itself. title: Cross-sector moment kernel
summary: The unaveraged quadratic kernel retains the tensor data needed to investigate orientation dependence.
text: Physical premise (IDWT): There is one infinite-dimensional physical manifold. All sectors form one nested chain of submanifolds within it. The explicit rectangular identification and tensor generalization below are an adaptation derived during the import review, not a theorem quoted from V1. Retain the second moments Let x in R^d, y in R^e, and let B:R^e -> R^d be a specified identification. For unit-normalized densities define K_B(x,y)=g(x^{\mathsf T}By)^2,\qquad M_x=\int xx^{\mathsf T}\rho_x(x)\,dx,\quad M_y=\int yy^{\mathsf T}\rho_y(y)\,dy. Then, exactly, V_x(x)=g x^{\mathsf T}B M_y B^{\mathsf T}x,\qquad U_{xy}=g\operatorname{tr}(M_x B M_y B^{\mathsf T}). For fixed M_y and B, the coordinate Hessian of V_x is 2g B M_y B^T. This is not automatically the full coupled-field Hessian: the background moments can fluctuate too. For equal dimensions and B=I, write M_x=aI+Q_x and M_y=bI+Q_y, with traceless Q_x,Q_y. Then U_{xy}=g\left[dab+\operatorname{tr}(Q_xQ_y)\right]. The historical isotropic reduction sets both Q tensors to zero. Retaining them gives an explicit orientation-sensitive term. Its sign and eigenvalue structure must determine the preferred orientation; alignment is not automatic. Even a preferred quadrupole-axis alignment need not determine a unique signed frame or the electron's complex-structure polarization. Symmetry and missing inputs Under independent orthogonal frame changes x->R x and y->S y, covariance requires B->R B S^T. Holding B fixed preserves only compatible transformations. An unspecified cross-sector dot product is therefore not invariant under arbitrary independent rotations. For complex coordinates, specify a Hermitian kernel such as |x-dagger B y|^2 and its representation separately. Rank-one sector coefficients g_de=v_d v_e do not force the coordinate kernel or its projected matrix elements to be rank one. Promising next calculation: derive B and background moments from the V2 field, retain their fluctuations, and project onto the actual polarization states. Do not identify this scalar coordinate Hessian with a spin-dependent lock operator without that projection and the corresponding kinetic form. Explicit normalized basis For H=-Delta+lambda r^2, w=sqrt(lambda)>0, and angular harmonics normalized to unit integral on S^(d-1), \chi_{n_r\ell m}(r,\Omega)= N_{n_r\ell}r^\ell L_{n_r}^{(\ell+d/2-1)}(wr^2) e^{-wr^2/2}Y_{\ell m}(\Omega), \qquad N_{n_r\ell}^2=\frac{2w^{\ell+d/2}n_r!}{\Gamma(n_r+\ell+d/2)}. N=2n_r+\ell,\qquad E_N=w(2N+d),\qquad \langle r^2\rangle_N=\frac{2N+d}{2w}. The level degeneracy is binomial(N+d-1,d-1); the cumulative count through N=n-1 is S(n,d)=binomial(n+d-1,d). This count is not E_N. Equality of dimensions with another representation does not establish an operator intertwiner or an equivalence of physical state spaces. Density overlap versus transition matrix element For isotropic normalized densities in the same R^d, O_{ij}=\iint(x\cdot y)^2|\chi_i(x)|^2|\chi_j(y)|^2\,dx\,dy =\frac{\langle r^2\rangle_i\langle r^2\rangle_j}{d}. Isotropy must hold for the actual density, for example an s-wave or a uniform shell mixture; an arbitrary individual oscillator eigenstate need not have it. With one mode fixed, this overlap grows linearly with the other shell index, unlike the degree-d cumulative count. It is a density-density expectation, not a normalized charged-current amplitude. For actual coherent transitions use off-diagonal moments such as integral chi_i^*(x) x_a x_b chi_j(x) dx, retaining phases, angular indices, selection rules, and any spinor vertex. A reusable radial integral For s>0 and integer n_r>=0, \int_0^\infty u^{1/2}e^{-su}L_{n_r}^{(1/2)}(u)\,du =\frac{\Gamma(n_r+3/2)}{n_r!} \frac{(s-1)^{n_r}}{s^{n_r+3/2}}. At s=1 it vanishes for n_r>=1; at s=3/2 no finite radial level is eliminated. The weight must be obtained from the actual vertex before using this as a selection rule. It does not select a particle tower by itself. Product shell counts Shell degeneracies obey a useful convolution. For g_d(N)=\binom{N+d-1}{d-1}, \sum_{k=0}^{N}g_a(k)g_b(N-k)=g_{a+b}(N). The generating functions multiply as (1-z)^{-a}(1-z)^{-b}=(1-z)^{-(a+b)}. This counts product states of the specified separated oscillators with fixed total excitation. Using cumulative counts as though they were shell degeneracies would give a different convolution. The partition into a and b directions is a calculation choice among equivalent ordinary spatial directions. The a=b=3 example does not give the electron an inherent 3+3 split or prove colour neutrality. The simplex band moments instead average shell observables across a whole cumulative band. Constant-background overlaps A uniform continuation and an oscillator ground state have different overlap weights. For the physicists' Hermite polynomials in a dimensionless coordinate, \int_{-\infty}^{\infty}H_{2m}(y)e^{-y^2/2}\,dy =\sqrt{2\pi}\frac{(2m)!}{m!},\qquad \int_{-\infty}^{\infty}H_{2m+1}(y)e^{-y^2/2}\,dy=0. To derive this, integrate the generating function e^{2ty-t^2}=\sum_jH_j(y)t^j/j! against e^{-y^2/2}. The result is \sqrt{2\pi}e^{t^2}. Thus overlap against a constant background removes odd modes by parity, but every even mode has a nonzero overlap. Normalized oscillator modes add nonzero prefactors and do not change these zeros. The constant is a generalized background on the line, not a normalizable oscillator state. A ground-state bra would supply another Gaussian and a different orthogonality relation. This distinction matters for the cylindrical continuation premise: a low-degree insertion and parity alone do not exclude excitation in several added coordinates when the relevant modes are even. The actual vertex and integration weight must be supplied. Finite spatial operators The complete source marginal uses these normalized constant-background integrals in a finite matrix; its singular strengths follow a weighted Hockey-Stick identity. Physical bilinear currents must be formed before that linear map is applied. The spatial evaluation kernel uses the same paired-occupation weights at the oscillator center and fixes the distinction between spatial point contact and projective ray contact. Review checks Independent quadrature in the preceding review checked unit normalization and the radial second moment for (d,n_r,ell,w)=(3,2,0,2.195), (4,1,2,1.314), and (6,6,0,0.5), with errors below 1e-13. This was a representative check, not a rerun of the entire historical script or validation of its conclusions. The mode counting checks verify shell convolutions and independently integrate the Hermite overlaps by Gaussian quadrature. Related Self-consistent functional — supplies the harmonic background under stated assumptions. Import boundaries — prevents reinterpreting density overlaps as CKM probabilities. Counting mode tools — collects the counting and spectral identities.

title: Reference-band normalization
summary: The historical mass-scale prescription uses a fixed occupied reference count whose dynamical origin remains open.
text: Physical premise (IDWT): There is one infinite-dimensional physical manifold. All sectors form one nested chain of submanifolds within it. Particle depth counts ordinary, literal macroscopic spatial dimensions. “Observed” and “unobserved” describe an observer's access to those dimensions, not different kinds of physical dimension. See spatial meaning and mathematical scope. Source Mass §10, beginning near line 633, states that the squared lightest occupied mass scales as g_dd/g_66 relative to the electron. Preserve this as a historical prescription, not an established consequence of varying the displayed action. The useful distinction Write D_d*=S(n_min(d),d) for a fixed occupied reference count and m(n,d)=mu_d S(n,d). The historical reference condition is (\mu_d D_d^*)^2=\frac{g_{dd}}{g_{66}}m_e^2, \qquad \mu_d=\frac{m_e}{D_d^*}\sqrt{\frac{g_{dd}}{g_{66}}}. For the d=3,4,6 comparison the reference counts are 1,15,18564. Once fixed, D_d* is a sector constant, not the variable S(n,d) of whichever excited mode is being evaluated. Consequently mu_d=C v_d/D_d*, with v_d=sqrt(g_dd) and C=m_e/sqrt(g_66), is compatible with band blindness. This supports the corrected common-anchor interpretation in the existing V2 notes: a fixed-reference relation is not ruled out merely because it contains a count. It does not prove the relation or select its reference bands. Remaining derivation Derive the stationary cross-sector equations and kinetic normalization that select the occupied-reference masses rather than the pre-count coefficients. Explain why these particular occupied modes define the reference. Do not extend this prescription indiscriminately: V1 also uses different neutrino, boson, and tau scale constructions despite some universal wording. The scalar oscillator closure lambda proportional to (gQ)^(2/3) is a different equation. Converting it into this mass-reference condition requires an explicit operator and units dictionary, not a relabeling of lambda. Related Self-consistent functional — distinguishes the actual mean-field closure from the reference prescription. Import boundaries — records what normalization arguments do not establish.

title: Self-consistent functional
summary: A reusable harmonic mean-field closure with explicit norm and variation assumptions.
text: Physical premise (IDWT): There is one infinite-dimensional physical manifold. All sectors form one nested chain of submanifolds within it. Particle depth counts ordinary, literal macroscopic spatial dimensions. “Observed” and “unobserved” describe an observer's access to those dimensions, not different kinds of physical dimension. See spatial meaning and mathematical scope. Source and scope Adapted from IDWT_04_Gravity.md, §3.10.2–3.10.5c, especially the explicit functional, near line 315. Status: checked algebra within a flat, scalar, fixed-norm mean-field model; not a derivation of the V2 master dynamics. Functional and stationary equation For real coordinates x,y in R^d, coupling g>0, kinetic coefficient set to one, and Q = integral |Psi|^2 fixed, retain the source functional E[\Psi]=\int |\nabla\Psi(x)|^2\,dx +\frac g2\iint(x\cdot y)^2|\Psi(x)|^2|\Psi(y)|^2\,dx\,dy. Variation of E-mu Q gives \left[-\Delta+g\int(x\cdot y)^2|\Psi(y)|^2\,dy\right]\Psi(x)=\mu\Psi(x). For an isotropic density, its second moment is integral y_i y_j |Psi(y)|^2 dy = Q delta_ij <r^2>/d. Thus V(x)=lambda |x|^2, with lambda=g Q <r^2>/d. The normalized oscillator ground state has <r^2>=d/(2 sqrt(lambda)), so \lambda=(gQ/2)^{2/3},\qquad \Psi(x)=\sqrt Q\,\lambda^{d/8}\pi^{-d/4} \exp(-\sqrt\lambda\,|x|^2/2). The historical formula lambda=(g/2)^(2/3) is the Q=1 specialization. Choosing Q=1 is not a derivation of quantum charge discreteness. Transfer conditions This produces an isotropic stationary solution, not a proof that it is the unique physical background or that its full fluctuation spectrum is stable. The eigenvalue mu includes the full mean-field potential; the interaction appears with one-half its double integral in E. Do not equate mu Q with E. When expanding this functional in oscillator modes, retain the kinetic matrix and quartic term, or explicitly subtract the background potential already included in oscillator eigenvalues. Otherwise it is double-counted. A resonant-only quartic mode sum requires a justified rotating-wave or time-averaging reduction; index-resonance restrictions do not follow merely from expanding the static functional in a basis. The formula as written uses a fixed origin. The centroid-relative completion defines and varies a centred version with translation covariance and zero net self-force. That completion remains a flat scalar auxiliary model. This closure does not identify oscillator eigenvalues with cumulative state counts, select occupied particle indices, or supply a physical lock frequency. Related Cross-sector moment kernel — generalizes the isotropic moment retained here. Normalized oscillator modes — supplies the normalized stationary basis. Centroid-relative self-binding — makes the centre dynamical rather than tying the self-potential to an external origin.

title: Spectral weights in oscillator response
summary: Weighted Hockey-Stick source strengths have a sharp response-stiffness convergence threshold, and a four-normal-direction affine spectrum retains shared-mode-dependent cutoff growth that a common additive constant cannot remove.
text:
Summary: Weighted Hockey-Stick source strengths have a sharp response-stiffness convergence threshold, and a four-normal-direction affine spectrum retains shared-mode-dependent cutoff growth that a common additive constant cannot remove. Keep the source map and the response spectrum together The oscillator source marginal integrates a specified linear scalar source over q ordinary normal spatial directions. At shared oscillator degree k and total cutoff N, its paired normal occupations have weights a= rac q2,\qquad M=\left\lfloor rac{N-k}{2}ightfloor, \qquad w_q(r)= rac{(a)_r}{r!},\qquad \sum_{r=0}^M w_q(r)= inom{M+a}{M}. 	ag{1} Here (a)_r=a(a+1)\cdots(a+r-1) and (a)_0=1. The final equality is the weighted Hockey-Stick identity. It follows by multiplying the shell generating function (1-t)^{-a} by (1-t)^{-1}. All spatial coordinates retain their ordinary physical meaning; this flat oscillator comparison introduces no compactification. Let R be that full complex linear source map and let L be a specified positive response operator on modes of the same field. If its eigenvalue at total degree k+2r is \ell_{k+2r}>0, then G_{N,k}=(RL^{-1}R^\dagger)_k =c_0^{2q}\sum_{r=0}^{M} rac{w_q(r)}{\ell_{k+2r}}, \qquad c_0=\sqrt2\,\pi^{1/4}w^{-1/4}. 	ag{2} The oscillator parameter w uses the convention in the source-marginal note. Dividing by c_0^{2q} expresses the sum in ground-integral units; it does not perform physical kinetic normalization. For example, the real energy E[u,v]=E_0[u]+ rac12\langle v,Lvangle -g\operatorname{Re}\langle u,Rvangle 	ag{3} has stationary response v=gL^{-1}R^\dagger u and correction -g^2\langle u,Guangle/2. Both variations use the same complex map and its adjoint, as in common field response. The positivity assumption belongs to this response example; it is not an assertion that the full signed Dirac Hamiltonian is positive. The exact threshold for removing the mode cutoff Fix k, and suppose at large r \ell_{k+2r}\sim\lambda r^s,\qquad \lambda>0. 	ag{4} The gamma-ratio asymptotic gives w_q(r)=\Gamma(r+a)/(\Gamma(a)\Gamma(r+1)) \sim r^{a-1}/\Gamma(a). Thus the positive summand in (2) is asymptotic to r^{a-s-1}/(\lambda\Gamma(a)). Comparison with a power integral proves  oxed{G_{\infty,k}<\infty\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad s>q/2.} 	ag{5} More precisely, writing \widetilde G=G/c_0^{2q},  egin{aligned} \widetilde G_{N,k}&\sim  rac{M^{a-s}}{\lambda\Gamma(a)(a-s)},&&s<a,\ \widetilde G_{N,k}&\sim rac{\log M}{\lambda\Gamma(a)},&&s=a,\ \widetilde G_{\infty,k}-\widetilde G_{N,k}&\sim  rac{M^{a-s}}{\lambda\Gamma(a)(s-a)},&&s>a. \end{aligned} 	ag{6} Finite lower levels affect finite constants, not this classification. The result concerns a fixed source map and its stated spectrum as a regulator is removed. If N instead labels a physically selected finite branch, the finite sum remains valid without taking this limit. Those distinct uses of a band are also separated in consistent band contacts. An affine spectrum has explicit borderline cases Take the comparison spectrum \ell_{k+2r}=\kappa+
u(k+2r)=2
u(r+b_k), \qquad b_k= rac{\kappa+
u k}{2
u}>0, \qquad \kappa,
u>0. 	ag{7} It has s=1. Define S_M(a,b)=\sum_{r=0}^M(a)_r/[r!(r+b)], so G_{N,k}=c_0^{2q}S_M(a,b_k)/(2
u). For 0<a<1, positivity permits termwise integration:  egin{aligned} S_\infty(a,b) &=\int_0^1 t^{b-1}\sum_{r=0}^\infty rac{(a)_r}{r!}t^r\,dt\ &=\int_0^1t^{b-1}(1-t)^{-a}dt = rac{\Gamma(b)\Gamma(1-a)}{\Gamma(b+1-a)}. \end{aligned} 	ag{8} The last equality is Euler's beta integral. Among positive integer codimensions, this convergent case is q=1. For a\ge1 the endpoint integral and the positive sum both diverge; analytically continuing the gamma expression does not assign their ordinary positive response a finite value. Put H_M(b)=\sum_{r=0}^M(r+b)^{-1} =\psi(M+b+1)-\psi(b), where \psi=\Gamma'/\Gamma is the digamma function. The equality follows by telescoping its recurrence. Then  oxed{S_M(1,b)=H_M(b),\qquad S_M(2,b)=M+1+(1-b)H_M(b).} 	ag{9} The second formula uses (2)_r/r!=r+1 and (r+1)/(r+b)=1+(1-b)/(r+b). Normal directions q Affine-spectrum response S_M 1 Finite limit \mathrm B(b,1/2) 2 \log M+O(1) 3 4\sqrt{M}/\sqrt\pi+O(1) 4 M+(1-b)\log M+O(1) 6 M^2/4+O(M) These are scalar-source response sums in the stated units, not particle charges or experimentally measured coupling factors. Four normal directions retain a shared-mode-dependent divergence Codimension four is relevant to a ten-to-six flat spatial comparison, although the occupied particle modes and their physical kernel have not been identified with this oscillator example. For fixed shared degrees k
e l, use the same total cutoff N in both responses. Their paired cutoffs differ only by a bounded integer. Equation (9) therefore gives  oxed{G_{N,k}-G_{N,l} = rac{c_0^8}{2
u}(b_l-b_k)\log(N/2)+O(1) = rac{c_0^8(l-k)}{4
u}\log(N/2)+O(1).} 	ag{10} The common linear growth cancels, but the displayed logarithm does not. Subtracting one cutoff-dependent constant times the identity changes neither side's difference, so it cannot make every shared-mode response finite. This is an additive-subtraction statement, not a prohibition of all effective theories. Further direct terms or a different source and spectrum would need to follow from the same action and normalization. The divergence is not automatically a short-distance singularity. Here the cylindrical source dual is constant in the normal coordinates and is not in their untruncated L^2 space. High oscillator levels also explore increasing spatial extent. The mode cutoff does not by itself separate large-distance and short-distance contributions. Field norm and effective response have different thresholds For one retained source coefficient u_k, the stationary field in (3) has canonical squared norm \|v\|^2=g^2|u_k|^2c_0^{2q} \sum_{r=0}^M rac{w_q(r)}{\ell_{k+2r}^2}. 	ag{11} Under (4), this positive sum converges precisely when 2s>q/2, or s>q/4. Its energy norm instead obeys \langle v,Lvangle=g^2|u_k|^2G_{N,k} and needs the stronger condition (5). For an affine spectrum, two or three normal directions therefore permit a finite canonical field norm while the effective response still diverges. At four normal directions even the canonical norm has logarithmic growth. A finite norm alone does not establish a finite source energy or a finite induced coupling. What additional source structure would have to do Suppose an actual projection supplies a shell amplitude f_r as well as the marginal. The positive response then contains w_q(r)|f_r|^2/\ell_{k+2r}. If |f_r|^2\sim C r^{-t} with C>0, the same proof gives the convergence threshold s+t>q/2; an upper bound of that order gives sufficiency. This specifies a requirement on a derived source profile, not a new adjustable suppression assigned to a chosen particle depth. Finally, the linear scalar-source map must not be applied to a wave and then squared in place of its physical current. A bilinear current \Psi^\dagger\Gamma\Psi has its own coherent coefficient contractions before projection. Its normal density marginal can be finite even when the unrestricted linear-source response in (2) diverges. The source-marginal derivation gives that distinction explicitly. Verification oscillator_response_tails.py evaluates the finite weighted response and its closed borderline forms. oscillator_response_tail_checks.py runs 105 checks. It independently enumerates normal occupations using exact central-binomial weights, integrates the convergent beta case, checks growing and decaying tail blocks, and compares shared degrees at a common total cutoff. Full complex source matrices also reproduce the reciprocal stationary response, its canonical norm and its Schur energy correction. The all-cutoff conclusions follow from (4)–(10), rather than from a finite numerical scan.

title: Complete radial polarization fields
summary: A spherical scalar Dirac family retains independent complex radial polarization vectors, tangential spatial currents and reciprocal source variations in both odd and even dimensions, including six and ten.
text:
Summary: A spherical scalar Dirac family retains independent complex radial polarization vectors, tangential spatial currents and reciprocal source variations in both odd and even dimensions, including six and ten. A spatial family available in even dimensions The localized axial family uses odd-dimensional kinetic chiral blocks. A separate spherical family works for every D\ge2, including the proposed depths six and ten. It extends the fixed-polarization radial construction by allowing every radial polarization component to have its own complex profile. The spatial domain here is a specified flat chart, not a selected global particle geometry. Let the Hermitian matrices \alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_D, eta obey the complete Dirac Clifford relations. Their minimal complex size is n=2^{\lfloor(D+1)/2floor}. Choose an orthonormal matrix W whose P=n/2 columns span the entire  eta=+1 eigenspace. For r=|x|>0, put \alpha_r=\alpha\cdot\widehat x and set  oxed{\Psi(x,t)=W F(r,t)+\alpha_r W G(r,t), \qquad F,G\in\mathbb C^P.} 	ag{1} The vectors F and G are independent functions of radius and time. They need not be scalar functions multiplying one fixed polarization. Their components describe a field on D ordinary spatial coordinates; they introduce no additional physical dimensions. At the origin, sufficient smoothness conditions are that F is a smooth function of r^2 and G=r\widetilde G(r^2) with smooth \widetilde G. Then \alpha_rG=\alpha\cdot x\,\widetilde G is regular in the original Cartesian coordinates. Decay or appropriate boundary conditions must also support the stated integrations by parts. Spatial dimension D Complete Dirac size n Components of each radial vector P 3 4 2 5 8 4 6 8 4 10 32 16 These counts belong to (1); they are not extra interaction multipliers. The scalar and positive density are radial Because  eta\alpha_r=-\alpha_r eta, the columns of \alpha_rW span the opposite  eta eigenspace. Thus W^\dagger\alpha_rW=0 and \alpha_r^2=I give pointwise  oxed{ho=\Psi^\dagger\Psi=F^\dagger F+G^\dagger G, \qquad \sigma=\Psi^\dagger eta\Psi=F^\dagger F-G^\dagger G.} 	ag{2} No angular averaging is used to obtain either identity. If two radial patterns are superposed, their complete vector sums enter (2). In particular their scalar includes 2\operatorname{Re}(F_1^\dagger F_2-G_1^\dagger G_2). Their phases and polarization contractions remain present. Exact closure under the local scalar equation Consider the same specified local interaction, i\partial_t\Psi=-i\alpha\cdot
abla\Psi +[m+g\sigma] eta\Psi,\qquad m\ge0, 	ag{3} and define M(r,t)=m+g\sigma(r,t). The two Cartesian identities \alpha\cdot
abla(WF)=\alpha_rWF',\qquad \alpha\cdot
abla(\alpha_rWG) =W\left(G'+ rac{D-1}{r}Gight) 	ag{4} follow from \partial_i\widehat x_j=(\delta_{ij}-\widehat x_i\widehat x_j)/r and the Clifford anticommutators. Substitution gives the exact vector equations  egin{aligned} i\partial_tF&=-i\left(\partial_r+ rac{D-1}{r}ight)G+MF,\ i\partial_tG&=-i\partial_rF-MG. \end{aligned} 	ag{5} Every regular solution of (5) reconstructs a solution of the full D-dimensional equation through (1). The nonlinearity preserves this angular family because its scalar (2) is radial. It still couples all occupied vector components through the common M. This is an invariant spatial family, not a claim that arbitrary angular patterns solve (5). The full scalar-source variation is also retained. For independent variations \delta F,\delta G, \delta\sigma=2\operatorname{Re} (F^\dagger\delta F-G^\dagger\delta G),\quad \delta inom{\sigma F}{-\sigma G} = inom{\delta\sigma F+\sigma\delta F} {-\delta\sigma G-\sigma\delta G}. 	ag{6} Both ordinary and conjugate-dependent responses remain in this real-linear derivative. No fixed partner or additional pair coefficient is inserted. A radial density can carry a tangential current The full spatial number current is not determined by ho alone. For a unit direction \widehat x, define K_i(\widehat x)=W^\dagger\alpha_i\alpha_rW-\widehat x_iI_P. 	ag{7} These matrices are anti-Hermitian and obey \sum_i\widehat x_iK_i=0. Direct reconstruction of j_i=\Psi^\dagger\alpha_i\Psi yields  oxed{j_i=2\widehat x_i\operatorname{Re}(F^\dagger G) +2\operatorname{Re}(F^\dagger K_iG).} 	ag{8} The second term is tangential. Its coefficients retain the complete spatial rotation matrices and complex polarization texture. For fixed radius it is a linear combination of tangential rotation fields on the sphere; its divergence is zero. The radial component j_r=2\operatorname{Re}(F^\dagger G) therefore gives \partial_tho+ rac1{r^{D-1}}\partial_r(r^{D-1}j_r)=0. 	ag{9} Thus a radial scalar and density do not imply absence of angular current. Nor is this number current already an identified electromagnetic current. Canonical norm and the full polarization matrix Let \Omega_{D-1}=2\pi^{D/2}/\Gamma(D/2). The physical norm and its matrix refinement are \mathcal Q=\Omega_{D-1}\int_0^\infty (FF^\dagger+GG^\dagger)r^{D-1}dr, \qquad Q=\operatorname{tr}\mathcal Q. 	ag{10} The convention in (1) includes no factor 1/\sqrt{\Omega_{D-1}}; that physical area consequently remains in (10). Using (5), the matrix integrand obeys \partial_t(FF^\dagger+GG^\dagger) =-\left(\partial_r+ rac{D-1}{r}ight) (GF^\dagger+FG^\dagger). 	ag{11} The real scalar terms cancel, including the nonlinear part of M. Vanishing endpoint flux proves conservation of every entry of \mathcal Q, not just its trace. This is a property of the stated radial family; it does not assert a new unrestricted internal symmetry of every spatial Dirac field. Local polarization profiles and tangential currents can still change while their integrated matrix is conserved. For a common physical rotation O with spin lift S, S commutes with  eta and induces the unitary matrix U=W^\dagger SW. Transforming F,G to UF,UG reconstructs S\Psi(O^{-1}x), so (2)–(11) are covariant under rotation of all physical data. The checks also reconstruct every current component, rotate the full field, retain the complete scalar Hessian and integrate the derivative of the full conserved matrix (10). This supplies a controlled spatial family at the even particle depths as well as at odd depths. Its patterns share one radial center. General separated-center encounters, arbitrary angular textures, stable occupied particle states and physically normalized cross-depth coupling require additional calculations. The family does not select the global geometry of our three-dimensional space or of a higher sector.

The fixed-point equation is therefore: \bigl(m_{\rm scale,d}\times S(n_{\min}(d),d)\bigr)^2 = \frac{g_{dd}}{g_{66}}\times m_e^2 \;\Longrightarrow\; m_{\rm scale,d} = m_e\times\frac{\sqrt{g_{dd}/g_{66}}}{S(n_{\min}(d),d)} This is one formula for all sectors. So g_{22} is a state-count (IDOS), on the same footing as the CKM formula: combinatorial, empirically exact, mechanism = counting. The 1/2 and the leg-counting are kernel-motivated; the magnitude is a count of eigenstates, not a dynamical overlap. A count is not a foreign mechanism here — counting is the framework's native currency: the mass law itself is the integrated density of states (Part 8 §5, Theorem S1), and the CKM formula is a relative state count of the Born-ratio form (Part 3 §0.9, Part 1 §2.3). What remains open (🔶) is the operator-level counting theorem — a dynamical selection operator whose spectral-projector trace makes the eigenspace dimensions an output rather than an input. The d=2 sector has no self-confinement — the W is massive but not confined in the quark sense. Its self-coupling g_{22} is instead fixed by the cross-sector back-reaction: the requirement that the d=2 vacuum amplitude is consistent with the d=3 and d=4 quark sector structures at the level n_s=4. The derivation: Step 1. The positive Dirac eigenvalue \lambda_{l=3} = 7/2 on S^3 has multiplicity M_3 = (3+1)(3+2) = 20 = S(n_s,3) (Theorem S1, Part 8 §5). The remaining p = M_3^{S^3} - n_u = S(n_s,3) - n_u = 20 - 3 = 17 [Notation: p is used here rather than \alpha to avoid collision with the fine structure constant \alpha = e^2/4\pi \approx 1/137, which is a separately derived quantity in Part 3 §8.] eigenstates are available to couple to the d=2 sector through G_{23}. The kernel is two-body — (\xi\cdot\xi')^2 couples two copies of J^{d=3} — so both legs contribute, giving p^2. Step 2. Consequences: m_{\rm scale,2} = m_e\times\sqrt{g_{22}/g_{66}} = m_e\times\sqrt{722.5/0.25} = 27.471\ \text{MeV} Quantity From seeds + m_e PDG Error m_W m_{\rm scale,2} \times S(76,2) = 80{,}379 MeV 80,369 MeV +0.012% m_Z m_{\rm scale,2} \times S(81,2) = 91{,}230 MeV 91,188.0 MeV +0.046% m_H m_{\rm scale,2} \times S(95,2) = 125{,}266 MeV 125,200 MeV +0.053% IDWT has a sole unit reference m_e = 0.511 MeV.
